articles.title: A. Gori Greataxe
articles.content:
A small be-spectacled dwarf who runs a small print shop in @[The Dwarrow](settlement:fa91fd8a-f74e-409d-a703-26a9b8e09954), and publishes a weekly newsletter featuring local news and gossip called The TeaSeR. Most of the TeaSeR's readers buy it for the well-drawn cartoons contributed by various local artists; nonetheless, Gori uses the newsletter as a vehicle to pontificate about his pet peeve, the absence of bearded dwarven women in Haven. Gori swears that there is a dwarven city near the borders of the Namori Empire where such bearded beauties dwell, and has actively been trying to organize an expedition to bring back some as wives. 

Most of the older dwarves view these claims with skepticism, but Gori has developed quite a following among the younger males of @[The Dwarrow](settlement:fa91fd8a-f74e-409d-a703-26a9b8e09954). 

 It is also rumored that @[Browin Treebeard](person:4c0d4fe9-907c-45f9-8239-087a69b08d0a), the proprietor of @[Martin Metals](landmark:61b488f5-84e7-48be-af8a-3bb6b4297d45) and a regular advertiser on the back page of the TeaSeR, has donated a substantial sum of capital to finance the expedition.

articles.title: Abel Hofstra
articles.content: The spitting image of his father, except for the graying temples. He does not have the uncanny business sense his sire shows, but is a capable businessman who seldom makes bad investments. He has a wife of whom he is reasonably fond, and three young daughters he positively adores. When not at the banking house, he is at home with his family. [br][br] [familytree:12a241b5-fcfe-4712-817f-0a12106d70e0] [br]

articles.title: Adrielle Ilorim
articles.content:
Daughter of @[Firlirrel Ilorim](person:b6f4ea90-5699-457a-bbd3-4c56917306cf) and @[Lachoriel Ilorim](person:dad2aa8f-106f-4c05-aab6-0c9b7f40b572), Adrielle is a lovely young elven woman of middle height, with long black hair. She appears frequently to be totally absorbed in her own thoughts, even when dealing with customers. 

 Adrielle disappeared for a number of years when still a very young girl of 30, but eventually returned, and now runs a shop (Fine Silks and Fabrics, Erinhir) on Lorien Street specializing in silks and other fine fabrics. 

 She somewhat secretly funds the informal watch group calling themselves @[Adrielle's Watch](organization:81808025-b365-4b84-9f1f-9a7025b37278). How she comes by the money is a mystery.

[spoiler]Adrielle's shop has been under the scrutiny of the @[Thieves' Guild](organization:08dce3b2-80f7-468b-be7b-dd5fdbfac799) (as the object of a probable robbery) for some time. As a result of this, the guild has noticed that Adrielle has a second "business" - trade in human flesh.  Refer to scenario @[Silks and Slavery](plot:cc3bdf6f-e133-4777-8c05-ee2f93753738).[/spoiler] [br][br] [familytree:5d239bee-e2a5-4952-b7ad-412596ca7c50]

articles.title: Adrienne Geronde
articles.content:
A tall, full-bodied girl of sixteen with shoulder-length, curly auburn hair, green eyes, and a thin aquiline nose. Her grandmother, @[Rowena Geronde](person:c44f3336-7f83-4e89-a5c8-78896cc3f650), sees much of herself in Adrienne, and has pushed very hard to interest her daughter in the study of magic. Unfortunately, the Baroness is also a perfectionist, and soon cooled any ardor for the arcane arts that Adrienne possessed. Adrienne is very intellectually oriented, however, and seems likely to become either a scholar, or a cleric of some sort. 

Adrienne finds most social events around @[The Heights](settlement:1f0571c0-b8de-4b50-b010-5529cab6603b) to be dreadfully boring, for she is expected to mingle with the other noble daughters of her age group, almost all of whom are preoccupied with men, marriage, and clothing (and not necessarily in that order). Although she has blossomed in the last two years and become very physically attractive she has a negative self-image of herself in this regard, and considers flattery of this type to be vaguely insulting. 

 She wears a @[Pendant of the Sisters of the Unicorn](item:dd32fe8d-e097-4c49-9857-99d9048cfbc3), which glows red whenever it is held or worn by one who is not sexually chaste. (@[Marita Maggia](person:7c9dab1a-8221-41ca-83f6-0d3b49331e37) has one also). [br][br] [familytree:fe12391b-39d9-4a0d-901e-dfbb25ccb9ef] [br]

articles.title: Aintree
articles.content: Aintree is a muscular, black-haired man of middle-age; he enjoys working behind the bar, drawing drinks for the customers, and has an appreciative sense of humor - his booming, jocular laugh is heard frequently, resounding through the main room of the tavern.

articles.title: Alain Tainley
articles.content:
Alain, @[Tenley Tainley's](person:abedfa62-b993-4d72-acdf-a10e5c2fc4f7) younger brother is an enigmatic religious scholar and devoted priest at the @[Temple of Vairë](landmark:937c3787-8711-4dc8-92e8-b251c978c751). Like the god he worships, Alain is a creature of the night, seldom seen in public by the light of day. He has dark eyes, close-cropped brown hair, and a mottled complexion; he projects a very foreboding presence that normally discourages others from speaking with him. He occupies the tower room of the temple of Kar, and spends his nights in detailed study of the movements of the moon and stars. 

At present, Alain is abroad in the city far more often than usual as he seeks to learn the whereabouts of a meteor which recently fell to earth. He will show an interest in any traveler in Haven who has recently come from the far north (the Khuz mountains area). 

Alain will not communicate with the rest of his family, unless they are in dire need. Indeed, his brothers in the sect know nothing of his noble background, or his true identity, for he has kept these things secret. [br][br] [familytree:eaa390bb-f783-46fb-88ff-5d451e049112] [br]

articles.title: Albert
articles.content: Runs a water driven mill as his public job but is also a torturer in the employ of @[The Black Hand](organization:d1a96263-4191-482e-ace6-360d25106f60)

articles.title: Aldegott Sprig
articles.content: A fletcher who specializes in the shaft and point of arrows and bolts.

articles.title: Alekhine
articles.content: The landlord of a boarding house, Alekhine is a shriveled, bald-headed old codger who attributes his longevity to his lack of curiosity about his boarders. As long as the rents are paid (in advance, please), he cares nothing for the doings of the residents.

articles.title: Alfio Credenza
articles.content:
Owner of a shop selling musical instruments, Alfio has had a running feud with @[Luciano Clarino](person:2110a45a-d4b1-47c4-be2d-e35a52471a31) for 30 years, and will not abide even the mention of his name. 

 He is planing to marry his beautiful daughter Zofia to one of his journeymen, Nikklas in a few months. He is however blissfully unaware that Zofia loves Derek Clarino, the son of his enemy, and Nikklas loves a different female every week. 

 The source of his feud with @[Luciano Clarino](person:2110a45a-d4b1-47c4-be2d-e35a52471a31) lies back 30 years ago when they both loved the same woman, Elissa, who married Alfio, and died giving birth to Zofia. Both men blame the other for causing her death.

articles.title: Alfonso Caradallo
articles.content:
Alfonso is one of @[Angelina](person:b297fe62-c085-4612-a439-fc80b5da899d)'s lieutenants in @[The Black Hand](organization:d1a96263-4191-482e-ace6-360d25106f60). Along with three other subordinates of slightly greater brawn but vastly inferior wit, directs a small longshoreman's firm and storage warehouse, known respectively as Longshoremen Inc. and @[Caradello's Storage](landmark:061fa499-04c8-404a-a4a2-dd450f701b04). 

 He also supervises the activities of Constantine Maylino, owner of a dockside warehouse, Maylino's night watchman @[Rufus](person:16e2a95b-ef60-477f-99ef-237cef2eef14), and @[Lazar Symbocca](person:2c51d376-29e2-4868-ac54-050e58f8c59c), owner of @[Sym's Storage Company](landmark:950bc2b9-c121-4be6-a597-f3373ed455b0). Under the direction of Caradello, Maylino oversees the buying and storage of illicit cargos for the small fleet of Black Hand smugglers that operates along the river. Unknown to Maylino, cargos smuggled into Haven are stored in Caradello's warehouse, or at Sym's Storage. 

 A large and burly man whose bull neck and sloping forehead belie his fierce and arrogant intelligence. He is not a man given to sparkling wit and prolonged conversation, but rather to violent repartee and organizational insight; this latter capability, and his mastery of codes and ciphers, has made him invaluable to @[Angelina](person:b297fe62-c085-4612-a439-fc80b5da899d). 

 Ostensibly he is the owner and chief foreman for the small longshoreman's firm called Longshoremen Inc., and part owner of @[Caradello's Storage](landmark:061fa499-04c8-404a-a4a2-dd450f701b04); however, he also directs Black Hand smuggling operations on @[The South Docks](settlement:e2e38a16-2c10-443d-b40a-6789aa7c041a). He is not a thief, and his promotion within the Hand has been the result of his managerial capabilities. 

 He is a well-liked local figure who uses his influence to look after or protect the neighborhood populace; as a consequence, he has many favors to collect from the common folk of his area. 

 Although he is well past thirty, he is not too old to hold his own in dockside brawls, and his great strength and fast reflexes make him a dangerous opponent.

articles.title: Algipon
articles.content:
Known as Gip, for short - the name's the only thing about him that is short) stands 6'9“, and weighs 150 pounds; in overall appearance he resembles Boris Karloff. He runs an off-the-rack ready-to wear clothing store.  
 [imgblock]https://i1.wp.com/universalmonstersuniverse.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/02/Annex-Karloff-Boris_NRFPT_27.jpg[/img]

articles.title: Ali Zander
articles.content: There is a passenger aboard Atlantia, a handsome young man, dark-haired and bearded, dressed as a merchant. He is actually a mage entrusted with the delivery of certain letters and documents from the @[Circle Chamber](organization:61e67a7d-70ca-4b03-818c-e3f7beb47566) to various high- ranking mages in Belakor.

articles.content: The cook at TheSilver Penny, she is a stocky woman with a sharp tongue and quick knife. She is also mistress to @[Varkin Jelas](person:7a7cdc39-e8ed-4807-b4b7-907a54be3146), the owner.

articles.title: Alonzo Boarstuffer
articles.content: A large, jovial man, with little hair on his head and much on his chin (his beard is waist length). He enjoys the study of the law in his spare time, and has always dreamed of sitting as judge for a trial. He got his name from his habit of procuring a large boar from one of the farms outside the city, stuffing it and roasting it whole whenever there is a spectacular trial in the @[Courts](landmark:5fe07c2b-bce5-4c96-880d-d72a70bb1352).

articles.title: Alvona de Kammeron
articles.content: Wife of @[Boccaccio de Kammeron](person:7987c903-5d74-4fd2-ba5a-b45ef9d76f18). Bedridden for months with pleurisy. [br][br] [familytree:6995aa4c-ba18-4141-9108-a2903a6dfd93] [br]

articles.title: Amelia d'Larette
articles.content:
Bartholomew's wife is a plump and matronly woman, is a lover of music and theater, having grown up on @[The Street of Harps](settlement:6053011d-37a6-4d6b-8e0b-41925f3bbd77). She is the daughter of @[Artemis Guisto](person:804ce8e0-190f-4321-982f-5c304ed4b844), the Drum maker and has five children - Branden, Ophelia, Andrio, Carmen, and Petrio. 

 She is involved more in running the inn than in direct contact with the guests. She spends a good deal of her time in the kitchen gossiping with @[Brisla Stoneaxe](person:fec6ca9c-c9e2-4773-906a-f3d24116222a) the cook and knows everyone on @[The Street of Harps](settlement:6053011d-37a6-4d6b-8e0b-41925f3bbd77).

articles.title: Americus
articles.content: Tall, thin, bespectacled "healer" riding high on high doctrine of health through special herbs only he sells.

articles.title: Amsterdam Craddock
articles.content: Runs a shop selling house an garden tools as well as small pieces of agricultural equipment. They will also do simply repairs and small services such as blade sharpening.

articles.title: Anathea
articles.content: Anathea is an older woman, with greying hair and many wrinkles on her face. She will tell a client's fortune using any method that pleases them: the bones, a crystal ball, phrenology (head bump reading), palmistry, reading tea leaves, the Tarot, etc. - she is expert with all these.

articles.title: Andros Petropopolous
articles.content: A slight and slender man with coal-black hair (in pomaded ringlets), two or three rings on each finger (and thumb), and a tendency to behave like a worried mother hen at the least provocation. He is quite effeminate in movements and attitudes, but is one of the deadliest knife fighters in the city of Haven - and has no compunctions about slitting an opponent’s throat (whether the opponent is up or down).

articles.title: Angelina
articles.content:
A tall, stunning black woman who talks with a lilting accent, called "Angel" by those who know her well (few though they be). Her eyes are jet black, and piercing, and her skin is the rich color of light brown coffee. Clearly no native of Haven, she does not look at all dangerous; behind her appealing exterior, however, lurks one of Haven's finest criminal minds. 

Angelina is one of @[The Black Hand](organization:d1a96263-4191-482e-ace6-360d25106f60)'s masters and controls their interests in smuggling, both by sea and by caravan, and the supply of drugs to many of Haven's noxious opium dens. Auxiliary concerns include the brothel, @[The Black Whip](landmark:6f66e600-9089-49a6-b9dc-7e4dd9febe5c) (DU), on @[The Street of Silk Veils](settlement:587a7a3a-ba45-4bfd-94bc-fe6e17ae023c), and the small but lucrative underground slave trade, a highly illegal business centered around the shop of @[Adrielle Ilorim](person:5d239bee-e2a5-4952-b7ad-412596ca7c50) (JB). Its headquarters are a posh and seemingly respectable dining establishment in @[The North Corridor](settlement:4554e4a9-db69-47da-9921-6c5850001ce8) known as @[Silvante's](landmark:5799fe2e-05a4-44fa-91b3-d10868b94923) (SW) owned and operated by the guild. 

 Angelina's exceptional degree of emotional control has aided her well in her rise to her present position as head of the Hand's largest guild. Her face seldom reflects her true thoughts, and she expects her subordinates to exhibit the same control; as a consequence, her organization is remarkably well regimented, and well led. 

 Angelina was not one of the original Hand leaders; her rise through the ranks has been as steady as it has been rapid. She began her career as a street thief, but was soon promoted to second story operations, and showed some promise as an assassin (a skill which doubtless facilitated her quick promotion). Now, though her skills are somewhat rusty, she carries a pair of small throwing daggers, coated with deadly venom, in sheaths at her neck and forearm, and will not hesitate to use them. As the most ambitious of Father @[Marco](person:92490b02-65df-4f78-9e42-accf38ae00d1)'s guild masters, Angelina is hopeful of engineering his eventual downfall. She has not moved against him yet because her foe is so elusive and unknown, and because she does not know the extent of his support among the other masters. She is currently seeking to find out who @[Marco](person:92490b02-65df-4f78-9e42-accf38ae00d1) is, and to pinpoint his movements. So far, however, she has been markedly unsuccessful, and several of her operatives put on that job have turned up face down in the Dorian, or hanging in the deep freeze unit at @[Silvante's](landmark:5799fe2e-05a4-44fa-91b3-d10868b94923).

articles.title: Angus MacFarland
articles.content: A small, energetic man who runs this booth in the @[Thieves' Market](settlement:8b3bf96f-ea9a-4e39-8c3f-bda804df5cdb) selling assorted powdered spices and minerals (sort of an early version of a natural health store), and assorted drugs (particularly hashish) under the counter.

articles.title: Anise Thyme
articles.content: Sells exotic spices, rare food delicacies, and other unusual items. Anise will be fascinated by any new knick-knacks that characters show him, and will attempt to buy or barter for them if possible.

articles.title: Anson Blackbourne
articles.content:
The oldest son, Anson is a slender man with prematurely thinning golden hair, a pale complexion, and he is not physically strong. He has not only demonstrated an ability to manage the Blackbourne business effectively, but has proven much more adroit than his father at making use of the family's considerable political clout. 

Anson, regardless of the time of day, is always willing to widen his circle of influential acquaintances. He is very friendly to strangers if they are well-dressed and mannered, and polite to almost everyone and generally conveys an image of amiability that people respond to warmly. Anson usually sits in for his father at the meetings of the Council of Boroughs, and it is he who keeps the officials of the Ministries of Trade and Ports (and the clandestine powers of the Thieves Guild) content through payoffs and gifts. 

 Anson is always dressed in the latest Blackbourne fashion styles, and has a frame that shows these garments to good advantage; he always carries an elegant walking stick studded with diamonds. 

 Anson has one severe weakness: despite being married (Talia Blackbourne), he has a fondness for cheap trollops and frequently spends his afternoons or early evenings at one of the many houses of prostitution that line @[The Street of Silk Veils](settlement:587a7a3a-ba45-4bfd-94bc-fe6e17ae023c). He recently was nearly caught in a disastrous scandal, when a blackmailer obtained information that linked Anson to a young prostitute who had been strangled in the South End.  He [b]believes[/b] he has eliminated that threat by having the blackmailer assassinated. [br][br] [familytree:681f57c3-a3f7-4a8d-a44a-34b06fbbf06d] [br]

articles.title: Anton Valvidi
articles.content: An elderly gentleman, with thinning white hair, a prominent nose, and spectacles. He doesn't move as well as he used to, but he still has plenty of spirit left, and is just as demanding as a conductor and teacher as ever.

articles.title: Antonio Berensten
articles.content:
A muscularly built young man with long, shaggy blond hair and a bushy moustache, Antonio is one of @[Tenley Tainley](person:abedfa62-b993-4d72-acdf-a10e5c2fc4f7)'s wards. He has been here in Haven for almost three years, and has become a major figure in the @[Young Stallions](organization:7340b23d-2c0c-45fd-8222-13b00aa2760c) movement. He possesses immense personal charisma, and fervently believes in the righteousness of their cause. 

 Antonio’s heart is beset with great inner turmoil, however, for he has fallen madly in love with @[Marita Maggia](person:7c9dab1a-8221-41ca-83f6-0d3b49331e37), the daughter of one of his staunchest Guild opponents. The two have sworn their love to each other, and are trying to find a cleric willing to marry them secretly (see @[Scenarios](article:088e33cf-5a28-4c3f-bbe5-a243e610d2ff): The Secret Ceremony). 

In the meantime, Antonio lives a double life, and has begun to show external signs of strain - a haggard look to the eyes, a growing habit of nervously drumming his fingers on his sword belt, impatience with some of his colleagues. @[Paul de la Riis](person:61db5c85-e436-459e-926e-17ad7e116b03), his closest friend, suspects that something is seriously wrong with Antonio, and has begun to keep a closer eye on the latter's activities - this of course makes it even harder for Antonio and Marita to see another, even for a few moments. 

 Antonio is oblivious to the fact that @[Taramilla](person:d02504da-377c-43d6-a256-70d7be64077c) of Seki, also a Tainley ward, has become hopelessly infatuated with him. 

 Antonio wears @[The Green](landmark:58c2143a-18ef-4281-89c4-96547a184d4a) cloak and brooch of the Stallions, but does not go in for the elaborate accessories favored by some of the others (walking sticks, plumed hats, etc.) In the past, Antonio always wore a pendant in the shape of a small golden claw (his family's insignia) on formal occasions; he has given this pendant to Marita as a troth of his love. There are some (close friend @[Paul de la Riis](person:61db5c85-e436-459e-926e-17ad7e116b03) or Margery Savonna) who may take note of its absence, and ask Antonio discomforting questions about its whereabouts; of course, if other Maggia were to come upon it in Marita's possession . . . (50% chance he is with other Stallions when encountered) [br][br] [familytree:ec8f50d3-84f6-48a6-95d0-d7d6b5b65cb8] [br]

articles.title: Arada Thornkin
articles.excerpt: Arada is a sunny redheaded SHORT halfling. She's a Lightfoot and it shows. Bright blue eyes and red hair, freckles over her face and a loud and ready laugh with her own odd sense of humour.

articles.title: Arbutus Kystem
articles.content: See Street Encounter: Trailing Arbutus

articles.title: Argli arn Skibur
articles.content: Of the Iron tribe of dwarves, and it shows in his courtroom procedure; he is steely hard. Of average height for a dwarf (but built like an arena wrestler, and exceptionally strong for his size), he has bright red hair and beard (not uncommon among the Iron tribe) and bright blue eyes; his beard is always curled and beribboned (one of the few vanities he has), and reaches to his belt. He tends to accept only dwarven clients, but will take others if sufficient remuneration is offered (fee structure 5). Cardallo is afraid of this man, one of the few in the city that he respects, and gives him a +15% bonus (Argli felt Cardallo had been influenced unduly in a trial one time, and swore he would break every bone in Cardallo's body if he ever had any evidence that, at any trial at which both he and Cardallo worked, Cardallo took bribes or unduly favored either side - Cardallo believes him implicitly? None of the other judges particularly favor or dislike the dwarf, but because of his reputation for honesty and righteousness, all do give him a +5% bonus.

articles.content:
Followers are often artists and entertainers.

It should be noted that she is not a sex goddess; sex is a beautiful aspect of love, but isn't part of any specific rituals.

Also of note is the fact that her full parentage is not clear. Some say that @[Serindë](person:fed8a554-c5c1-48cd-932a-2457b1cc820d) brought Ariel into the world alone since love and beauty are unknowable thus @[Ladros](person:b07298f6-f8f9-4277-9023-b5771d9bcc85) can't be her father.

articles.content: Older scribe with a large collection of scrolls and leather bound volumes. While he copies with great flair and beauty, if the item is a magic scroll or instructional tome there is a chance of copying error or ommission.

articles.title: Arlog Gutray
articles.content: A fat, middle aged man with a thick beard and spectacles.  Arlog enjoys reading and has amassed a collection of over 500 books. They are in his private library near his personal quarters, which are on the second floor of his shop.

articles.title: Arquephus
articles.content:
The diminutive Keeper of Records may well be the most potentially powerful figure in the entire Guild (including the Grand and Chapter Masters). Arquephus and his staff of four maintain the complete ledgers of the Guild, and receive twice weekly reports from each Chapter leader detailing group activities and delivering the Guild's share of its take. His domain of rooms in the new Guild complex is isolated from the other chambers and well-guarded; judging from the frequent sounds of excavation and construction within, it appears that the area is still being modified to the Keeper's fastidious satisfactions. 

 It is he who keeps the Guild's steady fences and lawyers happy when the latter lodge complaints, and actually makes the decisions on the vast majority of requisitions. Though he wields these powers firmly, he has somehow managed to do so without inciting the concerns of his superiors, as evidenced by the fact that @[Sulemon Duur](person:287e8880-066e-4f87-971f-707c2560db62) is the fourth Grand Master Arquephus has served in this capacity.

articles.title: Artemis Guisto
articles.content: Artemis is a pleasant, white-haired old man; he is well-loved by the children of the neighborhood for his storytelling. Children are in and out of the shop and the yard of the house next door; all call Artemis, and his wife Glory, their "grandparents".

articles.title: Arthol Tedius
articles.content: A fletcher who specializes in the feathers and nock of arrows and bolts

articles.title: Arthur Emrys
articles.content: The owner of @[The Pendragon Inn](landmark:8aaefea5-dcd6-4b71-9167-d94a465e453f) is a tall, brawny man and a former caravan drover. He retains good relations with old friends who travel the Long Road, and is an excellent source of the most recent news (8 weeks old at most) from other cities and towns along the trade routes.

articles.title: Asgird asha Nikkolai
articles.content: Refer to the scenario @[The Bartered Brides](plot:dd72b5ff-fc3a-4506-9585-fd49f6a1bbd2).

articles.title: Astrilde de la Riis
articles.content: Astrilde, Morgan del la Riis' wife, is happy with her lot as a Guard's wife. She has honey-blond waist length hair, high cheekbones, and delicate features. Astrilde is sweet-tempered, but more than a trifle slow upstairs. If seen in the shops of Haven, she will be carrying her 6 month old baby daughter Bismunde, whom she dotes on to make up for her feelings of failure regarding Carlo, whose inquisitive, intellectual nature is beyond her comprehension. articles.content:
See Street Encounter: Astrologer 

 A tall skinny man in a robe elaborately decorated with symbols of sun, stars, moons, and planets.

articles.title: Aukhan Thuliaga
articles.content:
A bouncer at @[The Aerie](landmark:f24b8234-a53d-47df-84dd-26adc048a141), Aukhan is an example of the strong silent type. He is over 7' tall and 350lbs. He is so mean-looking, even his friends call him "Sir". Besides maintaining a strict watch over the entrance, Aukhan and the other goliath bouncers are summoned to the scene whenever trouble erupts. 

 Though he rarely speaks, he understands the need for delicacy in performing his job. He has become particularly adept at eliminating potential combatants by means of a surprisingly rapid head slap which renders the recipient unconscious, but causes no permanent damage  other than a ringing in one's ears for several hours after. 

 Aukhan seems to have little interest in fleshly pleasures, save for an occasional craving for raw meat

articles.title: Aygona Budge
articles.content: A ruddy-faced halfling who always wears a velvet waistcoat and pocket watch, Aygona moves about the rooms of his establishment making sure everything runs smoothly. He is a fairly wealthy man and pays top dollar to get the best caliber staff.  He firmly believes that the customer is always right - especially if the latter is bigger and meaner.

articles.title: Azimuth
articles.content:
To the Guild, Azimuth is dead and gone, assumed to have perished along with his two hulking bodyguards in the Rogues' Roost inferno, although his body was never found. In fact, Azimuth lives, albeit a maimed and disfigured shadow of his former gray eminence, in one of the many shabby flophouses in @[The Labyrinth](settlement:e05f9a94-a44d-4991-b419-28cae89db0ee), watching his former charges and plotting his grim vengeance; for Azimuth knows in his heart what only a few suspect - that while the fire was unquestionably set by members of the rival Black Hand, the arsonists were aided by Guild thieves, including at least one of his own lieutenants. 

 On the fateful evening of the fire, Azimuth and his ever-present guards dined with the members of his innermost council to discuss future strategies. He wakened later that night from a deep unnatural sleep long after the flames had begun racing through the building and found his bodyguards in a similar drugged slumber. The Master was forced to leave them behind to take the only possible route remaining through the ravaging blaze - the secret crawlway into the flue of the chimney. Even here, he suffered severe burns, and had the left side of his upper torso crushed as a section of @[Brick](person:d9388a1c-1b0e-471b-89a1-50f0b805b6c3) collapsed on him scant feet from safety. Still his will to live forced him to crawl onward, into the maze of underground passages beneath @[The Labyrinth](settlement:e05f9a94-a44d-4991-b419-28cae89db0ee). There, as he lay in a huddled, broken mass, he heard the voices of Hand operatives down an adjacent corridor congratulating themselves on the success of their efforts and the effectiveness of their "inside help". He decided then that one of his most trusted aides had deliberately drugged his meal, to ensure his death - and vowed silently to have his revenge. 

 Trusting no one in the Guild, Azimuth was forced to turn to one of the several disreputable surgeons in @[The Labyrinth](settlement:e05f9a94-a44d-4991-b419-28cae89db0ee) for medical aid – that healer's botched treatments (since paid for by his death) left Azimuth's one side badly crippled, and his face an ugly mass of scar fissure. He has rejoined the Guild's ranks (his mangled features disguised still further) as a common bigger named Nadiros, in order to obtain what information he can about his possible betrayers. He is incredibly paranoid (and who can blame him?) about anyone who seems to take an interest in his welfare, and often talks to himself. Although there is little question that the man is unhinged, he retains a dangerous and crafty intellect, with considerable monetary resources at his disposal (recovered from a number of private caches around the city). Although he has no proof, Azimuth is reasonably confident that his supplanter, Duur, is his Judas (he is totally wrong in this belief).

articles.title: Baez Sweetsinger
articles.content: Baez Sweetsinger drayed for some thirty years before he bought the @[Wagoneer's Delight](landmark:781675f6-3281-4e46-a7f5-808d404e5f24) caravanserai he now runs and rather prefers catering to drayers than drovers but will not turn away any business. The tall, spare owner is in his sixties, but still hale and healthy, with hair only slightly grayed at the temples. He is often found in the compound talking with the waggoneers who drive the Long Road, reminiscing about old times.

articles.title: Bag Lady
articles.content: See Street Encounter: Bag Lady

articles.title: Bakka Hofstra
articles.content:
Bakka resembles his mother, with a gentle smile, flame-red hair and blue eyes; he is of medium height, with a slight tendency to fat - in fact, he looks soft and pliable, not at all like the hard-headed and -hearted businessman he actually is. Bakka has inherited all his father's abilities and talents for finance, and he is Jaime's favorite (and chosen successor). 

 Bakka's one weak spot is his wife, of whom he is fiercely possessive. He does like to party, and he and Linden (his wife is one-quarter elvish, and the family is proud of the blood of the forest people) are frequently seen at various evening spots throughout the city. However, excessive attention paid to Linden (just about any attention is excessive) will raise the specter of jealousy in Bakka; he is not a fighter, but he knows his financial power, and has succeeded in driving out of the city more than one man of whom he was jealous. articles.content: A large man with ham-like fists will usually wade in to settle disputes before too much furniture gets destroyed in the refutations; he is usually fairly successful in these endeavors.

articles.content: Balin is a harried looking fellow, thinning hair perpetually mussed, and is constantly worried about meeting impossible deadlines.

articles.title: Barbara Weyr
articles.content: A youngish woman of fair complexion and feature who deals normally in fine rugs and carpets and maintains a good stock of such in the tent. She also functions as a fence for jewelry items lifted by some of the markets thieves.

articles.title: Bardol Murchisson
articles.content: Bardol retired from the practice of magic about ten years ago but keeps his hand in by entertaining his customers in the evenings with small displays of prestidigitation and minor illusions. The @[Mystic Valley Inn](landmark:fc4977a0-97c2-4523-b5ff-b34449124515) has been part of the Haven cityscape for nearly two centuries, and Bardol inherited it from his father. He has no children of his own, and plans to will the establishment to the Mages Guild with the proviso that they keep it open to the public. He is tall and round (he likes good food and drink), with a wreath of white hair which flies wildly in all directions.

articles.title: Bartholomew d'Larette
articles.content: A short, round little man, with thick grey hair and a moustache; he wears a tasteful, but not gaudy tunic, and hose and a cheerful smile. His family has managed the @[Horn and Hardart](landmark:4bebd228-9482-45ed-8753-23962694809d) for four generations, and he is very much a traditionalist. Serving the inn's patrons is his life and he allows nothing less than perfection in that service. Knows most of Haven's elite by sight and name.

articles.title: Benham Barleyman
articles.content:
A sandy-haired, handsome young halfling who frequently takes long trips out of Haven, the purpose of which he remains silent about. On the rare occasions he returns to @[The Dell](settlement:e8aa9d8f-68be-4d89-9e11-6ba288e71515), he is usually surrounded and pressed for tales of his travels. 

 He may also be cajoled into playing a few tunes on the fiddle, which always brings a crowd to @[The Green](landmark:58c2143a-18ef-4281-89c4-96547a184d4a). Barleyman is quite an experienced thief, but will not ply his trade while within the confines of the city.

articles.title: Benjaman MacRyan
articles.content: The proprietor of this sprawling stone and half-timber inn, he stands 6 foot 4 inches tall, with bushy sideburns and a jovial face - and a belly that attests to the quality and quantity of his beer. Ben is a good natured fellow, always ready for a beer, a good joke, or a good brawl - he has hands like a wrestler's and usually acts as his own bouncer if things get "unneighbourly".

articles.content: A baker who looks as if she's sampled too many of her own wares. She and her husband @[Porginald](person:625968eb-e3bf-4169-8896-6c7132cc19a8) have numerous children, all on the pudgy side.

articles.title: Bethli
articles.content: Bethli himself is a rather congenial dwarf with a ruddy complexion and a love of fine whiskey. He forges hammers and swords as a hobby - though he is a mediocre craftsman.

articles.title: Beydom
articles.content: Looks like a large bowling pin with arms and legs. He runs a stall in the @[Thieves' Market](settlement:8b3bf96f-ea9a-4e39-8c3f-bda804df5cdb)

articles.title: Bianca
articles.content:
Bianca is a young newcomer at @[The Blue Lantern](landmark:c39a381b-8d84-4ac7-aa93-3f280a7f2dba) and has made quite a splash with the customers. She is very beautiful, of medium height, slender, with blonde hair and blue eyes. 

She is in reality the runaway daughter of a noble family on @[The Heights](settlement:1f0571c0-b8de-4b50-b010-5529cab6603b), the Tainleys. She has altered her name and dyed her hair to change her appearance. (Refer to scenario The Nobleman's Daughter). 

 @[Byelaya Tainley](person:fc9ce341-d93f-4d7f-a194-022a4e7ece22) was always known as a loner by the other maidens of @[The Heights](settlement:1f0571c0-b8de-4b50-b010-5529cab6603b) and has only one close friend - @[Cortina de la Riis](person:bc9967fb-4969-46fd-94cf-0294e48ffb27). As a young girl she heard a very romantic story in which the heroine was a courtesan and since then has had dreams of being a hetaera (a very high class courtesan) herself. She has confided these dreams to no one, not even her closest friend. 

 Three months ago, she dyed her hair blonde, changed her name to Bianca, and ran away from home. Bianca eventually started  working at @[The Blue Lantern](landmark:c39a381b-8d84-4ac7-aa93-3f280a7f2dba) on @[The Street of Silk Veils](settlement:587a7a3a-ba45-4bfd-94bc-fe6e17ae023c). No one at the house knows her origins and certainly no one suspects she is the daughter of a noble house. 

Bianca/Byelaya is a natural courtesan - she enjoys men and women and her clients definitely enjoy her. Bianca has that indefinable quality of innocence that they find irresistible. She has rapidly progressed, in the little time she has been at @[The Blue Lantern](landmark:c39a381b-8d84-4ac7-aa93-3f280a7f2dba), from a very green novice to a competent intermediate.

articles.title: Bick Dutkus
articles.content: A 6'6", 250lb. Bruiser who provides "insurance" for @[Tael I'she-Kel](person:ca90a378-b14d-41af-86f3-d9037a365727) in the @[Thieves' Market](settlement:8b3bf96f-ea9a-4e39-8c3f-bda804df5cdb).

articles.title: Biduli Munarkil
articles.content: A tall, heavy set horse trainer with a limp, who works for Hrubilasz (????????). One of his duties is to scout the horse pens each morning to check on likely stock for training; he has noticed the odd palomino belonging to Liriki, and is wondering why anyone would try to sell such a miserable piece of horseflesh at @[The Auction Block](landmark:67b5d2df-9421-4945-8139-69de4d5ec4da). If engaged in conversation, he is friendly and talkative, and there is a 35% chance he will make a reference to the "awkward looking stallion with the weird blue eyes".

articles.title: Biff Tekk
articles.content: A butcher selling in the @[Thieves' Market](settlement:8b3bf96f-ea9a-4e39-8c3f-bda804df5cdb).

articles.title: Bing
articles.content:
Bing and his brother, @[Bob](person:a6d18909-f289-433c-ad20-5c682eac3f83), seem to act as two halves of one personality. He has a ruddy-face and slightly rotund and is a bit taller than @[Bob](person:a6d18909-f289-433c-ad20-5c682eac3f83). 

 Bing fancies himself a singer and loves to sing love songs and ballads, particularly when there are ladies present. @[Bob](person:a6d18909-f289-433c-ad20-5c682eac3f83) may be known for his interest in the opposite sex, but Bing always seems to get the girl. 

 He and @[Bob](person:a6d18909-f289-433c-ad20-5c682eac3f83) stick together, and frequently one finishes a sentence the other had started, and they occasionally answer in unison. 

 Bing uses a sling with proficiency but will fight only to save his or @[Bob](person:a6d18909-f289-433c-ad20-5c682eac3f83)'s life; content to take cover under a wagon at any hint of trouble. 

 The brothers are also the cooks for the troupe.

articles.title: Bob
articles.content:
Bob and his brother, @[Bing](person:1c2912cc-9c2e-4c7c-afbf-4851697692ed), seem to act as two halves of one personality. He is ruddy-faced, slightly rotund and losing his hair. 

 Bob tells jokes and funny stories, and has a quick wit, and an incredible arsenal of bad puns. He is also known for his interest in the opposite sex, but @[Bing](person:1c2912cc-9c2e-4c7c-afbf-4851697692ed) always seems to get the girl. 

 He and @[Bing](person:1c2912cc-9c2e-4c7c-afbf-4851697692ed) stick together, and frequently one finishes a sentence the other had started, and they occasionally answer in unison. 

 Bob uses a sling with proficiency but will fight only to save his or @[Bing](person:1c2912cc-9c2e-4c7c-afbf-4851697692ed)'s life; content to take cover under a wagon at any hint of trouble. 

 The brothers are also the cooks for the troupe.

articles.title: Boccaccio de Kammeron
articles.content:
The younger de Kammeron is known around Haven as the "Merry Widower", for he has recently remarried - the third time in seven years. All Boccaccio's brides have been very old matrons who were the sole heirs to sizable financial estates and it is rumored that all three of his prior wives "died smiling", made happy in their waning days by his grace, charm and razor-sharp wit. His current wife, the Lady Alvona Dwillian de Kammeron, has been bedridden for months with pleurisy. During her illness, Boccaccio has expertly handled the day to day affairs of the family's watchmaking business. 

Boccaccio has inherited a number of choice residential properties in @[The Heights](settlement:1f0571c0-b8de-4b50-b010-5529cab6603b) section of Haven and in each case he has divided this real estate into a number of parcels. He then sold the fragments at a huge profit to members of the "nouveau riche" anxious to acquire the status associated with this exclusive neighborhood. This practice infuriates the @[Young Stallions](organization:7340b23d-2c0c-45fd-8222-13b00aa2760c) to no end, but to date they have been able to do little about it except attempt to intimidate potential buyers. 

Though Boccaccio’s brief forays into the business world clearly indicates his acumen, he also goes through phases of extreme self-indulgence when he wastes great sums of money on epic binges of debauchery. In these latter times (which sometimes last for weeks), Boccaccio may acquire an entourage of up to 50 fellow revelers. [br][br] [familytree:7987c903-5d74-4fd2-ba5a-b45ef9d76f18] [br]

articles.title: Bokkhra
articles.content:
An exceptional Goliath, Bokkhra stands about 7'8" and weighs near 600 pounds; his skin is a slatey-gray and his eyes are red. Bokkhra's exceptional status is from his mental abilities - he is an esper, capable of reading emotions and, occasionally, sensing the meaning of the thoughts of the people around him. 

Presently, he is working in a saloon called @[The Snowblind Mouse](landmark:17267de1-5a94-4939-91d2-84cec7582207), as the bouncer; the tavern has become known as a great place to go for a quiet drink since he began work there, since anyone who attempts to cause trouble is likely to leave rapidly, crashing through the swinging doors and rolling down the street. Bokkhra dislikes "troublemakers" because of the pain in the head they give him and he tends to remove the irritating presence as quickly as possible - usually by chucking the person bodily out of the tavern (or wherever else he happens to be). People swiftly learn to "think pretty" around him. 

He rents a room 'in a rambling pile of a building referred to as @[Duhm's Rooms](landmark:f83b9e6a-745d-459a-b363-a6759cb707bd), but usually eats at the tavern. Bokkhra does like the city, for its variety and color, but wishes more people would "think pretty", so he could stop having "hurt in head".

articles.title: Boldan Hansumrogge
articles.content:
The Minister of Highways is occasionally seen galloping into Haven from either the Horse Gate in @[The South Corridor](settlement:d684e9e8-9b69-45fc-8352-3de0e6e7f870), or the Caravan Gate in the North.  He and his band are charged with the suppression of banditry along the Long Road and the routine maintenance of the roadway. 

 Boldan  is an exceptionally strong, well built, and good-looking centaur, with green eyes and long blond hair which whips in the wind when he runs. He has developed a fondness for a half-elven girl (who happens to reciprocate his feelings), and will normally be found at her home in @[The Glens](settlement:e11d38ab-9461-4be2-b745-34ddf86ec7fb) when not out of the city on anti-highwaymen forays (most of Haven is wondering about this relationship). 

 He leads a band of mixed two- and four-legged fighters (two-legs frequently riding four-legs), who have developed a reputation for ruthless efficiency in the extermination of bandits and other undesirables who attempt to prey on the Long Road's traffic.

articles.title: Bonyodel
articles.content: A stout man in a herald-style tabard and a staff, who struts about the Island, occasionally making announcements in a booming, clear voice. These range from bans of marriage, advertisements for one merchant or another, to help wanted and lost dogs. Bonyodel charges 5 CP for a given announcement of a limited duration, given twice, at opposite ends of the Island. No Insults, Profanity, or Foreign Tongues.

articles.title: Branden d'Larette
articles.content:
Branden, oldest child of Bartholomew and Amelia, is a chunky youth of 19 who he is trying to learn the business of running the inn, but lacks his father's drive for perfection when he feels his service is not appreciated. 

 He is in love with Felitia, a singer/actress who occasionally performs at the @[Horn and Hardart](landmark:4bebd228-9482-45ed-8753-23962694809d). He has an intense dislike of @[Paul de la Riis](person:61db5c85-e436-459e-926e-17ad7e116b03), for the latter's flirting with Felitia, and will be less than gracious to any other offender.

articles.title: Branden Varrasch
articles.content:
Brandon is the aged former leader of the Varrasch clan. He was renowned in his prime as a fearless horse breaker, able to calm the wildest stallions. A few years ago Branden suffered a fall from a horse that left his legs completely crippled, and he is now confined to a wheelchair. 

His brother @[Valken Varrasch](person:c56af9c6-97bd-4393-9e4b-3dbadea05e92) is not ageing well, so younger brothers Heidel Varrash and Kronen Varrash have taken over the business. Despite them having done well, both Branden and Valken are angry that they are no longer consulted about major business decisions. [br][br] [familytree:d0d6bb38-4e31-4b06-8814-90d8d3ce984c] [br]

articles.title: Brick
articles.content:
Built like the dockworker he once was, he now works for @[Neberhard Ohlfaardt](person:aa435b8d-e5f0-4e61-8d17-d6db601760b6), along with three others filling a job officially described as "personal assistant". It is however primarily aimed at keeping @[Sui Tuong Ding](person:908c4354-d81f-42f0-9be5-c227e30d2e2c) out of the clutches of other men. Brick will defer to @[Skiff Borden](person:3cade294-0a89-4913-884a-a82dc2ef320c) in all things and is often called upon to provide a demonstration of what will happen if a potential suitor won’t leave Sui alone. 

 Brick is built like a refrigerator with legs, with a completely shaven head and a maniacal look in his eyes; when the mood strikes him, he has been known to juggle three or four oaken chairs like they were tennis balls, or to lift the central beam holding up the roof of a building off the floor. 

 Brick is not very intelligent and it's not clear that Brick actually thinks at all, but he does like beer, and gets to drink it in copious quantities. [br][br] [familytree:d9388a1c-1b0e-471b-89a1-50f0b805b6c3] [br]

articles.content: Browin has the physical appearance of a dwarf but is actually an alien being from another sphere which has a portal that opens onto this world on rare occasions. The shop is the only two-story aboveground structure in @[The Dwarrow](settlement:fa91fd8a-f74e-409d-a703-26a9b8e09954), and most of its neighbors view Browin and his employees as almost dangerously eccentric.

articles.title: Bruning de la Riis
articles.content:
A stocky man with dirty blond hair, and a robust appearance that belies his age. Well-known in Haven in his youth for his several victories in city jousting tournaments, he has spent the last twenty years as a knight in the military service of the late Viscount of Kveklan. With the coronation of the Viscount's son, Bruning was dismissed; the old warhorse is now chafing at the bit from inactivity and would be receptive to joining an expedition if it were satisfactorily funded and led by a fellow noble. 

Bruning returned to the city after an absence of many years with a new bride, a commoner woman almost half his age named K'maill.

He can be contacted through the mercenaries guild in Haven, the Sworn Swords (OE) in @[The South Corridor](settlement:d684e9e8-9b69-45fc-8352-3de0e6e7f870). [br][br] [familytree:743beb40-df18-47f5-8bdf-144dcc690b88] [br]

articles.title: Bundy Chubb
articles.content:
Daughter of Otto Chub, Bundy has gotten herself in the "family way", and is desperately searching for a male halfling willing to be her husband. To that end she hangs around outside her parents' butcher shop checking out male halflings that wander by. 

 She is quite comely of face and form (though looking at her parents, one could justifiably have doubts about how long her svelteness will last); and would make a good homemaker.

articles.title: Burbas the Finder
articles.content: Provides a service find "misplaced" items

articles.title: Burley Stonecastle
articles.content: Slender for a halfling, and seems to have an excess of energy for this usually sedate folk. In court, he is attentive to all that happens, and is sharp in questioning witnesses. Most of the judges like him, and he has a +10% preference with all except Cardallo, who dislikes the little man intensely (-15% penalty). Burley lives in @[The Dell](settlement:e8aa9d8f-68be-4d89-9e11-6ba288e71515), and may be found of an evening at the larger of the two halflings-only-taverns in @[The Dell](settlement:e8aa9d8f-68be-4d89-9e11-6ba288e71515). He prefers halfling clients, but will accept as client anybody he believes is innocent, or getting a raw deal.

articles.title: Byelaya Tainley
articles.content:
The Lady Byelaya went missing a little while ago and her father is looking to hire someone to ensure her safe return (refer to scenario The Nobleman's Daughter). 

 Byelaya Tainley was always known as a loner by the other maidens of @[The Heights](settlement:1f0571c0-b8de-4b50-b010-5529cab6603b) and has only one close friend - @[Cortina de la Riis](person:bc9967fb-4969-46fd-94cf-0294e48ffb27). 
 
 As a young girl she heard a very romantic story in which the heroine was a courtesan and since then has had dreams of being a hetaera (a very high class courtesan) herself. She has confided these dreams to no one, not even her closest friend. 

 Three months ago, she dyed her hair brown, changed her name to @[Bianca](person:e63156eb-0dbc-4d4f-acf6-7a26e6af346f), and ran away from home. @[Bianca](person:e63156eb-0dbc-4d4f-acf6-7a26e6af346f) eventually started  working at @[The Blue Lantern](landmark:c39a381b-8d84-4ac7-aa93-3f280a7f2dba) on @[The Street of Silk Veils](settlement:587a7a3a-ba45-4bfd-94bc-fe6e17ae023c). No one at the house knows her origins and certainly no one suspects she is the daughter of a noble house. [br][br] [familytree:fc9ce341-d93f-4d7f-a194-022a4e7ece22] [br]

articles.title: Calder the Whip
articles.content: @[The Briarthorn Inn](landmark:133a86b1-73a5-44d6-a46c-a247fdb06a5e) is run by a tall, broad-shouldered man with a scarred face known as Calder the Whip (#1828); he is a former highwayman, and is an expert with the bullwhip he wears at his hip. Calder does little of the work of the inn, except lounge behind his desk and collect rents.

articles.title: Cariadoc
articles.content:
Cariadoc is a short, broad-shouldered man with a handsome' face and a wide grin. His cheerful expression conceals a temperament cold and vicious, and a disposition rarely better than dourly melancholy. Cariadoc grins widest while watching the death throes of his enemies, and likes to be present when his men torture and interrogate opponents. 

 He is the master of @[The Black Hand](organization:d1a96263-4191-482e-ace6-360d25106f60) guild that controls assassination and murder for hire, and his thugs and toughs provide protection and strong-arm support for other Hand guilds.

articles.title: Carlo de la Riis
articles.content:
Carlo is a thin, frail young lad of 10, with an unkempt mop of brown hair, and very intense brown eyes; his left arm is severely withered, and hangs uselessly at his side. His father, @[Morgan de la Riis](person:2a538a9e-2951-4c43-9f63-ad552ddc25df) has a hard time dealing with Carlo’s deformity ignores him while his disability also isolates him from his peers. Carlo possesses an almost eerie intensity that often makes adults in his presence uncomfortable. Because of this, Carlo spends his days wandering through @[The Heights](settlement:1f0571c0-b8de-4b50-b010-5529cab6603b), @[The North Corridor](settlement:4554e4a9-db69-47da-9921-6c5850001ce8), and even @[Trade Island](settlement:eec2fc60-5565-40fa-9047-69924589c400), observing (and sometimes reacting to) the events going on around him. 

 The boy has minor precognitive abilities (visions of events that will happen 10-15 minutes in the future). If he is in the vicinity of a player-character or NPC about to take an action, there is a 30% chance that Carlo will "see" the event in advance. If the actions to be taken by the other character arouse Carlo's curiosity, he is likely to approach and ask questions of the other that reveal what he knows. 

 Carlo is quite capable of using his knowledge to bargain for a piece of the action, or a bribe to purchase his silence. If he is treated with respect, and not as a "child", there is some chance that Carlo would agree to use his powers to aid others (particularly if these characters will provide him with some useful training in exchange for these services). [br][br] [familytree:aa55a60e-fe80-4403-a70c-5b2823bd8983] [br]

articles.title: Carp
articles.content:
A small, brown fellow, who hawks his odiferous wares in a surprisingly powerful basso profundo, wheeling his little pushcart throughout the dock area. There is little that escapes his notice as he patrols his turf, and he is perfectly willing to pass on interesting information for a little cash. 

 Although he claims to be loyal to none save himself, there beats beneath his smelly exterior a heart of purest mush, and he has been known to surreptitiously aid others who were down on their luck.

See scenario @[The Lady in the Bottle](plot:784140fc-e6b0-4b58-ad03-943ad240153c)

articles.title: Cecilia Sandhill
articles.content: Waitress at @[The Bandersnatch Inn](landmark:673b7551-f8ba-46cd-876a-1af1cec5e801) with her twin sister Lurella

articles.title: Celebel
articles.content: Celebel, so called because he has silvery hair and eyes as white as stars, runs a fine dining establishment in @[Erinhir](settlement:96d2680b-e669-4c07-ba6b-f4727fb8d9d9). He works mostly in the kitchen with 4 journeymen chefs.

articles.title: Celeblinde Conindir
articles.content: Son of @[Teleril Conindir](person:bc2a44c4-5c6e-4d5e-ab5f-46c2d2791193) and @[Khelekien Conindir](person:65d84133-9176-4cfe-9b19-bc0c6f5a9235) [br][br] [familytree:41f15dd8-e212-4061-8e40-e045a31d023e] [br]

articles.title: Chalka
articles.content:
Common thief. 

 A former street rat, Chalka is small and lean, her dark hair cut short like a boy’s. Time spent as a child hanging around the acrobats and tumblers of @[Circus Park](landmark:9b3f3e48-d7d7-4cc0-82b3-de141c42956d) was put to good use; Chalka is an expert climber, but prefers the more lucrative career as a second story burglar to that of a carnival acrobat. She is also a practiced lock pick. Part of her success is due to her careful planning of any heist; Chalka never takes needless risks, and will abort a job if something unexpected occurs that she had not planned for.

articles.title: Charlie Hofstra
articles.content:
Charlie and brother @[Dauge](person:985abb36-bd46-4191-a8d9-aaf0a14bade2) are identical twins. They are tall, heavily built, with black hair and dark eyes, and even seem to think alike. Both are outdoorsmen, and are quite likely (and happy for the opportunity) to take to the road as couriers for the family business on very short notice, not to return for two or three weeks. They are in the process of arranging remount stations, coach stops, and contracts for light freighting in the @[Ten Cities](organization:0efc56fc-301e-4d3f-ba8c-019da1b01590), hoping to provide competition for Messers Welshe and Fargot. 

Neither is married, but they are currently sharing quarters with identical twin girls (the confusion must be incredible - who sleeps with whom?). [br][br] [familytree:2a76cfbd-2b71-47b8-b505-c9cad32e55af] [br]

articles.title: Chawser
articles.content:
See scenario The Tiefling's Tale 

 Known for his quick wit and inventive mind when it comes to getting out of tight scrapes.

articles.title: Chelsea Cheddar
articles.content:
Chelsea is a rather chunky, dark-haired, young halfling woman with a throaty alto voice and a falsely sultry demeanor. She desperately wants to become an adventuress, and has become good friends with the old wanderer @[Rombo Alecastle](person:47bb3055-9d64-4cfb-8e98-cf96cd3170aa), for whom she runs errands, and transcribes and edits the undisciplined mass of jottings and notes he has made of his life's adventures. 

 Chelsea may often be found at either the Wayfarer's Rest or Bandersnatch Inn during the evening, keeping an ear open for one or more adventurers who might be interested in helping Rombo find his lost son (see Dell, Scenarios). In helping Rombo, she hopes to kill two birds with one stone by accompanying the search party on its journey. 

 As noted, Chelsea will try to tempt potential employers with the intimation of sexual favors to come. In fact, however, she is very romantic and innocent at heart, and would be at a great loss about what to do if her bluff were called.

articles.title: Chiles Putney
articles.content:
A tall, ruggedly handsome fellow with thick, curly blond hair, piercing blue eyes and a deep, masculine voice. Dresses in the height of fashion; appears poised and somewhat foppish. Chiles is an actor, in the best of the classic tradition. On stage he cuts a dashing figure; a perfect leading man. 

 Off stage, Chiles still acts the part of the "star" he is extravagant with money when he has it (and a borrower of money when he has it not). He is vain about his appearance, always positioning himself to show off his best side, constantly smoothing his hair or his garments with his fingers. Unfortunately, Chiles is not too bright, but he seems to be able to be able to overlook this flow, as does his "public", which Chiles speaks of constantly and in reverent tone after all, his "public" made him into what he is today.

articles.title: Cimeron
articles.content: Ship's mage on the Pavanne, he is a small, dark fellow whose skills include weather and repair spells.  Doesn't really trust the captain, Emilio.

articles.title: Clairone
articles.content:
A beautiful girl of 18, with wide, violet eyes, fair skin, and waist-length hair of jet black, with a sweet soprano voice. Clairone always plays the heroine in the troupe's various plays, a part she is admirably suited for, due to her looks and the fact that to play the princess-in-distress is not a difficult role. 

 Clairone's chief joy is beautiful clothes, and will spend a great deal of time on trying on costumes and putting on cosmetics. She is a bit of an airhead at best, and only the loving supervision of her father keeps her from doing incredibly foolish things. She, alone of all the company, believes Toric's stories, and will actually be upset when he is kicked out of the troupe but this will only last until the next morning, when she will have forgotten his name.

articles.title: Claudia de la Riis
articles.content:
The wife of @[Harz de la Riis](person:35c67bc0-3762-429d-b35e-c4d0eac46490) is a tall, spare woman with sharp angular features and a thin, oval face. She uses excessive make-up, perfume, and tight-bodiced clothing to hide the effects of middle age of her appearance, and is extremely vain about her looks. 

[ul]
[li]Talkative, and gossipy, and always has an opinion on how things should be done. [br][br]
[li]In her youth, she was an excellent equestrian, but now she rarely rides in the hunt. [br][br]
[li]She is prone to hypochondria, and frequently seeks the medical advice of the charlatan @[Americus](person:db7258df-d1e4-483a-a65f-df6464ef8489)[br][br]
[li]Owns a dog names Billy that she dotes upon and refers to as "her baby" (See @[My Baby!](plot:16cf4663-8cf0-40a5-87fd-be654b60816d)).
[/ul] [br][br] [familytree:646e36a4-cc41-4a91-8076-5af2dcb007fb] [br]

articles.title: Clearwater
articles.content: @[Silverthorne](person:6314ff3e-fadd-42ba-aa6c-bf26fc2767bc) has a small band of loyal followers, who have sworn to defend him and his interests, and to help him regain his throne. Clearwater is a mage and a good judge of character. All are staying at @[The Mallorn](landmark:11a61b6d-c93a-47c0-b483-46c0dcf8996d), and may be encountered at various places throughout the city.

articles.title: Clemente Panfusille
articles.content:
Clemente, Rutmilla de la Riis’ husband, is close friends with @[Morgan de la Riis](person:2a538a9e-2951-4c43-9f63-ad552ddc25df) and they are fellow officers in Haven's prestigious @[Citadel Guard](organization:d8426ad5-1874-4152-82a5-98179c3a4666). Both have served in the Guard for more than ten years, and are very pleased to have the chance to exert authority over the vendors and visitors of @[Trade Island](settlement:eec2fc60-5565-40fa-9047-69924589c400). 

 Clemente's face still shows the ravages of a childhood bout of smallpox. Unlike Morgan, who is almost universally liked, Clemente is viewed as a martinet by the men in his barracks, for he drills his command hard and very frequently. He is a very loyal husband uninterested in other women, and is happy with his rather pedestrian duties harboring no great urges to seek a more adventurous avocation. [br][br] [familytree:fcb05ff0-a44e-435c-88c3-7c7d8eb9ad00] [br]

articles.title: Cocoa Tobler
articles.content: Cocoa, a large and very brown man (with a taste for chocolate - hence his nickname), has a great love for animals

articles.title: Conrad Bissell
articles.content:
Conrad is a small ferret faced man and is one of the three day-shift assistant customs inspectors employed by the ministry of Ports and Shipping to collect customs duties along @[The South Docks](settlement:e2e38a16-2c10-443d-b40a-6789aa7c041a), under the direction of Inspector @[Valyri Pipper](person:652a7861-c505-4742-85a0-2d8163986283). Alphonso Caradello attempts to arrange for Black Hand cargos to be inspected by Bissell  who places the proper seals and stamps upon the appropriate items. Nonetheless, there is only a 65% chance that Bissell will be the inspector on duty at any given time. Illegal Black Hand cargos, therefore, are usually well concealed, even when Caradello has arranged for Bissell to inspect the smuggler. 

 In exchange for his duplicity, Caradello pays Bissell an annual gratuity, and arranged for Bissell's sister to receive training and employment as a courtesan from @[The Black Whip](landmark:6f66e600-9089-49a6-b9dc-7e4dd9febe5c) (small government officials, like beggars, cannot afford to be choosers).

articles.title: Constantino Maylino
articles.content: Under the direction of Alphonso Caradello, Maylino oversees the buying and storage of illicit cargos for the small fleet of Black Hand smugglers that operates along the river. Unknown to Maylino, cargos smuggled into Haven are stored in Caradello's warehouse, or at Sym's Storage.

articles.title: Coppin Oxblood
articles.content:
Leader of the @[Brotherhood of the Broken Blade](organization:4a287a6e-7bd4-4721-9333-79ee98681350), Coppin is a rugged-looking fellow, with a weather-beaten face, and part of his right ear missing (a souvenir of a barroom knife fight in his younger days). Coppin is one of the few members of the Brotherhood who still earns his living with his sword and still accepts guard and mercenary assignments provided they do not last longer than 3 months duration.  

 He visited Arkendelve in his youth, and has strong memories of the great Halls, and the massive smelters rumbling deep in the bowels of Mount Thaare. It is his steadfast perseverance that keeps the Brotherhood going in its darkest hours of disappointment. Coppin is certain that the dwarf fated to possess Waarhite will be a great fighter, and is hopeful that he will also be of noble blood (and thereby likely to resettle Arkendelve and rebuild its greatness). 

 He is adamantly opposed to letting those who are not fighters handle @[The Broken Blade](plot:4db0d0e3-3179-4e90-855f-ad252b32b4c5), for he believes they sully its greatness. 

 See also scenario @[The Broken Blade](plot:4db0d0e3-3179-4e90-855f-ad252b32b4c5).

articles.title: Cor del Brasso
articles.content: Random entertainer to be user as necessary

articles.title: Cortina de la Riis
articles.content: Harz del la Riis' daughter is a small but amply endowed girl, with long brown hair and hazel eyes. Both of her older brothers are very protective of her; she longs to be independent, and often develops impetuous crushes on young gentlemen she meets (particularly if they are well-traveled). Her parents both indulge her every whim; thus, though she shows little aptitude, Cortina is taking (at great expenses) operatic singing lessons with @[Largo Profundo](person:650522c3-ae93-4b5e-b2bb-43bd5ef14271) on @[The Street of Harps](settlement:6053011d-37a6-4d6b-8e0b-41925f3bbd77). articles.title: Corwin Ariosto
articles.content:
Corwin is master of one of @[The Black Hand](organization:d1a96263-4191-482e-ace6-360d25106f60)’s two traditional thieving guilds. He is an older, more cautious man, who has been with the Hand for many years. Because of his experience and his known trustworthiness, Ariosto has been assigned the much more difficult territory of @[The South Corridor](settlement:d684e9e8-9b69-45fc-8352-3de0e6e7f870) and adjoining areas including @[The Labyrinth](settlement:e05f9a94-a44d-4991-b419-28cae89db0ee). 

 His guild is larger, containing four cells (almost twenty men) and includes a cell made up of the finest Hand thieves - possibly the best thieving team in Haven, although a few individuals surpass them in skill.

articles.title: Cowry Keltus
articles.content: Cowry is a stocky but well-built middle-aged man with white hair and eyebrows, green eyes, and a nose that appears to have been broken many times. He is a hearty drinker, and, when reasonably lit, will tell lurid stories of his exploits (in which he always leaves scores of corpses strewn about, and invariably winds up with at least three beautiful women panting in his arms).

articles.title: Creature of Earth and Stone
articles.content:
Small creatures of earth and stone, which function as rather slow bare-handed fighters (packing a reasonable wallop, but likely to be shattered to pieces by a good blow) 

 Refer to scenario @[The Broken Blade](plot:4db0d0e3-3179-4e90-855f-ad252b32b4c5)

articles.title: Creature of Flesh and Bone
articles.content:
Vaguely recognizable as their former dwarven identities but with misshapen hunks of rock and mud jutting out of their joints or oozing from their eyes and mouths. They retain some instinctive memory of their former fighting skills, and can use weapons; their new form provides them with a natural AC of 17. 

 Refer to scenario @[The Broken Blade](plot:4db0d0e3-3179-4e90-855f-ad252b32b4c5)

articles.title: Credence Bond
articles.content:
Guard in @[The Grey Halls](landmark:29cb4deb-4fef-475f-8c31-0d8e6f188cda). See scenario @[The Rescue Attempt](plot:226319b0-e928-43f5-ab74-bb3e6df90e77). 

  A dark complexioned, dark haired man of melancholy countenance

articles.title: Cruncher McGee
articles.content:
General alley basher/legbreakers/other muscle.

 Cruncher is slow-witted even by alley basher standards, and has a tendency to forget even simple instructions if left alone for more than five minutes. His chief value is as a visible threat, and he is very good at crushing bricks to rubble with his bare hands as a demonstration.

articles.title: Culver Trask
articles.content: Culver is a tall middle-aged merchant with hair still jet black, and piercing gray eyes; possessed of a humble self-image, he is genuinely grateful for his modest business successes, and strives to provide rapid service for his customers (he will make urgent or private personal deliveries himself, and can be trusted to keep a confidence - except from his wife, whom he worships completely).

articles.title: Culvhen
articles.content: The leader of @[Adrielle's Watch](organization:81808025-b365-4b84-9f1f-9a7025b37278) is a golden-eyed elf who has developed an excessive fondness for brandy. He keeps in surreptitious contact with Adrielle concerning payment for his watchers' work.

articles.title: Curadon
articles.content:
An excellent healer, although he cannot heal his own condition. Disfigured, hideous to behold, bent and misshapen, he is frequently referred to as the Monster Man; the other healers, even the priests of the various temples, have reached the conclusion that Curadon is the victim of some horrific and incredibly strong curse, one that there seems to be no relieving. 

Curadon normally stays in @[The House of Healing](landmark:1492ed4d-d033-49ab-8758-b8a004a61d2d), but he will venture out to help the rare person who has need of his skill but is unable to travel to him.

He is much revered by the healers in the city, and they do what they can to protect him.

articles.title: Custer
articles.content:
Common thief. 

 A cutpurse and pickpocket, Custer's favorite trick is the use of a gaudy red hat to attract attention away from his face. To affect his disguise, he discards the hat, and fades into the crowds. His plain features and drab clothing also serve to make him less memorable. The ruse is so successful that Custer has had the chance to hone his pickpocketing skills until he rarely has to rely on the hat to save his skin.

articles.title: Dagar Oakenhaft
articles.content:
Although rather slight for a smith this red-bearded dwarf is no less powerful for his lack of girth (his secret is tremendous upper arm strength). He works at a forge mounted on a large, rectangular wooden platform, under a partially open wood canopy. 

Dagar is newlywed, and totally and completely infatuated with his new bride, Merian (found for him by Meydal).  He may be convinced to trade his services for a traveler's small trinket if he thinks it will brighten Merian's eye.

articles.title: Dagnir Saurul
articles.content: Dagnir is the only non-human judge in the Haven @[Courts](landmark:5fe07c2b-bce5-4c96-880d-d72a70bb1352); he is a handsome elf, of middle years (only 193 last birthday), with flowing brown hair and brown eyes, average in height and weight. As can be seen from his decision tables, he favors elves in any court action, and is fairly strict with non-elves. He hates Cardallo, and would eliminate him from the @[Courts](landmark:5fe07c2b-bce5-4c96-880d-d72a70bb1352) with little provocation, and from the city, and from the world.

articles.title: Daisy Pinafore
articles.content: A plump, matronly woman with a cheery smile, Daisy greets each ship with a fray full of ribbons, laces, snuff, pipe weed, and candy for sailors to use for gifts to their sweethearts; she is well-known among the sailors and dock denizens. She knows almost every ship and captain better than the register of ships, and is an excellent source of trivial information about the ships and their crews.

articles.title: Dalbert
articles.content: Dalbert runs a small low budget apothecary.

articles.title: Dallarie asha Orli
articles.content: Refer to scenario @[The Bartered Brides](plot:dd72b5ff-fc3a-4506-9585-fd49f6a1bbd2).

articles.title: Damiano Dwarf-Friend
articles.content:
Short and getting stout in his later years, Damiano has a long beard, and his chestnut hair is shot with grey. Damiano represents a number of Dwarven communities in the south-eastern mountains, and his cart contains toys and other small well-crafted items made by skilled Dwarven craftsmen abroad and in Haven, often carrying mail and other messages to and from @[The Dwarrow](settlement:fa91fd8a-f74e-409d-a703-26a9b8e09954). 

 Damiano speaks the @[Dwarven Language](language:42256458-13cf-4a77-aa71-bda19f673522) well, and has a 20% bonus to dealings with Dwarves. It is said that he is never (well, hardly ever) cheated by a Dwarf, because he is also a sharp bargainer, 

 Damiano is well-acquainted with @[The Dwarrow](settlement:fa91fd8a-f74e-409d-a703-26a9b8e09954), and knows of both the @[Brotherhood of the Broken Blade](organization:4a287a6e-7bd4-4721-9333-79ee98681350), and the planned expedition by @[A. Gori Greataxe](person:e45f77bd-aace-4c5f-bf40-811011d61b14) (see @[The Dwarrow](settlement:fa91fd8a-f74e-409d-a703-26a9b8e09954), Scenarios).

articles.title: Damon N. Pythias
articles.content:
Damon is a short, skinny man with hair that can't seem to make up its mind. In a line down the center, and around his ears, Damon's hair is very thick and full. In between these two strips, however, there isn't any hair at all. The combination is weird, and presents an interesting addition to this thoroughly disgusting man, 

 Damon, for a living, sells things. He has, in his lifetime, sold Scollian Strip Scales, Phantastic Phantasmal Phizz, Ollander's Awful Owls, etc. At present, he is now selling a concoction of his own: Damon's Dastardly Drops, a proposed cure-all for sight, hearing, and office related ailments. To coin a phrase: “it’s all a crock of bull.” 

 Several years ago, Damon acquired a dozen small bottles which he "found" in a "deserted, empty house". These bottles, although Damon doesn't know it, are magical, and will double the power of any magical liquid put into it (i.e. a healing potion heals double the normal amount; a poison is twice as powerful; etc.)

articles.title: Daniel Moloxinizasky
articles.content: Owns @[The Crocked Constable](landmark:41a1be96-7b91-4a0f-83c4-adde2fdca6b9), an inn and tavern

articles.title: Dannel
articles.content: A small, slim young man, with brownish hair and odd golden eyes, who works as a stable hand for one of the rental stables; he is superb with horses, possessing a skill surpassing that of Heidel. To date, none of the major dealers or trainers have noticed the boy, but word is starting to spread of his ability. Dannel would be a superb trainer, at least as good as a centaur, and he has the eye to pick good horseflesh; he spends a good bit of his time on Wednesdays and Saturdays near @[The Auction Block](landmark:67b5d2df-9421-4945-8139-69de4d5ec4da), and will happily describe the points of the various horses up to anyone who asks or takes the trouble to listen.

articles.title: Daquis Reeve
articles.content: A small, dark fellow with black eyes and a thoughtful manner, Reeve is an information broker, a risky business in this part of town. He employs a number of people to keep him informed of doings around town, and will often personally check out a particularly interesting lead. He will both buy Information from reliable sources (no tieflings, please) and take "commissions" for researching a particular subject or person. Daquis is careful, methodical, and a reasonably reliable source of information; he is also a good businessman, and prices his information according to how valuable it is to the prospective buyer. He can be found in several taverns around @[The Labyrinth](settlement:e05f9a94-a44d-4991-b419-28cae89db0ee) in the afternoons, such as @[The Hearth and Hound](landmark:225a529d-f3ae-496a-81bc-7f698f8adcd4), or @[The Silver Penny](landmark:de34a211-1b72-4561-b5a0-2908200ef8c4); he does not stay in @[The Labyrinth](settlement:e05f9a94-a44d-4991-b419-28cae89db0ee) after dark.

articles.title: Daran Tiko
articles.content: Runs a second hand furniture stall in the @[Thieves' Market](settlement:8b3bf96f-ea9a-4e39-8c3f-bda804df5cdb)

articles.title: Darankis t'Goran
articles.content:
A slender, dark-haired, dark-complexioned man of later years. He is a prominent horse trader, maintaining large sets of stables in the @[Horse Market](settlement:3987cb08-4abd-4e55-a582-128df2ff71db); his stables are the only ones capable of giving the Varrasches a run for the title of biggest dealer. 

 Darankis gets his horses from the herds of the Golden Plateau, by trading with the nomads, breaking and training them in Haven; his charges for draining are comparable with most of the other trainers (350-600gp).

locations.title: Stables and Pens of Darankis t'Goran

articles.title: Darius
articles.content:
A tall, blonde and bearded centaur; he pulls a cart with several large barrels with spigots on it; a painted sign on both sides of the wagon proclaims: Wine and Ale - Cold and Refreshing! 1sp per cup. Those who wish to partake of this mobile beverage fountain must provide their own cups, however; and Darius is not gentle with those who try to drink without paying, 

 Darius samples generously of his own wares, and is far less observant of drink-filchers by late afternoon. He does not stay in one place, but slowly travels the Loop around the Island all day long. The barrels are kept cool in the hottest weather magically.
