articles.title: Daruko Ken-Ursa
articles.content:
A slender man of middle years, with grizzled hair bound with an ornate leather headband bearing a single opal. He wears usual gypsy raiment, but includes a long flowing blue velvet cape, and an authoritative air, 

 Daruko is the leader of the tribe of the @[Wandering Folk](ethnicity:24b9b845-e6f9-43c3-81c7-acae85db7481) presently on @[Trade Island](settlement:eec2fc60-5565-40fa-9047-69924589c400). He is a dominating, magnetic individual whose people follow him with great loyalty; the fortunes of the tribe have prospered under his strict leadership, 

 Daruko is a firm believer in everyone working hard and making sacrifices for the good of the tribe. 

 @[Dzarina](person:6f02edd2-cbdc-4025-b7ac-f76406316154)'s singing is part of her contribution to the tribe since she is not good at anything useful, and he is quick to point out her faults, in hopes that the humiliation might spur her on to improve. But, he is also quick to hide her if he hears the Entertainer's Guild is seeking her, for he is well aware that she is performing illegally under Haven's laws, 

 Daruko is not above a bit of petty larceny on strangers, but will not bother the @[Trade Island](settlement:eec2fc60-5565-40fa-9047-69924589c400) regulars.

articles.title: Darvi arn Malakki
articles.content: A bespectacled dwarf of middle years with bright blue eyes and a cheery voice married to @[Meekin arn Malakki](person:fe51898a-e94e-4b00-b82d-fc379c6b3371). Darvi is more than a seller of books and maps -  he is a trained scholar and historian and can read over a dozen languages, both contemporary and ancient. He is also a student of myth and legend and has an 85% chance of having some information on a given topic if it concerns dwarves or dwarvish history, with a 45% chance on non-dwarvish topics.

articles.title: Dash
articles.content: See scenario @[The South Keep Gang](plot:652ff4d1-71f3-44ac-9ac1-57e1b1f881c8)

articles.title: Dauge Hofstra
articles.content:
Dauge and his identical twin @[Charlie](person:2a76cfbd-2b71-47b8-b505-c9cad32e55af) are identical twins. They are tall, heavily built, with black hair and dark eyes, and even seem to think alike. Both are outdoorsmen, and are quite likely (and happy for the opportunity) to take to the road as couriers for the family business on very short notice, not to return for two or three weeks. They are in the process of arranging remount stations, coach stops, and contracts for light freighting in the @[Ten Cities](organization:0efc56fc-301e-4d3f-ba8c-019da1b01590), hoping to provide competition for Messers Welshe and Fargot. 

 Neither is married, but they are currently sharing quarters with identical twin girls (the confusion must be incredible - who sleeps with whom?). [br][br] [familytree:985abb36-bd46-4191-a8d9-aaf0a14bade2] [br]

articles.title: Dewleaf
articles.content: @[Silverthorne](person:6314ff3e-fadd-42ba-aa6c-bf26fc2767bc) has a small band of loyal followers, who have sworn to defend him and his interests, and to help him regain his throne. Dewleaf is  skilled with the bow. All are staying at @[The Mallorn](landmark:11a61b6d-c93a-47c0-b483-46c0dcf8996d), and may be encountered at various places throughout the city.

articles.title: Deza
articles.content: An 18-year old half-orc girl who has been taken in by Master @[Nimoyin](person:c30e6ac0-4f3f-49cb-9b90-20d2919ada2e). She has been a source of consternation among the elves of @[The Cauldron](settlement:983c8fa2-3df5-46b0-91fb-3dbe004450da) and despite her obviously talented mind, she is less than welcome even at the multi-racial University. There are even dark rumors (false) among the students that her position with Master @[Nimoyin](person:c30e6ac0-4f3f-49cb-9b90-20d2919ada2e) has been obtained through intimate favors.

articles.title: Dickens
articles.content:
Common thief. 

 A hulk of a man, with an unshaven face and dark, brooding eyes, Dickens is sullen and dangerous. Muggings and armed robbery are his favored styles, with his trusty blackjack or a wicked long- bladed dagger. He has also done some burglary, using a captured street rat to slip inside to unlock the doors. Dickens is a brutal man, a cold-hearted bully, mistreating even his mistress, who is surprisingly devoted to him.

articles.title: Dinana
articles.content: See Street Encounter: Wedding Celebration

articles.title: Dingo Proudbottom
articles.content:
Dingo is a traveler and scholar of the Tabled cultures far to the east of the city, who makes his living by dealing in spices and rare volumes that he brings back from his travels. @[Bucklander's Import Emporium](landmark:3737ee0a-7d2a-4738-a381-a8c05cd128e1) is a major customer for these products. 

He is very lean for a halfling, and tends to dress in exotic, bright-colored silken robes. Dingo is extremely pacifistic in nature, and will not take life even in self-defense; he is protected on his travels by [ul] [li]1) a silver bracelet that contains a permanent 12 point Missile Repulsor spell, and[/li] [li] 2) his training in judo (in close combat, he has a 25% + (5 x (18 - opponent's CO rating)) chance of throwing any human or smaller sized foe in his grasp to the ground - if successful, the opponent must make a CON saving roll or be stunned for 1d6 melee round).[/li] [/ul] 

Dingo is only in the city about 25% of the time. When he is gone, his housekeeper Sobelia lives in and maintains his home in @[The Dell](settlement:e8aa9d8f-68be-4d89-9e11-6ba288e71515) which is a cornucopia filled with artifacts, books and maps from his wanderings. The biggest thing protecting his smial from robbers is the fact that most of his neighbors consider his collection to be junk.

articles.title: Div
articles.content: Works for @[Lazar Symbocca](person:2c51d376-29e2-4868-ac54-050e58f8c59c) at @[Sym's Storage Company](landmark:950bc2b9-c121-4be6-a597-f3373ed455b0). He is a Black Hand member but doesn't know the full extent of Lazar's business.

articles.title: Doc
articles.content:
See scenario @[The Stoned Maiden](plot:6a3785ed-a090-42aa-949e-da36d73d4b1e) 

 A two-bit operator within the Thieves guild

articles.title: Dog-end
articles.content: Dog-end (Jethro Tull reference) is an old man who lives on the streets. He can be seen either wandering lonely taking time the only way he knows or sitting near parks or other places where children play. He has long, grey, filthy hair, snot running down his nose and greasy fingers smearing shabby clothes. Essentially harmless, Dog-end is just one of those people who just fell through the cracks of society and gets by somehow. For the most part people ignore him and this constant muttering but from time to time his appearance causes alarm in the more upstanding Haven residents. Normally found in @[The Labyrinth](settlement:e05f9a94-a44d-4991-b419-28cae89db0ee), he will from time to time be found wandering the streets and parks in @[The South Corridor](settlement:d684e9e8-9b69-45fc-8352-3de0e6e7f870).  Around meal times he if often found at one of the Crotofiran Missions

articles.title: Dolby Spreeker
articles.content: A gregarious, well-loved fellow with a heart of gold, always willing to lend a sympathetic ear to a patron's problems. He keeps undesirable elements out of his establishment, however, with an iron hand, and is a deadly accurate artist with a knife if pushed to violence.

articles.title: Donia Savonna
articles.content:
Quiet, very plain girl in her late teens; she is very nervous around men and stutters heavily in their presence. Years of perpetual browbeating from her strong-willed mother - @[Margery Savonna](person:932609a3-02d8-4138-a3a1-0fab988a932e) - has badly undermined her self-confidence. 

She is well-versed in household skills, especially weaving (she makes fine rugs, and all her own clothing). Donia has burning artistic desires that she keeps secret from Margery and hides a sketch pad in her room. She draws the scenes she sees from her window  showing reasonable talent given her total absence of formal training. 

Donia is desperate for real affection from others, but too terrified to seek it out; a kind word or gesture from another would make that person an immediate friend.

articles.title: Dragontooth
articles.content:
General alley basher/legbreakers/other muscle.

 A psychopathic killer 10% of the time, otherwise a normal thug. Uncontrollable once in a state except by magic. Dragontooth once served a mage who knew his problem and kept it under control except when it suited his purpose. 

 Dragontooth is particularly susceptible to SLEEP and CHARM spells, and saves against them at a penalty of 6.

articles.title: Dunstan Herlihea
articles.content: Dunstan Herlihea is of average height, slender, red-haired, and black eyed. He makes most of the pipes available in his shop, carving them from seasoned briar, blackthorn, or cherry, sandstone, soapstone, or corn-cobs. His wife is names Colleen.

articles.title: Duumin
articles.content: A metalsmith whose works are decorative and ceremonial, not functional. He works primarily on goblets, bowls, and small statuary, and always uses gold as his medium.

articles.title: Dzarina
articles.content:
A slender girl of 15, with wide dark eyes and curly black hair caught up in a red kerchief. She wears a colorful assortment of garments, numerous bangles, and gold hoop earrings; she wears a knife at her belt, and sometimes carries an old, well-worn guitar, 

 Dzarina is blessed with a beautiful, lyrical voice, and frequently sings for donations from the audience. She also has two left hands (and feet) as far as moving gracefully, is afraid of horses, and is prone to trip over her own feet, but her fingers are deft and sure on the strings of the guitar, 

 Dzarina is not well treated by her father, who appropriates all the coins her musical talents bring in, and berates her for her clumsiness and lack of domestic skills. But, like most of the @[Wandering Folk](ethnicity:24b9b845-e6f9-43c3-81c7-acae85db7481), Dzarina distrusts the non gypsies, and will not readily leave the life she knows for the stifling houses of the city. She is also very close to her younger sister Anhilde and doesn't want to leave her, 

 Dzarina is watched by the hopeful young men of the tribe; if a stranger engages her in conversation for any length of time, they will not interfere, but there is a 60% chance one will report it to Daruko.

articles.title: Ea
articles.content:
Ea rules the air and is popular with the @[Avanthari](ethnicity:10367593-b9d9-4dca-94f3-7f44bf047ebb) who believe that the Deva from which they are descended were sent by Ea. Sailors are also known to prey to Ea in addition to @[Nenya](person:928a98b6-5cca-47d7-82cc-78f092e55d65) when hoping for steady winds to speed them along.

Her worshipers are the ultimate free spirits. They believe that it is improper to allow oneself to be tied down for any length of time. They are always seeking new adventures and new journeys. It is said that she is the favorite of Ladros, because she is the one who goes off to gather new knowledge, always to return. It is this love of adventure that led people to offer a prayer or other devotion before setting out on a journey - and hence become the patron of travellers.

Her followers love to climb and explore as high places as they can, if nothing else than to see the horizon. They are also known to be excellent mapmakers. 

Ea gave no gift to the races of man, choosing instead to be an inspiration for their own greatness.

Her holy symbol is a compass rose, with a blank circle in the middle. It is customary for her worshipers to fill this circle with a symbol that has personal meaning to them.
articles.honorific: Goddess of the Air, Patron of Travellers

articles.title: Eaglewing Longeye
articles.content:
A slight, grey haired avanthar of many years’ experience in the caravan trade. Wing (as he is usually called) tends to frequent the northern route on the expeditions he organizes, and has many business connections. Occasionally he will guide a caravan to the east onto the Golden Plateau, a large and very rich region populated by bands of roving nomads.  

 He captains caravans from Haven, but maintains only a sleeping space there in the home of one of the other avanthari; his family resides in the crags and cliffs of the White Wing Mountains near Seki, southeast of Haven. Wing will fly home whenever he has sufficient free time to warrant the trip. 

 Usually, Wing leaves the actual organizing of the caravans (mostly horseback) to his assistant, a centaur named @[Turikonis Plainsrunner](person:8a30d8ab-d420-405f-bae6-50e431305294) (#1716), who does the majority of the hiring. Current plans call for the pair to leave within a week on their next venture.

articles.content: Starseeker's captain, Earnil is a tall elf with pale hair and sea-green eyes.

articles.content: A petite, vivacious brunette with blue eyes and a luscious figure. She is totally devoted to husband @[Zalle Rand](person:25c3009e-ebca-4784-a006-a813e43739ee), but does like to enjoy herself with a lot of people. She frequently talks Zalle into "going out for the evening? Please, I've been stuck in this stuffy old house all day." He's putty in her soft little hands. articles.content: A typical elf physically, medium tall, slender, brownish hair, brown eyes. His idealism rating is 10 where elves are concerned. He tends to frequent @[The Hanged Man](landmark:6f703365-4d51-4c2c-ae5a-201bff349ce2) (65%), but may occasionally be found at @[The Lying Lawyer](landmark:0f5a29ce-4b27-422f-a557-e53239d964d0) (30%).

articles.title: Eldri
articles.content: A talented, expert fighter who is qualified to teach any axe or hammer weapon, as well as the bastard and broadsword. Eldri can also train fighters in the use of battle-axe or war hammer up to expert level in these weapons after three months of extensive sessions, these sessions are only available to dwarves.

articles.title: Electra
articles.content: Electra is the subject of the scenario @[Rescue by Moonlight](plot:5bdba0a4-107c-439e-8816-fa4cddbeaab9).  She is a lovely girl of average height, with long red hair with a pronounced streak of silver (a very rare hair combination in Haven)

articles.title: Elegrin Herundor
articles.content: Handles "real estate" transactions for the folk of the trees (although land in @[Erinhir](settlement:96d2680b-e669-4c07-ba6b-f4727fb8d9d9) is never actually bought or sold, he advises his people in their choices of living space). Non-elves are simply told there is none available.

articles.title: Elias Pennywhistle
articles.content: Elias is the part-owner of one of @[The Dell](settlement:e8aa9d8f-68be-4d89-9e11-6ba288e71515)'s fresh produce stands. A fervent Royalist, he uniformly blames the Guild government for all the city's current problems. Possesses excellent hearing, and a very good sense of smell, and is an astute observer of passersby.

articles.title: Elias Thornapple
articles.content:
Also known as "Roundbottom", he is a middle-aged halfling of considerable girth; a jester by trade. Makes his living by playing the country simpleton; he is sharper of wit than ha appears, and acts as an agent for the @[Thieves' Guild](organization:08dce3b2-80f7-468b-be7b-dd5fdbfac799). 

 A good-natured fellow who loves a good pipe and a good joke (Shaggy dog variety). Has not been a practicing thief for some time (he doesn't fit into windows very well any more). He knows Haven very well, and would tag along for an "adventure", playing the bumpkin until he can take the loot and disappear, unless one of the party is also in the @[Thieves' Guild](organization:08dce3b2-80f7-468b-be7b-dd5fdbfac799). 

 Most folk consider Elias a silly old halfling, and he likes it that way. Well known and respected by the elder generation on @[The Street of Harps](settlement:6053011d-37a6-4d6b-8e0b-41925f3bbd77) for his talent and drive, but the younger bards believe he is too subservient to the whims of his patron, Duke Fernando di Cottilion.

articles.title: Ellian
articles.content: The only woman among the High Judges, Ellian (#216) was chosen because she was a living example of what is good in the study of the Philosophical Way. She is in her middle thirties, with mid-length brown hair, green eyes, and a reasonable figure (Tut! Tut! She's a judge.). Ellian has never married, but has a relationship with Herven (no secret about it, their affair is common knowledge in Haven) which they have maintained for over a decade. She strives to be as fair in the courtroom as possible, but has her occasional slips into mild bigotry (as with Meron, the half-orc - but then, who wouldn't?). Ellian despises Cardallo, and feels ashamed that early in her career she almost succumbed to his wiles.

articles.content: Works at his brother @[Varkin Jelas](person:7a7cdc39-e8ed-4807-b4b7-907a54be3146)' tavern, The Silber Penny. Hi is a tough thug and can sling ale or patrons as necessary

articles.title: Elsbeth Windermere
articles.content:
Elsbeth Windermere has served as Haven's mayor for the past decade, showing the city her prowess as a competent and steadfast leader. Before stepping into the political arena, she was a successful merchant who had a keen eye for opportunities and a strong business acumen. Her firm but fair trade policies earned her the respect of both guilders and nobles and, eventually, the financial means to influence Haven politics.

As a leader, Mayor Windermere has always prioritized the safety and prosperity of Haven above all else. She is a strong advocate for industrial and economic development, but not at the cost of her people's welfare. She has a reputation for being pragmatic and determined. While she's far from an adventurer herself, she's not above recruiting others to tackle whatever is required.

She can usually be found in her private office in the @[Mayor's Palace](landmark:c0ab8179-cf4b-415f-b825-6c2535ae893b) from 10:00am to about 7:00pm, or in the Council Chambers whenever they are in session, usually explaining why she had something done or spent city funds on a particular project. She is not required to seek Council permission to do her job or to spend money, but the Council does have the right to remove her from office at any time. 

She has appointed all of the current Ministers to their positions; for most of these jobs, she succeeded in choosing people of her own stripe, but she did not pick all angels - one devil snuck in.

As mayor, Windermere is more likely to engage in social encounters rather than combat. Use her high Charisma and Persuasion skills to reflect her diplomatic experience and her ability to rally her people in times of crisis. She's a natural leader and a shrewd politician, always aiming to secure the best outcome for her city and its people.
articles.motivation: For the good of the city and its inhabitants

articles.title: Elsi Klukoo
articles.content: Elsi is a rather elderly but spry woman who makes pocket watches and large clocks.

articles.title: Emel d'Lormai
articles.content:
A tall, lean man with silver hair, handsome, rugged features and the slightly slanted eyes and brows of his Elvish kindred; he wears a well-made tunic and breeches of Elvish fashion, and a grey cloak. Emel and his elvish wife Mordaina have been plying the spice trade for nearly three decades, traveling the Long Road and the river. But when in Haven, on the Island, they have a home, for they always camp on the same spot, which is quickly vacated should it be occupied when Emel rides in, 

 Emel is well known among the @[Free Traders](organization:49945ba5-c9eb-4451-8ac9-773ea36d3c92) as a fair and honest man, who owes no favors to the Guilds or to any individuals. Emel is trusted as an arbitrator of petty disputes, a source of sound advice, and wise counsel, 

 Emel and Mordaina have been endeavoring for the past few years to organize the @[Free Traders](organization:49945ba5-c9eb-4451-8ac9-773ea36d3c92) so that they might be a more effective economic force, but so far, the traders are too fiercely jealous of their independence to co-operate on anything but short-term agreements. They will talk to traders at night on the Island, advocating their new idea, and adjudicating disputes.

articles.content: Captain Emilio di Cordoba of the Pavanne is an enterprising fellow who never overlooks a possibly profitable deal, despite its legality. He is also one of the few captains that keeps a ship's mage (Cimeron) though he doesn't really trust him.

articles.title: Enos the Maul
articles.content: A solid man, a granite block in human guise, who wields a 9-pound maul as if it was a flyswatter. He is usually up at dawn, working in his livery stable near the Judgement Gate. A forthright, upright, righteous man, he will aid anyone who is in trouble (physical, not financial).

articles.title: Enver
articles.content:
Chief wrangler for the Varrasches; tall and lanky, he sports an curving scar on one cheek where he was kicked by a horse as a youth. He is a friendly fellow, and is quite willing to teach the skills of riding and wrangling to those with whom he works. Enver is probably the best man with a whip or lariat in the Market or for several hundred miles around. 

 His name advertises the fact that no one has ever seen him fly off a horse, regardless of the animal's antics - he sticks like a burr, with or without saddle. 

 Enver will be the trail boss for the Varrasch brothers' expedition to the Golden Plateau and he will tell interested parties about the particulars. He will inform those that strike him as good material for a drive (saving roll against CHA) that an air of confidence is the best way to get a job with Heidel. 

 The wrangler can usually be found in the vicinity of @[The Auction Block](landmark:67b5d2df-9421-4945-8139-69de4d5ec4da) or the Varrasch stables. 

See also scenario @[Varrasch’s Expedition](plot:23ea9e01-debb-4055-89b1-05d6630ee5c0).

articles.title: Ephi
articles.content:
Ephi has lived among the patrons at The @[Rose Garden Inn](landmark:d657f21f-881e-4050-bf0b-e5bc103ac61a) longer than she can remember. After turning herself invisible one day, she followed a carriage through the main gate, and its company through the main doors. From that point forward, she has magically disguised herself by altering her appearance into a near-carbon copy of the inn’s guests—or more specifically, their children. Occasionally she will take on the appearance of a chaste human female in search of courtship and dazzle in the ballroom; at others that of a distinguished gentleman so as to lounge in the smoking room. 

Hers is a genuine, insatiable thirst for innocent mischief. She particularly enjoys confounding guests to the point of utter bewilderment.

articles.title: er-Keng Varrasch
articles.content:
er-Keng loved both Branden and Valken at different times during her youth, and the relationship between the three after her marriage to Brandon has always seemed ambiguous to those outside the immediate family (and served as the source of many a juicy rumor over the years). 

 er-Keng has tried to subtly inform the younger brothers of their elder's discontentment, but has so far been unsuccessful (an unsurprising result, given that Heidel and Kronen seldom notice anything more subtle than a 2 by 4, "upside the head”). articles.title: Erin O'Shea
articles.content: A lovely young woman completely devoted to Kelly O-Shea whom she recently married. She also an excellent harpist and often demonstrates her husband's wares.

articles.title: Ernie
articles.content:
Common thief. 

 Forming a Laurel and Hardy team with brother @[Mugs](person:a10a5716-43ed-4ece-be52-cfb83e10429b), these brothers work together on armed robberies and burglaries. Ernie is small and wiry, and provides the brains of the operation, while slow-witted @[Mugs](person:a10a5716-43ed-4ece-be52-cfb83e10429b) provides the muscle. Unfortunately, with only one brain between them, their success rate is not high; Ernie's plans start out logically but often go awry due to later elaborate embellishments, while @[Mugs](person:a10a5716-43ed-4ece-be52-cfb83e10429b) can remember only the simplest of instructions and is apt to falter in or bungle the job assigned to him.

articles.title: Esgar
articles.content: Works for @[Lazar Symbocca](person:2c51d376-29e2-4868-ac54-050e58f8c59c) at @[Sym's Storage Company](landmark:950bc2b9-c121-4be6-a597-f3373ed455b0). He is a Black Hand member but doesn't know the full extent of Lazar's business.

articles.content: A ruthless man, who is also a Black Hand agent and captain of Dark of the Moon.

articles.title: Etheah
articles.content: The rites are simple and gentle: to the accompaniment of the sweet music of a harp, the congregation thanks Etheah for her gifts that makes life worth living. Most of the sacrifices celebrate life and living (such as planting a tree or a flower, releasing doves, etc.).

articles.title: Eugene the Elf
articles.content: You'll only mis-pronounce my elvish name

articles.title: Evan Monier
articles.content:
A tall, ruggedly handsome sort of fellow with a bushy chestnut beard and sparkling black eyes, Monier is a Guild member of long good standing. He is a valuable cog in the organization despite his own modest thieving abilities, due to his talents as a courier and his contacts among the city's many mercenary groups. 

 Evan has served as an officer, in the companies of both Halidar the Bold and Donelek of Petiz, and has good friends in several units. He is a rough and tumble fellow who likes his carousing and pursues the good life with vigor, but is all business when the situation depends upon it. 

 If he has a weakness, it is his tendency to deal with all problems in a straightforward manner (i.e., by physically eliminating anyone who is perceived as being part of the cause).

articles.title: Fagin Childstealer
articles.content: Fagin, a wiry old half-elf with wild eyes, has set up a thriving business in child labor, capturing "street rats" in the twisting alleyways and dark corners of @[The Labyrinth](settlement:e05f9a94-a44d-4991-b419-28cae89db0ee). The ragged children, along with the occasional careless tiefling, are starved and beaten into submission, and sold for slave (indenture) labor in the workhouses of @[The Labyrinth](settlement:e05f9a94-a44d-4991-b419-28cae89db0ee) or @[The Commons](settlement:8ff1c19a-c29d-4050-9c7c-7200f23453be)

articles.title: Falstaff of Borrinstorr
articles.content:
A portly, extravagantly outfitted nobleman in his late forties, with a receding hairline and bushy mutton chop sideburns. He is usually dressed in a tunic of crimson or royal blue velvet, adorned with ruffles, gold piping, and an abundance of medals and insignia, most of which have been purchased just for the sake of appearance. 

Falstaff is an avid gambler and a prodigious liar who constantly tells fanciful tales of his fighting exploits - unfortunately, his facts are so garbled that anyone with even a smattering of knowledge about military history will see right through these tales. If caught in a lie, he will first try to bluster his way out of difficulty, and then meekly admit his mistake, playing on the sympathy of the crowd by confessing he "is an old warrior, whose memory is not what it once was". Within five minutes, he will be back at it again, undaunted by his experience. Indeed, Falstaff's family did sire many heroic warriors, and Falstaff for his part did serve long (albeit not particularly well) in the armies of the @[Ten Cities](organization:0efc56fc-301e-4d3f-ba8c-019da1b01590). 

 Though married twice for brief periods, Falstaff never was able to sire a heir, a fact that causes him great regret. He keeps a watch out for a young man "of character" without family ties, who might serve as his surrogate son and heir. The candidate need not be a noble, but must have demonstrated a taste for the finer things in life. 

 His best friend is Sir @[Rodney of Shaftesbury](person:7fe0e7da-e0bb-492b-afa7-217a058194db).

articles.title: Fandril C. Cloess
articles.content: Fandril is known around @[The Heights](settlement:1f0571c0-b8de-4b50-b010-5529cab6603b) as a quality tailor who produces good, well-fitting clothing, whose styles are conservative rather than trendy high fashion. This reputation is justifiable as Fandril and his assistants are very competent craftsmen.

articles.title: Farris
articles.content: The chief scribe at Bennichio's hop, Frarris usually oversees the work and keeps the rowdy apprentices and journeymen under control and productive. Farris is not above boxing a boy's ears for careless scribing or avoidable errors.

articles.title: Fenris Redbeard
articles.content:
A tall, burly man with thick red hair and beard. An experienced showman, he has lived most of his life on the road. Fenris is a shrewd money manager, a better than average playwright and lyricist, and capable of making his voice heard clear to the back row of any crowd. 

 Fenris is one of many in the "carney" trade who chafes at the restrictions placed upon him by the @[Guild of Entertainers](organization:f4889184-3aed-47bb-b7cb-0beeec445e22). Since he is a magnetic leader, the Guild is relieved to see him go on his yearly trek. 

 Fenris' first responsibility is to the safety of his troupe (Redbeard’s Repertory Players), and is quite likely to leave the player characters to fight while he gets the non-combatants out of danger (that is why he hired guards, after all), but he can wield a sword and will fight if pressed.

articles.title: Fernando di Cotillion
articles.content: Current, nominal ruler of Haven. Real power lies with Council of Boroughs (sort of) and really with the guilds, or more specifically, the five "great guilds".

articles.title: Fernando Garo
articles.content: Provides decent barbering, non-slip shanve and leaves your ears and throat intact.

articles.title: Fernlace
articles.content:
Fernlace is the top Herbalist in Haven; there is scarcely a plant she doesn't know and she can work wondrous things using them.  She can force-grow seedlings into mature plants overnight, shrink a very large tree down to its original seed in 72 hours, use the correct application of herbs to speed healing, draw up water from underground for drinking or filling moats.  She has written three Herbalism texts and 29 commentaries.

She appears ageless and in in fact a prophet of the goddess @[Etheah](person:da6b1939-060c-4f36-8da6-8d4be3b07cf0), which is where her powers originate.

articles.title: Ferrus Ironfist
articles.content: A grizzled dwarf of later years, is a retired warrior turned merchant. He specializes in importing items of dwarvish make, particularly from the inventive ironsmiths of Darnaiga, a city in the Khuz Mountains.

articles.title: Fertik
articles.content: Fertik has worked with @[Valli](person:34c3d4c1-63aa-40e4-84f3-ce75cdb96fee) for 22 years, and is very loyal to his employer. Knowing the seriousness of @[Valli](person:34c3d4c1-63aa-40e4-84f3-ce75cdb96fee)'s plight, Fertik has thought about the situation and concluded that the only way to save @[Valli](person:34c3d4c1-63aa-40e4-84f3-ce75cdb96fee)'s shop would be to kidnap @[Konig](person:e6dc3031-c63d-4249-8ccb-6a6d3d61fc97) and somehow convince him of the error of his ways. Fertik has talked to the Thieves Guild about this, but they categorically refused to take on such a job and he is now discreetly looking for an independent band of rogues that might be willing to perform the deed.

articles.title: Fessor del Cappo
articles.content: Random entertainer to be user as necessary

articles.title: Fingers Arthas
articles.content:
A short and relatively chubby (when on duty) half-orc. Arthas is a 5th Level thief, and has fair abilities: 62% pickpocketing, 38% moving silently, and 45% hiding in cover. He is capable of stretching and/or compressing the disks in his spine, almost at will (it takes about 30 seconds), and can change his height by as much as 6", from 5'2" to 5'8". He has used this ability to escape identification many times and the constables are firmly convinced that he has a twin (taller or shorter, as the case may be) who has committed an incredible number of purse cuttings and pocket pickings (albeit clumsily) and gotten away with all of them. 

 He is a fair lock pick (specializing in Cylinder and Pin locks, 68%) as well, and can be hired for various jobs through the Guild. 

 Fingers can be found in the Market throughout the day, and maintains a small flat not far away, on the edge of @[The Labyrinth](settlement:e05f9a94-a44d-4991-b419-28cae89db0ee). When not out in the square, Arthas can usually be found at either @[The Knighte Oute](landmark:9c8b1af3-8ee0-4161-a334-ceabc6b04d34) or @[The Silver Stringed Bouzouki](landmark:176d8619-120b-473b-9a40-cf0cdc04eaa9).

articles.title: Firlirrel Ilorim
articles.content:
Firlirrel, who is presently accounted as one of the five finest voices in Haven, arrived only some 120 years ago. After making a great impression on the Entertainers' Guild with his superb voice (as well as on the elves), he wooed, won, and married Lachoriel, a beautiful elfin maid of Londhin, a minor family in @[Erinhir](settlement:96d2680b-e669-4c07-ba6b-f4727fb8d9d9), and produced a daughter, Adrielle. 

 Firlirrel is still a power in the various ramifications of @[The Street of Harps](settlement:6053011d-37a6-4d6b-8e0b-41925f3bbd77), but seldom performs now, other than on special occasions. He is engaged in writing a history of the elvish peoples, and devotes most of his time to that project. [br][br] [familytree:b6f4ea90-5699-457a-bbd3-4c56917306cf] [br]

articles.title: Florina
articles.content: An Elven woman with violet eyes and hair of jet. She is one of the most beautiful women in the city, but her snobbish, and childish behavior creates numerous problems for her. She plays, but does not make, her flutes.

articles.title: Folonar Fairweather
articles.content: Folonar, a leatherworker, is half-elven, and a smooth talker. He always tries to convince his customer's to purchase more equipment, or a more elaborate version of whatever they want. Business partner to Gibbon Garranzano.

articles.title: Forindoc Bucket
articles.content: Waiter, cook and clean-up crew at @[The Leaf and Jar](landmark:275162bf-bd5f-4fc0-a2b8-79b45a5945cd), Furry is Laurel to his bosses Hardy. He is extrordinarily thin and tall for a halfling.  He is somewhat slow-witted, and has almost no hair on his feet or hands (resulting in his nickname).  He is occasionally the butt of practical jokes, but most of the patrons like the lad because of his eagerness to please. His two loves in life are whittling and his vegetable garden, which he tends with great care.

articles.title: Forti
articles.content: A formet wildcat prospector, Forti convinced his partner @[Ninar Goldrush](person:a15e3e21-667f-42d1-87d7-d6aeba64aca3) to abandon the miner's life for the "greater security" of owning this shop, which sells all manner of prospecting supplies.

articles.title: Foxcraft Q. Pennywhistle
articles.content:
General alley basher/legbreakers/other muscle.

 Sometimes, alley bashers are made, not born. Foxy's mom wanted him to be something dignified, like an artisan or barrister - she had no idea that her son would grow up to look like the entire Green Bay Packer front four. The taunts of his childhood, and the fights that followed hardened him into a sullen man. Foxcraft never trusts anybody, and seemingly small disagreements will set him off with a vengeance. If you like working with a time bomb, here's your boy.

articles.title: Francesca Maggia
articles.content: Recently deceased head of the @[Maggia Family](organization:7157ba84-27ce-44ee-998e-007b1b0b58fa). She leaves behind a large and somewhat fractured family. @[Gilberto Maggia](person:f8abcaf4-8f94-42f6-84ea-94c3c8c1b1a4) has assumed the family leadership role. [br][br] [familytree:a9232402-5b98-4e76-a3be-cfc0177ddaa3] [br]

articles.title: Freggo the Hairless
articles.content:
Freggo, the Minister of Ports and Shipping, is greedy and corrupt, and is widely (but unofficially) known to have his hand out for whatever baksheesh (bribe money) or graft he can weasel out of the captains and ship owners of the city. Unfortunately, he is clever, and seems to have a sixth sense that has enabled him to appear completely honest when an attempt has been made to catch him in the act. 

 Freggo is short, pale, and pasty, with piggy little dark eyes, and is totally hairless; his handshake feels like one has grasped an unbaked bagel. 

 He has accumulated enough graft money to buy himself an estate far up the river near Mandalai, and is beginning to fee, that it may be time to "resign" his post, and "retire" from the active public life. 

 One of his clerks has managed to locate and secrete a fund of information on his various activities which, if revealed, would probably lead to a swift execution following an equally swift trial - both Freggo and the @[Young Stallions](organization:7340b23d-2c0c-45fd-8222-13b00aa2760c) are searching for this clerk (see Adventure Opportunities - North Corridor), who seems to have recently thoroughly lost himself somewhere in the city.

articles.title: G. Maximus
articles.content:
The huge, obese, pig-eyed owner of @[The Black Whip](landmark:6f66e600-9089-49a6-b9dc-7e4dd9febe5c), a house of pleasure on @[The Street of Silk Veils](settlement:587a7a3a-ba45-4bfd-94bc-fe6e17ae023c) which caters to those who enjoy any of a variety of strange and bizarre fetishes.

Maximus lives at his somewhat disreputable establishment, and controls three cells in @[Angelina's Guild](organization:06d842f7-8aee-4ab6-ab5e-457cc1d9484d) containing some dozen men. One group consists of the three or four thugs in his employ, another of the uniquely trained staff of the Whip, and the third a group of four men who handle Black Hand involvement in the Haven slave trade - the leader of these men, Angus McFarland, is @[Adrielle Ilorim](person:5d239bee-e2a5-4952-b7ad-412596ca7c50)'s contact in @[Erinhir](settlement:96d2680b-e669-4c07-ba6b-f4727fb8d9d9). 

Maximus himself is as venal and loathsome as the activities he directs, and is well satisfied with his grimy little niche in the overall @[The Black Hand](organization:d1a96263-4191-482e-ace6-360d25106f60) power structure. There are few things beneath him, and it is rumored that he partakes liberally of the services offered by his establishment.

articles.title: Gabrielle de Kammeron
articles.content: Gabrielle is the beautiful daughter of a perfumer, Broutier. Along with he husband, Swayze, she has a love for the outdoor life, and they have journeyed together to many exotic climes. [br][br] [familytree:9b60f9bc-dd18-4f0e-9c45-17ad9d87f68b] [br]

articles.title: Galeana
articles.content:
A graceful Sindarin woman of middle years. She is frequently called in as an impartial arbitrator in neighborhood disputes. She takes this responsibility very seriously. 

Galeana is also an outspoken opponent of the growing materialism of the city's elves and her relations with the members of the @[House of Flanderin](landmark:cdb9ebbb-7478-469b-908c-41187de663a4) are frosty at best.

articles.title: Gallia Stonnard
articles.content:
Almost twelve years @[Gilberto Maggia](person:f8abcaf4-8f94-42f6-84ea-94c3c8c1b1a4)'s junior, Gallia has many of Marita's features but on a smaller, rounder face; she is of medium build, with brown hair and eyes. 

Gallia is a portrait painter, and spends part of her time engaged in this pursuit in a small walk-in cubicle located in an alleyway just off the Street of Caravans in @[The North Corridor](settlement:4554e4a9-db69-47da-9921-6c5850001ce8). She also has had formal training in mathematics, and helps Gilberto out two days a week by keeping his business accounts in financial order. 

 She is very soft-spoken, but confident; new challenges interest her and spur her on. Secretly, Gallia would like to be the family member that replaces Gilberto in the Council of Boroughs but she does not know how to show Gilberto that she is more qualified for this role than Romano. While she is around the Maggia offices, Gallia observes of the merchants and traders who come and go, and mentally notes those that have influence with Gilberto (hoping someday to convince one of them to intervene in her behalf). 

 Gallia and her husband @[Emmaeus Stonnard](person:95c3ce21-9114-4a5f-8c7b-d27664aedf32) (a lieutenant in the Ducal Guard) have two sons, 12 and 10 years old, and an enormous sheepdog, Stanislaus, who lies at Galliana's feet when she is working on her portraits. [br][br] [familytree:751038ab-43fe-415d-ab55-d45afa985182] [br]

articles.title: Gallo Trencher
articles.content: Owner and stablemaster of @[Trencher's Pony Stable](landmark:8a9ab4f3-6534-48d3-9b16-0d9bce2d6bcd)

articles.title: Garduccio
articles.content: A large, fat man in his early forties. He has black hair which curls in little ringlets and black eyes which can appraise a person in a few seconds. He likes food, beer, and company, particularly that of people who deal with money.

articles.title: Gavin Campanella
articles.content:
Keeper of the @[Carillon Tower](landmark:0723cf41-4ef8-46d2-baaf-7101f4146e4a), Gavin lives on the lower floors. He knows that there is a secret, 9th bell in the tower. The bell is magical, although Gavin is not sure what it does but he knows it must be rung if the city is ever threatened. 

 Gavin writes "adventure ballads" in his spare time  which are sometimes sung in the taverns. They are, however, totally fictional. 

 His mother, Ranna, owns @[Mixolydian Mode](landmark:11295957-2b7d-4d5c-bb99-2a0a765035f6).

articles.title: George
articles.content: George is Gip's nephew and helps out at Gip's store.

articles.title: Geraldine
articles.content: She is a large woman, who makes ends meet by renting rooms in her spacious row house, and by doing laundry for some of the neighbors.

articles.title: Geronio
articles.content: A dwarf who is both extremely greedy and exceedingly lazy. He therefore is trying to make as much money as he can with as little effort as possible. To this end, he runs a small, casino-type operation which, on better days, is thoroughly dishonest (you wouldn't believe the bad days).

articles.title: Geru Nohokkan
articles.content:
An orc-elf half-breed of less than ugly mien and disposition; tall but fairly slender, light haired and green eyed, he still betrays the signs of his orcish father in the set of his jaw and the heavy beard growing there. He has no trouble dealing with elves (they tend to be less harsh on half-breeds than other races), but will pretend that those of orcish descent do not even exist - he refuses to notice them and has been known to walk into (and over) a half-orc in his way. 

 Geru leads caravans primarily to the East, toward the cities of the fabled Namori Empire. He is usually successful, and is relatively well off from the fruits of his travels. 

 He maintains a home near @[Thieves' Market](settlement:8b3bf96f-ea9a-4e39-8c3f-bda804df5cdb) where his wife (a pretty human girl) raises their two children. He seldom travels more than 3 months away from Haven (a six month round trip) and will always spend at least 2 months with his family when he returns.

articles.title: Gib
articles.content: Stablehand at @[Trencher's Pony Stable](landmark:8a9ab4f3-6534-48d3-9b16-0d9bce2d6bcd). Not above a bit of larceny if the opportunity presents itself, like leaving valuables in their saddlebags.

articles.title: Gibbon Garrazano
articles.content: Gibbon, the @[Blacksmith](landmark:7cfb1b0f-92fe-4da7-8d2b-1fa59f1b6aa0), is a tough and darkly bearded dwarf who swings his nine pound hammer like a child's toy. He often works effortlessly for 10 to 12 hours a day, without rest breaks. Gibbon is a gentle type and enjoys wandering through the fields outside the Shield Gate during non-working days. He relies on @[Folonar Fairweather](person:2a43fc0e-a5c9-4683-9db5-78a2008d2f72) for guidance and will almost always (95%) accede to the latter's wishes in business or personal matters.

articles.title: Giblet
articles.content: Giblet is a counter clerk at the @[Professor's Challenge](landmark:406c46cf-0370-4cc8-940f-415e25fe9783) during the week.

articles.title: Gidri
articles.content:
Gidri almost always woks with his wife @[Gossij](person:8e7a7ca2-f926-4da8-8de2-2470a7a6b1db). Professionally, their primary skills are as lock picks/safecrackers and burglars. Both are also hardy, well-muscled types able to find employment as guards, laborers, or even as longshoreman for purposes of reconnoitering a job site (in point of fact, @[Gossij](person:8e7a7ca2-f926-4da8-8de2-2470a7a6b1db) is a good deal stronger and more proficient with weapons than her mate). They do not panic in an emergency, and have plugged their way out of several scrapes - though Gidri has spent one three month stretch in @[The Grey Halls](landmark:29cb4deb-4fef-475f-8c31-0d8e6f188cda) on an assault charge. 

 Notwithstanding their considerable criminal skills, the couple's most outstanding feature is that they are two of the most highly ranked Black Hand double agents in the Guild organization. To maintain their cover, they act only sparingly in the Hand's behalf, passing information as needed to either Angus McFarlane (Thieves Market) or @[Mordred de Laterre](person:cd862acf-c62c-4768-84c7-fea8d1aad3cd) (Caravan Street) for delivery and taking their instructions directly from Alphonso Caradello (the South Docks). On one critical occasion, their orders came from Father @[Marco](person:92490b02-65df-4f78-9e42-accf38ae00d1) himself. Ninety- five percent of the time, however, the dwarves act as wholly committed Guild thieves, and during these times will not take chances on betraying themselves by seeking to foil the plots they are privy to.

articles.title: Gilberto Maggia
articles.content:
An immensely proud, hardworking man of about fifty, who has olive skin and dark hair and eyes. His hands are covered with many small scars from his work. Gilberto himself is not a highly educated man, for he discovered at a young age that his heart was in the vineyards; he has a great respect for learning, however, and has encouraged other members of his family to seek a sound education. 

 He is a very emotional man given to flowery prose or earthy curses when his sensitivities are aroused. Lately he has been in ill health, and frequently bed-ridden; consequently, he is very pleased at the great progress his son @[Romano Maggia](person:816ba47f-c0aa-4d9a-afa9-161de52da738), or "Mano", has shown as a wine-maker and simultaneously fearful of his son's immaturity and quick temper. He hopes to find a suitable girl for Mano, so that the latter might settle down.  

 Gilberto is both head of the Winemakers Guild and master of the @[Guild of Provenders](organization:8880f281-e0e8-4dde-9ff9-a9251f1fbae9) that governs all the food production trades (butchering, baking, brewing, etc.) 

 Gilberto has used some of his wealth to encourage promising young artists, sculptors, and inventors; several of those receiving his patronage have work spaces in the flats and lofts along @[Studio Lane](landmark:a3a5c599-c67d-41a6-b3be-d94b4271a605) in @[The Heights](settlement:1f0571c0-b8de-4b50-b010-5529cab6603b). @[Romulo Velasquez](person:0abd1b09-4093-4a05-9563-7ff27309b96c),is one such beneficiary. [br][br] [familytree:f8abcaf4-8f94-42f6-84ea-94c3c8c1b1a4] [br]

articles.title: Gladiolus Blackbourne
articles.content:
A pudgy blond haired lad with very delicate features and an acerbic tongue, Gladiolus has exhibited rather unusual sexual preferences, and is known disparagingly around town as the "Fruit of the Loom". Gladiolus is his father's shame, and the two rarely speak (when they do, it is usually at the top of their lungs). Hamlin tried for a time to bring Gladiolus into the business as a clerk, but he was so insulting to customers that the idea was quickly abandoned. 

 He now receives a small stipend from his father, and has no other income. Consequently, he can often be found in local taverns, trying to find someone who will buy him a drink (there is also a 40% chance that Gladiolus will show a strong, non-platonic interest in any male in the party with a combined CHA + COM > 25). 

 Gladiolus spends most of his days hanging around @[Studio Lane](landmark:a3a5c599-c67d-41a6-b3be-d94b4271a605), for he has several friends among the artist community; he is working out a plan with one of them, Romary Claiph, to replace some of the valuable paintings in the homes of @[The Heights](settlement:1f0571c0-b8de-4b50-b010-5529cab6603b) with clever facsimiles painted by Claiph. [br][br] [familytree:89da4db7-deaa-40b5-a6c8-68f795bf113e] [br]

articles.title: Gladshaw
articles.content:
Gladshaw is egotistical and conceited and has never hired a helper due to this very fact.  Due to his very "noble" manner he will not deal with characters that do not show him proper respect. 

Gladshaw dresses in a dandified fashion when appearing socially, and often wears a gaudy cloak made of hundreds of different colored bird feathers and plumes.

articles.title: Glokkin Masterbell
articles.content: Black bearded, well-muscled, and perpetually scowling. He is notoriously hard to please, whether it be the tuning of a bell or the way the shop is swept by his apprentices. It is said that the only time he ever smiles is when he hears the Tower bells ring the changes.

articles.title: Glumin Duhm
articles.content: A morose man of middle years; he appears gray, and even projects an aura of gray. He will tell you all the terrible things that have happened to him, and the problem of his tenants, raining a veritable barrage of pessimism upon the ears of anyone willing to listen (or unwilling to be impolite and walk away).

articles.title: Golbur
articles.content: A dealer in cut and uncut stones, he dresses rather foppishly, in brightly colored clothing of golds, reds and oranges. He has a personal weakness for gems of those shades and will pay 10-20% more for these stones than he will for others of the same quality

articles.title: Goodreau
articles.content: Runs a food market selling meat, fruit and dairy products.

articles.title: Gorboo
articles.content: A long-time associate of @[Tenley Tainley](person:abedfa62-b993-4d72-acdf-a10e5c2fc4f7)'s from the yeoman class, Gorboo lives on the Tainley estate, and is responsible for training the wards in the use of a variety of weapons - sword, mace (men only), bow, and dagger (females only). Of the three current wards, of course, Antonio far outstrips the others in combat skill, and receives the bulk of Gorboo's personal attention. Gorboo often praises Antonio's fighting prowess publicly (particularly after he has had a few drinks) [br][br] [familytree:3f0d56c3-b68f-46a0-abc1-feee206853dc] [br]

articles.title: Gordon Vickery
articles.content: A good average lawyer; he wins the share of cases his ability entitles him to, and draws neither bonuses nor penalties from any of the judges. His reputation comes from winning a very messy murder case in which his client (actually innocent) was totally implicated by circumstantial evidence. Vickery is tall, stocky, with brown hair and blue eyes. He is frequently (90%) found at @[The Lying Lawyer](landmark:0f5a29ce-4b27-422f-a557-e53239d964d0); he might be a better lawyer, but he has an incredible taste for alcoholic beverages, and is not uncommonly poured into a bed in one of rooms upstairs at the inn at the close of business.

articles.content: Gorra and her husband @[Jambur](person:8e95192f-5952-4630-b6a0-baf8deec903b), make and sell men's and women's clothing.

articles.content:
Gossij almost always works with her husband @[Gidri](person:0fce811a-620e-4182-bc91-f74320f53062). Professionally, their primary skills are as lock picks/safecrackers and burglars. Both are also hardy, well-muscled types able to find employment as guards, laborers, or even as longshoreman for purposes of reconnoitering a job site (in point of fact, Gossij is a good deal stronger and more proficient with weapons than her mate). They do not panic in an emergency, and have plugged their way out of several scrapes - though @[Gidri](person:0fce811a-620e-4182-bc91-f74320f53062) has spent one three month stretch in @[The Grey Halls](landmark:29cb4deb-4fef-475f-8c31-0d8e6f188cda) on an assault charge. 

 Notwithstanding their considerable criminal skills, the couple's most outstanding feature is that they are two of the most highly ranked Black Hand double agents in the Guild organization. To maintain their cover, they act only sparingly in the Hand's behalf, passing information as needed to either Angus McFarlane (Thieves Market) or @[Mordred de Laterre](person:cd862acf-c62c-4768-84c7-fea8d1aad3cd) (Caravan Street) for delivery and taking their instructions directly from Alphonso Caradello (the South Docks). On one critical occasion, their orders came from Father @[Marco](person:92490b02-65df-4f78-9e42-accf38ae00d1) himself. Ninety- five percent of the time, however, the dwarves act as wholly committed Guild thieves, and during these times will not take chances on betraying themselves by seeking to foil the plots they are privy to.

articles.title: Gotbert
articles.content:
A hot, new priest in blue robes who preached on street corners. He is trying to convert passersby to the cult of XXXXXXX. 

See Street Encounter: Hot Priest

articles.title: Grabbit
articles.content: See scenario @[The South Keep Gang](plot:652ff4d1-71f3-44ac-9ac1-57e1b1f881c8)

articles.title: Graella Maggia
articles.content: @[Gilberto Maggia](person:f8abcaf4-8f94-42f6-84ea-94c3c8c1b1a4)'s wife is a very rotund, cheerful woman, she has wavy, shoulder-length black hair, several double chins, and seems to always reek of stale sweat. Graella is an excellent cook (which, in large part, accounts for her size), but a very lazy housekeeper; she treats her household maids as slaves, and no one has ever worked for her for more than 6 months. She knows full well that she is out of place in high society, and never attends social functions with Gilberto. She was well loved by the children who grew up in @[The Commons](settlement:8ff1c19a-c29d-4050-9c7c-7200f23453be) neighborhood where Gilberto and Graella spent their early married life, and many of these young men and women still stop by the Maggia estate to say hello to "Momma". [br][br] [familytree:8c74d2a0-a09b-4139-a4a1-e51fdb18413f] [br]

articles.title: Grazia de la Riis
articles.content: Once a beautiful, lively queen of the Haven social circuit, @[Tybalt de la Riis](person:4c0f8c89-3d7b-46e9-8e62-4506ed433370)' sister is now senile and feeble-minded. She rarely is taken beyond the boundaries of the manor house, for she has an unfortunate habit of mistaking young men that she meets for her dead son, Porcassio, making quite a scene in the process. [br][br] [familytree:43b58a87-6a4e-4e26-9477-c855f601f66c] [br]

articles.title: Green Card Man
articles.content: See Street Encounter: Green Cards

articles.title: Grimsby Farsteel
articles.content:
The Hand's loan shark in @[The South Docks](settlement:e2e38a16-2c10-443d-b40a-6789aa7c041a) area, runs a small pawnshop on Drayers' Loop. He is a wiry man, totally bald and bespectacled, with a permanent collection of ugly red welts adorning his arms and neck, and a wheezing but nasal voice. His unappetizing appearance seems somehow perfectly suited to his trade, for Farsteel's under-the-counter loans often represent the last desperate hope for a sea-trader down on his luck. 

 Grimsby has the resources to make loans of up to 50,000gp, but his terms are steep: 100% interest, payable in six months, and temporary transfer of the official registry of the borrower's ship into the name of one of @[The Black Hand](organization:d1a96263-4191-482e-ace6-360d25106f60) fronting companies. In this way, the Hand has obtained permanent (upon default of these loans) title to four of its current smuggling vessels at minimal cost. 

 Farsteel has fair sources of information about the wharf area, and will soon hear of any vessel/captain in financial distress. Thereafter, it will not be long before he makes an appearance on the scene, wheezing his solicitations and hinting at his ability to lend assistance for a proper "arrangement".

articles.title: Groton
articles.content: Vendor of top-of-the-line perfumes and colognes

articles.title: Gudyumar
articles.content: See Street Encounter: Jingle Bells

articles.title: Gunter Geronde
articles.content:
A thin lad of twenty with dirty-blond hair and a perpetual sneer, Gunter eats, sleeps and breathes the lifestyle of the @[Young Stallions](organization:7340b23d-2c0c-45fd-8222-13b00aa2760c). The group is his source of identity and without it, Gunter would probably be a faceless recruit in @[The Citadel](landmark:7b465292-ac23-4b4d-a13a-92af694b058b) Guard. He always wears @[The Green](landmark:58c2143a-18ef-4281-89c4-96547a184d4a) swordsman's cloak, white brooch, and black boots that constitute the Stallion's uniform, and seldom travels outside the presence of one or more of his compatriots. 

 A decent but not overpowering fighter, Gunter is nonetheless unafraid to take on very unpromising odds, if he believes that fighting will further the nobility's cause. Gunter, while not stupid, did not inherit his parents' intellectual prowess; he was an extremely lackadaisical student, and consequently cannot read or write very well (a fact he desperately tries to hide from the others). 

He would like to be @[Paul de la Riis](person:61db5c85-e436-459e-926e-17ad7e116b03)’ or @[Antonio Berensten](person:ec8f50d3-84f6-48a6-95d0-d7d6b5b65cb8)'s best friend, and is somewhat hurt by the unspoken closeness between the two that he cannot share. [br][br] [familytree:e174a916-f1e9-45b9-8291-2e42b7f39268] [br]

articles.title: Gustav Morris
articles.content: A young energetic composer working under the patronage of the @[Maggia Family](organization:7157ba84-27ce-44ee-998e-007b1b0b58fa). Tall and thin, with curly blond hair Gustav works odd hours, plunking on a harpsichord far into the night. Gustav has a well-deserved reputation for eccentricity, both in his person and his music.

articles.content: "Guzzler" is the owner of @[The Golden Goblet](landmark:ae0ead67-61dc-4e1e-b561-c3d265944e29), a fat little man who is never found without a mug in his hand (usually partially full of beer). He is normally behind the counter in the rear (near the expensive gold, silver, and glass).

articles.title: Gyr Windbreaker
articles.content: Short and stocky, greenish hued, wolf faced individual with stumpy unusable wings, named Gyr Windbreaker is a multi-breed  who is pleasant to all and finds animosity for none.

articles.title: Haldo Rumbutter
articles.content: @[The Golden Ducat](landmark:6c10e646-893f-4767-b911-e0cfeae3ea04)'s chef, Haldo Rumbutter, is an exceedingly rotund halfling who recognizes only one chef, Undo Hardcastle (at the Aerie), as his peer. He is exceptionally perturbed by all the recent uproar in @[The Heights](settlement:1f0571c0-b8de-4b50-b010-5529cab6603b) about the cooking feats of Biggs Oldbuck, and the mere mention of the latter's name when Haldo is in earshot is a good way to guarantee a badly burned meal.

articles.title: Hallen MacCormac
articles.content: A hulk of a man who helps @[Angus MacFarland](person:164c1af1-3217-4879-aaa1-3f5c49eb70f6) selling assorted powdered spices and minerals (sort of an early version of a natural health store), and assorted drugs (particularly hashish) under the counter.

articles.title: Hambo Stoutbarrel
articles.content: A middle-aged halfling of tremendous girth, who is always dressed in a tent-like brown tunic and a grease-stained leather apron; he dislikes working hard, and gets angry when patrons become impatient for service. Hambo is extremely chauvinistic (one may note the absence of female employees in this establishment), and an accomplished spinner of tall tales; he knows a smattering of lore (just enough to be dangerous) on about a thousand different subjects.

articles.title: Hamlin Blackbourne
articles.content:
A small, bald-headed man with a nagging cough and darting watery eyes; Hamlin is an austere, stern man who rarely laughs or smiles. Despite the key role he plays in setting the trends of fashion in Haven, Hamlin wears rather worn, out-of-date outfits himself, and often looks as if he has just slept in his clothing. He is a workaholic, who can often be seen burning the midnight oil in the study of his estate, poring over the scrawled notes taken by one of his traders on his last expedition. 

 He hates formal occasions, and does not drink alcohol. He does smoke a pipe incessantly (using only the finest blends of tobacco), despite his respiratory problems. 

 It is easy to respect Hamlin for his boundless energy and his business genius, yet he is difficult to like, for he is very opinionated and expects things to be done his way. [br][br] [familytree:24dec529-0265-4bb9-bb8c-d6240dea4bb9] [br]

articles.title: Han Vilkorus
articles.content:
Dark-haired, clean shaven, and very well-muscled, Han is the heartthrob of half the young ladies of the neighborhood. Han is also well aware of their interest, and it has gone to his head. Now he believes himself irresistible, and has become quite a ladies man. His ready smile and courtly manners have gained him many a pleasant evening, but he seems to love variety, and never stays with the same girl. Many of the local young men dislike him, not surprisingly. 

 Han sings when he works, and is charming and flirtatious with any attractive young woman he encounters.

articles.content: Husband of @[Valma](person:3bd5a0c5-d4b3-4307-9da1-01a0637fc374) (nee @[Geronde](organization:f19cd890-5d54-44cd-b4bf-d301b974af87)), Hanzal is a leatherworker from a merchant background who repairs tack and saddles in a little shop located very close to the city's immense @[Horse Market](settlement:3987cb08-4abd-4e55-a582-128df2ff71db). He and Valma live with the rest of the Matters family in a crowded, but nicely maintained, two-story wood structure in the residential area west of @[The Street of Harps](settlement:6053011d-37a6-4d6b-8e0b-41925f3bbd77). articles.content: The owner of @[Dunk's Tavern](landmark:b85508a0-047c-4029-b83d-0793982d4472), Hari is a former drover frequently referred to as "Dunk"

articles.title: Harlequin Bussbender
articles.content:
The night assistant at @[The Golden Ducat](landmark:6c10e646-893f-4767-b911-e0cfeae3ea04), Harlequin Bussbender, is a youth of 20, blond-haired and blue-eyed. He works a variety of jobs between 4:00pm and 2:00am (the official closing hour for the inn), tending the front desk, serving meals and drinks, and answering guest demands for services or repairs. He is sometimes lackadaisical in performing his duties, which earns him regular tongue-lashings from Perkins. 

The son of an affluent mercantile family, he dreams of someday running off with a beautiful noblewoman; he has excellent skills with thrown missile weapons, and an instinctive knack for repairing mechanical implements.

articles.title: Harz de la Riis
articles.content:
A husky, well-muscled man with grey-streaked dark hair, and a deeply furrowed brow. Harz has managed to keep the de la Riis property intact while many of the other noble families have had to sell off their hereditary lands. To do so, however, he was forced to adapt to the changing economic system resulting from the rise of the Guilds, and diversify the family's activities from farming into related businesses like grain milling. 

He has been rewarded for these efforts by the hostility of his two sons, who accuse him of “selling out" to the Guildsmen and their lack of affection has robbed him of his zest for living.     

On formal occasions, Harz wears a large emerald ring engraved with the family crest; at all times, he wears a bronze medallion inlaid with a sunburst design of orange and yellow zircons (a present from his wife Claudia de la Riis). 

Harz is one of the 24 members of the Council of Boroughs, and spends about 50% of his time in the city. He is also a supporter of Watch Captain @[Lyza](person:7bdbde76-bf2e-4c7d-9d8a-87b0d66a54de) and it was his support on council that got her command created, despite what @[Mikyl Swiftsword](person:403bf324-8208-4b8f-98d1-8e98ded30ba5) thought.

articles.title: Heidel Varrasch
articles.content:
The current master of the major Drayers Guild (which includes the horse trainers and sellers, the wagon makers and wheelwrights, the saddle and harness makers, and other allied trades) is a hulking bear of a man, with immense, well-muscled legs, arms and shoulders; he is almost completely bald with broad and rather unseemly features. He dresses in rugged leather breeches, and often works bare-chested; he also possesses a collection of vulgar personal habits better left unmentioned in a family oriented gaming aid. 

 Heidel is astonishingly agile for a man of his girth; and has inherited his father’s uncanny understanding of horses and can work and calm the most unruly mounts (those in the nobility given to sarcasm would contend that this is due to Heidel's own animal-like behavior).  

 He owns the fastest horse in Haven, which has beaten all challengers to date (no mean feat, considering the stallion carries Heidel's considerable bulk). 

 Heidel, has a very short temper; if verbally taunted by the Stallions or others, he will almost certainly respond with physical force unless his brother is present to calm him down. On one such prior occasion, Heidel badly thrashed @[Paul de la Riis](person:61db5c85-e436-459e-926e-17ad7e116b03) in a brawl, and Paul has sworn to get revenge. 

 Heidel has used some of his past business profits to buy lands outside of Haven put up for sale by the more impoverished nobility; the Stallions are strenuously opposing any further sales to Varrasch, so he now hires others to act as his agents in such negotiations (keeping his role anonymous). She is also known as an experienced navigator with a unbeatable weather sense. Helene is short and her faced lined with years of seafaring. Her hair is short and greying, but her crew have been with her for years, and wish no other captain.

articles.title: Helvia Larksong
articles.content:
Master of Journeymen in the Entertainers Guild, Helvia is a middle-aged, slightly built woman with bright blue eyes, greying hair, a vibrant personality, and an iron will. Dedicated to her job of overseeing the Guild's various journeymen, she knows them all by name. She also has on file were each journeyman is assigned, and would be in charge of finding a "situation" for a new journeyman (i.e. a player character). 

 She is happily married to Petrovio Larksong, a composer, and lives in @[The Cleff](landmark:4c5b107f-5d33-4bbf-87c8-a0d16335a80a). She despises @[Rael Gavotte](person:1217ee33-13e6-4a14-8fdb-9755b8a993dc) for personal reasons. 

 Helvia knows that the harper-journeyman @[Vernadot](person:70250451-96d9-441a-ba4b-3d3db516baf6) has recently become a member of the Temple of the Sky, and will answer questions to this effect, if she believes the questioners are friends of @[Vernadot](person:70250451-96d9-441a-ba4b-3d3db516baf6)'s, or have a legitimate reason for needing to find him.

articles.title: Herbert
articles.content: A portly, well-dressed man of middle years, with a shiny bald pate and gray eyes. He tends to specialize in civil cases, and has an excellent record in them, since he will split his fees with the judge involved. Any time Cardallo sees Herbert's name as lawyer of record on a civil case, he arranges to preside; Herbert has never failed the judge's expectations, and gets a healthy +60% preference from him. He limits his clientele to the more wealthy of the city, and seldom (10%) will he accept a criminal case. If any judge is presiding but Cardallo, he functions at a penalty of -10%, since all of them know of his deals with Cardallo. He is basically colorless in personality, and rarely, if ever, patronizes a tavern, preferring to spend his evenings at home with his family.

Herven is relatively staid in all other ways, and exhibits less bigotry than any other judge. He, too, despises Cardallo, and would like nothing better than to see the lecherous scoundrel removed from office; so far, no evidence sufficient for impeachment (even in the aggregate) has been discovered.

articles.title: Hughar Wolfskill
articles.content: One of the few tieflings tolerated outside @[The Labyrinth](settlement:e05f9a94-a44d-4991-b419-28cae89db0ee); grizzled and greying, of medium stature with dark, heavy-lidded eyes, he owns and runs a school to train and sell dogs and wolves for guard, pack, and companion duties (VI-S133). Hughar has been accustomed to working with and around canines and lupines since infancy; his ability with these animals is incredible - he can train any dog/wolf (even very vicious ones) to a high degree of performance (the better the training, the longer it takes, possibly as much as a year of daily sessions), working with the animal's master or without. His costs are High, but quite reasonable in view of the Superb quality of his work.

articles.title: Huiel Farris
articles.content: Tall, lean, dark-haired, with penetrating eyes. He has excellent connections with all the High Judges, and receives preference from all (a difficult feat, to say the least): +15% from Cardallo (who feels Huiel is no one to cross), +5% from Dagnir, +10% from @[Ellian](person:d55b0a64-eecc-4636-b48c-0f429ae8dccc) and Herven, and +20% from Mindal. Probably one of the finest legal minds in Haven, his schedule is usually so filled that there is only a 25% chance that he will accept a new client, although he makes no distinction as to class or ability to pay - if you hit him at the right time, you've got a good lawyer. Huiel is frequently (80%) found at @[The Lying Lawyer](landmark:0f5a29ce-4b27-422f-a557-e53239d964d0) in the evenings, shop talking with others in the legal profession.

She has not taken to her new step-mother, @[K'maill de la Riis](person:8999eb05-e84c-48a7-a490-a49df5429d0d), and along with aunt Rutmilla de la Riis has been spreading rumours that K'maill has evil magic powers. articles.title: Istara
articles.content:
Istara rules over all things magical and is the patron of wizards, sorcerers, and any others who draw on themselves for magic.

Unlike any of the other Firstborn, Istara has only one parent, Laydi. Whether there was a father, another mother, or was born through  parthenogenesis is not known. She is said to be unfavored, as those who would most benefit from her blessings are also those who are least prone to worship, namely the practitioners of the arcane arts.

She created the weave, the flow of arcane energy that allows magic to happen, and it is said that those born with the spontaneous gift of magic are touched by her. 

Her holy symbol is a chariot, based on the constellation Agrae with its eight stars, one representing each school of magic.

articles.title: Ivan Petrushka
articles.content: A tall, burly man with a thick black beard, bushy eyebrows and a scowl permanently on his face. He speaks in surly monosyllables and grunts, and walks with a painful limp. Through his puppets, however, he is a different man; cheerful, loving, and vivacious, but only through the puppets can he release his true gentle nature. He is not aware of this split of his personality - but the puppets talk about "the boss" constantly, bemoaning his hard heart!

He has an almost uncanny facility for knowing which way an investment, or a client, will run. Since his wife died 10 years ago, he has devoted himself almost entirely to his business affairs. Occasionally, he will treat himself to an evening of shoptalk at his favorite tavern, @[Garduccio's](landmark:fddb6dc5-8f76-4d9b-a810-3446cdbf7829) [br][br] [familytree:3c39acd4-67f1-40a3-8ef1-ba378524e0f1] [br]

articles.title: Jakuel Estankris
articles.content:
Fourteen with a slight boyish figure with shaggily cut black hair, and dark of skin and eye. She wears boy's clothes, and will pass herself off as a boy (use disguise rules) if she can. Like the average player-character, she is newly arrived in Haven, and is not familiar with the city. She has been supporting herself by picking pockets and petty theft - she is very quick. The Thieves Guild has been keeping an eye out for her, but they have yet to catch her, 

 Jaquel is a bitter girl, and on a mission of vengeance: only a year ago, a bandit gang raided and destroyed most of her clan in the southeastern mountain area. She has been on the lookout for members of this gang ever since, and has actually assassinated two men she believed to be some of the guilty ones. At the GM's discretion, she may enlist the aid of the players in her quest, or test them to see if any among them are guilty of her family's murders, 

 "Jac", as she calls herself, is very good with a bow, a dagger, or tracking; she has a small amount of poison she will use if necessary.

articles.title: Janus Trask
articles.content: Janus is the daughter of Pietro Domenici, a local ship's captain and explorer of some small renown, who was lost at sea when she was a young woman. She is still a striking woman with hip length auburn hair and greenish eyes, but the years of indoor labor have left her pale and wan, and she seems to have forgotten how to smile; she will not travel by water since her father's tragedy, though she loved to sail in her youth.

articles.title: Jarien the Jeweler
articles.content:
A small man, balding, with greedy eyes. Jarien buys and sells old jewelry and coins; his stall has glassed-in cases (enchanted to prevent breakage) where his more expensive wares are displayed. Jarien knows well the value of his pieces, and has a 65% chance of recognizing a fake at first glance (100% if he spends some time to study it more carefully), 

 Jarien is a notoriously hard bargainer, and is quick to take advantage of a customer's ignorance, should the occasion arise; but an aggressive bargainer can usually get a fair price out of him. Jarien collects rare old coins, in addition to his money-changing; he will be very interested in any coins he has never seen before. (30% chance they are unknown to him). The coin collection is in a secret panel in one of the three heavy traveling trunks on his wagon; it is heavily trapped. The existence of this collection is not well known, and he will reveal it only to another "collector". It is worth approximately 20,000 GP for the metal and rarity of the coins.

articles.content: Jasmine is a tattoo artist of renown, able to charge considerable amounts for her talents. She is a largish woman of indeterminate middle-age, with stringy brown hair, and is usually found in her shop, seated on a worn couch in front of a low table covered with needles, dye pots, etc. She pays local urchins to keep her apprised of the arrival of new ships in both the North and South docks

articles.title: Jasper Reid
articles.content: Old arthritic Jasper buys and sells used clothing from this dilapidated house. If he suspects anything of why business has improved in recent months, he says nothing. Jasper did not reach his present age by indulging his curiosity.

articles.title: Jelaine
articles.content: Jelaine, merchant, a tall, lean woman with short dark hair beginning to grey is a guest at @[The Pendragon Inn](landmark:8aaefea5-dcd6-4b71-9167-d94a465e453f). She is a dealer in pearls and semi-precious stones and her store of samples is cached in the Inn's safe. She will be looking for trustworthy guards in a few days to accompany her in a caravan going west to her home.

articles.title: Jigger Cassadi
articles.content:
Chief entertainer, Jigger plays a mean guitar, and also plays the more dangerous game of being a @[Thieves' Guild](organization:08dce3b2-80f7-468b-be7b-dd5fdbfac799) informant (he has a 30% chance of knowing given information about any ship on the docks).

He has a weakness for people (either sex) with red hair.

articles.title: Jim Bostry
articles.content: Works for @[Lazar Symbocca](person:2c51d376-29e2-4868-ac54-050e58f8c59c) at @[Sym's Storage Company](landmark:950bc2b9-c121-4be6-a597-f3373ed455b0). He is a Black Hand member but doesn't know the full extent of Lazar's business.

articles.title: Jock McPherson
articles.content:
Jock is the @[Blackbourne Family](organization:6c8621a2-aa73-4991-9953-e9d61539619c)'s oldest and wisest hand and is overseeing the tutalge of @[Marcus Blackbourne](person:c25b3e51-9cef-4227-9e6c-f65949acdd3c) as he learns move about the family's businesses. 

 Because of this there is only a 20% chance of he (and Marcus) being in town as the cloth trade keeps him on the road. When they are in town, the two will hit the taverns. Jock often needs to restrain Marcus who won't back down from a fight, even if the odds are against him. [br][br] [familytree:d607a9f6-86e2-4153-aea7-44c5e52859af] [br]

articles.title: Joffa the Barakite
articles.content: Joffa the Barakite is a small, dark-skinned man with an oily complexion, and a personality to match - it is certainly safe to say that people do not patronize this establishment out of personal affection for the owner. Joffa is an unctuous, hard-hearted individual who has little regard for his fellow man; however, he has made it his business to know what people like, and to spend the cash necessary to provide such comforts.
