articles.title: Nalla Thuliaga
articles.content:
A bouncer at @[The Aerie](landmark:f24b8234-a53d-47df-84dd-26adc048a141), Nalla is an example of the strong silent type. He is over 7' tall and 350lbs. He is so mean-looking, even his friends call him "Sir". Besides maintaining a strict watch over the entrance, Nalla and the other goliath bouncers are summoned to the scene whenever trouble erupts. 

 Though he rarely speaks, he understands the need for delicacy in performing his job. He has become particularly adept at eliminating potential combatants by means of a surprisingly rapid head slap which renders the recipient unconscious, but causes no permanent damage  other than a ringing in one's ears for several hours after. 

 Nalla seems to have little interest in fleshly pleasures, save for an occasional craving for raw meat

articles.title: Narconal
articles.content:
Narconal is god of the earth and the  patron of farmers and miners. Volcanos are what happens when he and brother @[Maedhros](person:1c8a7687-5623-48f0-b9bd-23725a2c8e34) get angry. 
[p]
articles.honorific: God of the Earth and Agriculture
articles.domains:
Unsurprisingly, the followers of Narconal feel a deep connection to the earth itself. They understand that each of the Firstborn works in harmony with the others, and that without any of them, life would be impossible. But they view Narconal as the base, or foundation upon which the others build. Virtually every farmer prays to Narconal, as he is ultimately responsible for the bounty of the earth.  

Somewhat surprisingly, many soldiers also hold him in nearly as deep reverence as Strathos, for they know that victory in battle becomes impossible if the ground turns against you.  

He is also the patron god of many craftsmen, particularly those who work with wood, one of his gifts to the races of mankind.
articles.codes:
The most holy book for those who worship Narconal is The Book of the Land. The first words in the centuries old text were written by Agromar of the Northern Wilds. The text is currently a collection of 107 parables that teach about respect and renewal of the land and describe ways that the races of man can thrive together.  

The Book of the Land is not a static document, but change comes slowly. In rare but not unheard of cases, an adherent of Narconal will have a vision in which a new parable is told. Clerics of Narconal will then determine if the parable is valid, often by asking Narconal himself. 

In even rarer circumstances, a parable may be removed if Narconal decrees it is no longer canon. These former parables have been collected in a lesser work known as the Book of Aged Wisdom. There is a very minor schism within those who worship Narconal as to if the Book of Aged Wisdom should be kept, or if those who read it are apostate.
articles.holysymbols: The holy symbol of Narconel depicts a sickle and a sheaf of wheat. It is also traditional for worshipers of Narconel to carry with them a small piece of charcoal wrapped in a linen cloth (this also serves a functional purpose, as they use it to write and make markings as needed).
articles.tenets: The core tenet of the faith is that we come from the earth, the earth gives us life, and someday we will return to the earth. Burial is considered the final sacrament, and worshipers are buried naked (though wrapped in a simple linen shroud) without any jewelry or adornments.
articles.goals: Worshipers are expected to respect the land, and give thanks for its gifts. The land is considered to be one thing. If one part of the land must be disturbed, such as to build a cellar, then care must be taken elsewhere to give back to allow the land to recover its strength. They are expected to understand that the land will give its gifts freely, but if it is abused, then there are no more gifts to give. Effort and respect are expected, but so are a degree of merriment, because if we work ourselves into an early grave we cannot aid the earth.
articles.holidays:
There are three holidays for Narconel.  One in the spring and two in the fall.

[b]The Day of Awakening[/b] takes place in the spring, on the day the last snow has melted.  It is a somber event, where the faithful give thanks for making it through the long winter, and remembering those who were lost. Priests will begin the preparation of bodies that died during the winter for burial, and farmers will choose the fields that will lay fallow (The Parable of the Restful Field) to regain its strength. In that field, they will construct a wooden shrine to Narconel, usually a rectangular frame, with branches on top serving as makeshift thatching. When Narconel visits the field to bless it, he uses this shrine as shelter when he naps (The Parable of Tulin and His Visitor).

[b]The Festival of Harvest[/b] is the most important of all holy events.  The festival typically lasts for a week, but the actual celebration is the Day of the Feast, where nearly everyone gives thanks for the bounty that Narconel has provided through the work of his followers. It is a festival of games, dancing, and general merriment. (The Parable of the Joyful Squirrel)

[b]The Day of Exchange[/b] is the joint holy day between Narconel and Maedhros, and is three weeks after the end of the Festival of the Harvest. It is the day when Narconel lends his strength to Maedhros so the latter can protect the races of man when the days and nights turn cold (The Parable of the Firstborn Brothers).   Worshipers of Narconel will light a fire at dawn, and tend to it until dawn the next day. In the fields, the farmers will burn the shrine to Narconel they built after the awakening. They will spread the ashes out over the field so that the last of Narconel’s strength can protect the field for when it returns to service in the spring. (The Parable of the Embers). They will also gather charcoal from the ashes, which they carry with them for the following year. In cities, priests and clerics (for both gods) will tend a communal fire, and worshipers and other faithful will drop by to assist.

articles.title: Nathalie Galutine
articles.content:
The Baroness is a no-nonsense elf who runs the inn with militaristic discipline. Her main objective is to keep her business lucrative and catering to only the most successful of upper nobility and their distinguished guests. She has neither the time nor tolerance for mistakes or half measures. Her countenance is stoically beautiful, and she speaks firmly and directly while very rarely engaging in small talk. She bears a cold and direct presence that is felt tenfold by those in her employ.

Despite the property’s rich history, it did not take much for Baroness Natalie Galutine to acquire the grounds. A member of high standing nobility herself, the only thing more prominent than her social status are her achievements garnered through adventuring.  Additionally, the more recent history of the grounds is marred by treachery and darkness,  as the former lord owner was executed for treason nigh two decades prior. This was enough deterrent for potential investors to be scarce at best, leaving negotiations all but wide open for the Baroness. 

She restored the inn in due time, seeing that the aesthetics of the vast property were aligned to its clientele of high nobility, their distinguished guests from nearby or distant lands, and successful adventurers whose achievements have rendered them celebrities across multiple regions.

Inn security’s influence pales in comparison to that of the Baroness, however. Natalie Galutine rules the inn with strict discipline. It is not uncommon for her to physically punish staff members in the more hidden areas of the mansion for breaking glassware, being rude to customers, or any other behavior she deems clumsy or unseemly. Her method of discipline is usually to cane an employee’s hands with a bamboo rod. As a result of such enforcement, a stay at the @[Rose Garden Inn](landmark:d657f21f-881e-4050-bf0b-e5bc103ac61a) is usually an unblemished experience.

articles.title: Neberhard Ohlfaardt
articles.content:
A stocky white-haired man with droopy moustaches and thick spectacles, the Count moves with a faltering step and looks his age, except for the boyish look of absolute rapture that lights up his face from time to time. 

He considers his bride, @[Sui Tuong Ding](person:908c4354-d81f-42f0-9be5-c227e30d2e2c), well worth the price he pays to keep her, and indeed she has revitalized his whole life. He is very attentive to his beloved's every whim, and seems to ignore the advances made on Sui by others (in fact, however, he monitors these flirtations very circumspectly, and takes action through his hired muscle if he considers someone a real threat). 

 He has almost daily consultations with the quack @[Americus](person:db7258df-d1e4-483a-a65f-df6464ef8489), and religiously follows an exercise and diet plan designed by the latter to restore his virility. [br][br] [familytree:aa435b8d-e5f0-4e61-8d17-d6db601760b6] [br]

articles.title: Nenya
articles.content:
Of the Firstborn, Nenya is considered to be the most capricious. She has always been at odds with her siblings, and is viewed by them as an outsider. Her worshipers are often wanderers, and the few temples she has are built in port cities and serve as respites before long sea journeys. Her worshipers believe that life is harsh and often unfair and are said to look for the worst. That said, they usually gain the most enjoyment from the good times.

It is considered disrespectful to not have a shrine to her aboard a ship, and most sailors will not leave beyond sight of the shoreline on any ship that does not have one.

Her gift to the races of man was the storm, to make them stronger through survival.

Her holy symbol is a cloud with a lightning bolt through it.
articles.honorific: Goddess of the Sea, Mother of Storms, Patron of Sailors

articles.title: Nera
articles.content:
A tiefling vagabond, a thin, bony girl of about 15, with dark shaggy hair and eyes set aslant in her homely face. Taken in by Ranna, she cleans pots and pans in the kitchen and other simple chores. 

Nera speaks common with a thick accent and is very shy around people, preferring to remain in the kitchen. 

Fiercely loyal to Ranna and Ryan, and dangerous with a thrown knife

articles.title: Neshima Kar-Aurim
articles.content: A dark-haired Namori beauty, Neshima is a skilled thief and a double agent for @[The Black Hand](organization:d1a96263-4191-482e-ace6-360d25106f60). She had a high position under @[Azimuth](person:38b3505c-7430-4028-8042-c9ce2756fab1), but has been less successful under @[Sulemon Duur](person:287e8880-066e-4f87-971f-707c2560db62), who distrusts her. He does not suspect in the least her double identity; it's just that she is known to be clever, and Duur equates cleverness with ambition. Neshima is a master of disguise, and is also known in various locales in @[The Labyrinth](settlement:e05f9a94-a44d-4991-b419-28cae89db0ee) as Ayeesha the trollop, Arla-Asim the dancer, and the Panther (her code name with the Hand).
articles.nickname: Ayeesha the trollop | Arla-Asim the dancer | the Panther

articles.title: Nikkulai arn Kolvi
articles.content: A dark-bearded, scowling fellow that runs the @[Boarshead Tavern](landmark:c0ea737f-d449-4cf9-9541-fe58d71844d7). He is helped by his daughter Asgird.

articles.title: Nima J. Neb
articles.content: Nima is an optician extradordinaire but tends to use archaic methods of eye adjustment (it is rumored that he once electrocuted a blind man to restore his sight). His wife, Nosi is also an optician and works with him.

articles.title: Nimoyin
articles.content:
A Sindar half-elf of later years, and a former adventurer and traveler, who now prefers the quiet life of his city home. To keep himself busy, he teaches mathematics and philosophy at the @[Institute of Mathematics](landmark:a10e59a2-ff2c-459d-9132-c5e2e57e267b) and lives on South Evenstar, near the @[University of Haven](organization:6ff2021c-f034-4831-9af5-51b6f4177316). He is thought to be a bit odd (probably due to his close association with humans) by the elves, but given some respect, for his vast knowledge. Nimoyin remains close friends with the mercenary Captain @[Kiroc](person:494bc70b-ba36-45cf-b9cf-df77d081ea03) and his band, with whom he traveled for several years, and would do anything to aid his old companions. Despite his years, he remains an expert at unarmed combat. 

 Nimoyin has two students living with him at present, an 18-year old half-orc girl named @[Deza](person:15748888-235d-4c37-9939-8255b0d0e4b1), and Peder, the 14-year old son of one of his old adventuring companions. The former has been a source of consternation among the elves of @[The Cauldron](settlement:983c8fa2-3df5-46b0-91fb-3dbe004450da) - despite her obviously talented mind she is less than welcome, even at the multi-racial University. There are even dark rumors (false) among the students that her position with Master Nimoyin has been obtained through intimate favors. 

 Though Nimoyin is neutral on the question of guild-noble dominance, he has a love of all knowledge, and will act to defend Diego di Mantua and his work if he can.

articles.title: Nimrodel
articles.content:
Has been building ships on the Dorian's banks for nearly 150 years, and his name has become a tradition among shipwrights. Nimrodel came from the Lake of Mists a very long time ago.

A tall Noldor elf, with dark hair slightly touched by frost, Nimrodel is one of the leading citizens of the city. He owns and operates four yards for the building and repairing of ships, and is a wealthy man, but because of his long interest and involvement in the political affairs of Haven, he is considered an outcast by the elvish community of @[Erinhir](settlement:96d2680b-e669-4c07-ba6b-f4727fb8d9d9), who disdain involvement in human affairs. 

He has become guildmaster for the @[Guild of the Ship](organization:a4013cdd-b725-4f7f-9844-9599dc2af814), one five "great guilds" that control much of what happens in Haven (see Government of Haven) but takes no side in the nobility/guild struggle; his only interest is in what is good for the city, and the growth of trade and commerce is certainly good for Haven.

Since the death of his beloved wife twenty years ago, he has become a melancholy and solitary man, leaving most of the running of his shipyards to his sons, and concentrating his energies on the politics of the city. Nimrodel blames the @[Thieves' Guild](organization:08dce3b2-80f7-468b-be7b-dd5fdbfac799) for his wife's death, and has been an active opponent of the Guild ever since, even going so far as to assist @[The Black Hand](organization:d1a96263-4191-482e-ace6-360d25106f60) on rare occasions. 

Nimrodel is also aware of the true identity of @[Silverthorne](person:6314ff3e-fadd-42ba-aa6c-bf26fc2767bc) and has offered his home as a place of safety for Silverthonre and his friends (see the scenario @[The Renegade Prince](plot:5339dc97-4ba1-4c12-92f6-d028f8b05005) for more information).

articles.title: Ninar Goldrush
articles.content: A formet wildcat prospector, Ninar is both incredibly gullible and incredibly lucky, the kind of fellow who spends his life savings on an abandoned, worthless mine, and then falls through a hole in its shaft and discovers an untapped mother lode beneath. He runs @[The Grubstake](landmark:b19a1629-5e9b-493d-a0a2-ac29d1f3e434) with his partner @[Forti](person:147481f4-3578-45ab-b2a9-6c5279b4ca46).

articles.title: Nithri Griffinrider
articles.content:
An extraordinary enigma, Nithri was orphaned as a youth when his parents were ambushed and murdered by brigands as Nithri crawled unnoticed from their burning wagon. He grew up on his own in the mountain wilderness, living simply and learning the ways of the beasts. In later years he became restless, as the dwarven yearning for gold grew within him, and ventured back into the cities of man. Now, he makes a living as a solitary soldier of fortune, coming to Haven from time to time to glean information about new opportunities for lucrative adventures that he can pursue. 

 He remains suspicious of his fellow man, and keeps his own counsel. He will not voluntarily put himself in a position where he is responsible to, or for others (hence his unwillingness to touch the Broken Blade). He also remains a master of wilderness lore, an expert tracker, trapper and mountaineer. He has wrestled a grizzly barehanded and been victorious, and flown on the back of a legendary griffin - yet one will learn of these feats only from others, for Nithri has no love of fame, or desire to impress anyone with his skills. 

 He dislikes royalty, and people of pretension, and has never shown the slightest interest in women of any race - if there is any way to stir his heart, no one living in Haven knows of it.

articles.content: Owner of No-Yen Drachmah, Goldsmiths

articles.title: Nosi Neb
articles.content: Nosi is an optician extradordinaire but tends to use archaic methods of eye adjustment (it is rumored that she once electrocuted a blind man to restore his sight). Nosi works with her husband Nima who is also an optician.

articles.title: Novig
articles.content: Assistant trainer under @[Eldri](person:b8240f19-94be-44ec-9e68-d2bf0235f2bb).

articles.title: Numirolakos
articles.content: Legend has it that a centaur trained horse will only throw a cruel master and Numirolako is one of the best

articles.title: Odino
articles.content:
A small, dark, wiry fellow, full of nervous energy. He teaches tumbling to students with at least an average DEX for 5gp a week for daily 2 hour sessions. Odino is a good teacher, and if a student does well after 3 months, can improve coordination and reflexes. 

 Odino is into a "health food" diet of brown rice and raw vegetables, which he eagerly espouses to his students, along with meditation sessions and a regular exercise ritual.

articles.title: Oin
articles.content:
An irascible old dwarf with wispy grey eyebrows and beard, and stormy dark eyes.  His fingers are gnarled with age, but his hands retain much of their metalworking skill. 

Oin conducts business dealings solely in the dwarven tongue (a fact hinted at by the dwarven store name), and non-dwarves must get along as best they can. His tone is fearsomely stern, and may give the impression that he is greatly insulted when a customer attempts to bargain; in fact, he loves to haggle, and a buyer will get a much better price if he perseveres.

articles.title: Old Lea
articles.content:
A fat, dark haired woman with a wide grin on her round cheeks and a loud, penetrating laugh. Old Lea sells sweetmeats and hot pastries from her stall, baked fresh "on the premises" in a stone oven. She has a loud, brassy voice to hawk her wares, and is a jovial person, easily moved to laughter, which causes her considerable bulk to shake. She will say many things in order to get a customer within selling distance, including both flattery and insults. Lea loves to banter, 

 Price Range: Fair 
Quality: very good

articles.title: Oriol
articles.content: An avanthar who works primarily with soft leather, feathers, beads, and other natural materials to create beautiful Festival masks. Married to @[Ibis](person:31453b97-8029-4488-8028-d988668bbd4a).

articles.title: Oskro
articles.content: Oskro the innkeeper is a grouchy old fellow who suffers from rheumatism, gout, indigestion, and bad teeth, and is seldom seen to smile. He spends much of his time bedridden, leaving operation of the inn to his wife and daughter, who wait on him hand and foot.

articles.title: Osondrea
articles.content: A high level elven enchantress who specializes in the enchantment of wood and fire. Her residence is in a tree in the Riversedge area of @[The North Corridor](settlement:4554e4a9-db69-47da-9921-6c5850001ce8)

articles.title: Othmar
articles.content: Othmar is about 50 years old, with a gray, wispy beard and mustache, and a raspy voice; a virtual recluse, little has been done in the matter of his personal hygiene for a long period - his body and the disheveled blue robe he constantly wears appear to have never been washed in the last ten years, and he constantly scratches himself. Othmar tells a good story when he gives a reading, and he always puts his predictions in the most optimistic context; as a result, he has developed a faithful clientele, despite his personal habits.

articles.title: Otto Chubb
articles.content: Offers meat on the hoof in more ways than one these days. While roly-poly Otto and his equally rotund wife Ingrid dispense cuts of meat, and trade tales and gossip with their customers, his daughter Bundy lounges around the front of the shop, hungrily eying the male customers that pass through

articles.title: Otto Heath
articles.content: Random entertainer to be user as necessary

articles.title: Paladin Brandybuck
articles.content:
Paladin is a very proud young halfling fighter with political aspirations, who has recently been appointed a Leftenant in the @[Haven City Guard](organization:d24af512-917c-4a1b-98d0-0b9d9934be00) company at Tower Stations despite his rather pedestrian record in that unit (rumor has it that Paladin's brother Rigaletto "coincidentally" made a large contribution to the company's upkeep a few weeks before this commission was awarded). 

He will almost always be wearing a spotlessly polished dress uniform when encountered, and will frequently (60%) be in the company of non-halflings (i.e., elves, dwarves, or humans). Considers matters in @[The Dell](settlement:e8aa9d8f-68be-4d89-9e11-6ba288e71515) to be unworthy of his attention, particularly the current problem posed by the gang of young human toughs (see Dell, Scenarios). 

Paladin shares a spacious smial with Rigaletto; their home is the frequent site of parties with guest lists including many influential Haveners from @[The South Corridor](settlement:d684e9e8-9b69-45fc-8352-3de0e6e7f870), and which are widely renowned as the dullest social events occurring in or around @[The Dell](settlement:e8aa9d8f-68be-4d89-9e11-6ba288e71515). 

Anyone wishing to make Paladin livid with rage need only persist in calling him "Lad", a derogatory nickname given to him by some of the more waggish members of the Guard.

articles.title: Pallinar
articles.content: The former owner of @[The Stone Hammer](landmark:bc6496c4-1ba0-4a37-9992-4e15a3f097a8), Pallinar was forced to sell in order to raise money for the treatment of his invalid daughter Arabel. He still works at the inn several nights a week and lives a few buildings away. He is a grim, joyless man, whose liveliness was snuffed out on the fateful day his daughter suffered her crippling accident in a fall.  He blames her injury on his own inattentiveness, and no one (not even Tolbin, who has tried repeatedly) can comfort him. Since the accident, he cannot abide to see others engaged in frivolous horseplay, and will unleash a violent outburst at anyone involved in such actions.

articles.title: Paraggio Lucca
articles.content: Paraggio, the master of one of @[The Black Hand](organization:d1a96263-4191-482e-ace6-360d25106f60)’s two traditional thieving guilds is a slender, boyish man with dark hair and an angular face. His guild consists of some three cells of highly competent thieves who operate mostly in @[The Commons](settlement:8ff1c19a-c29d-4050-9c7c-7200f23453be) and North Corridor.

articles.title: Paul de la Riis
articles.content:
A firebrand leader of the @[Young Stallions](organization:7340b23d-2c0c-45fd-8222-13b00aa2760c), Paul has a haughty bearing that exudes self-confidence. He is of medium height and clean shaven, with dark, elaborately pomaded hair, and lively dark eyes. 

In public, he wears the common symbols of the @[Young Stallions](organization:7340b23d-2c0c-45fd-8222-13b00aa2760c) - a dark green velvet swordsman’s cloak with the emblem of a rearing white horse on its back, a white ivory brooch shaped like a horse's head,  a walnut walking stick, and a broad-brimmed velvet hat with a feathered plume. Paul always carries a well-balanced, +2 longsword in a jet-black leather scabbard edged with gold leaf; he is an expert swordsman, and an excellent horseman. 

He is extremely disrespectful to all guildsmen, and particularly despises the Varrasch brothers. He and the other Stallions are frequently seen all over the city and in the surrounding region, listening to the grievances of merchants and commoners, and fomenting discontent with the current regime. One of his be friends in the Stallions is @[Antonio Berensten](person:ec8f50d3-84f6-48a6-95d0-d7d6b5b65cb8). [br][br] [familytree:61db5c85-e436-459e-926e-17ad7e116b03] [br]

articles.title: Pauli Bracegirdle
articles.content:
Pauli and his four deputies are charged with keeping the civil peace within @[The Dell](settlement:e8aa9d8f-68be-4d89-9e11-6ba288e71515), and handle those disturbances that are too petty to warrant the Tower Guard's involvement. He is normally a pleasant, easygoing man, conscientious while on duty and not averse to a bit of drink and womanizing (he is a bachelor and considered quite a catch by the young halfling woman) when off the job. 

 The current situation has made him much more edgy and irritable than usual, and greatly increased the watchfulness of himself and his men - Pauli and/or his deputies are likely (80%) to approach any human traveling in @[The Dell](settlement:e8aa9d8f-68be-4d89-9e11-6ba288e71515) who is not either well-dressed, or accompanied by a halfling, with their weapons drawn, and harshly question him about his business in the area.

articles.title: Peering Tiefling
articles.content: Random person frequently seen peering into the shop, squinting as if he has trouble seeing.

articles.title: Pegleg Peter
articles.content: A stout, good-natured fellow with a thick reddish beard and earrings in both ears, who gets around reasonably well on a sturdy crutch and a peg leg.

articles.title: Pelleas Pennywhistle
articles.content:
Pelleas is a modest man without pretensions of greatness, who has a penchant for finding common sense solutions to the problems that face his small community. He firmly believes that the citizens of @[The Dell](settlement:e8aa9d8f-68be-4d89-9e11-6ba288e71515) must keep their own house in order, and will discourage non-halflings from getting involved in the current struggle the community faces in trying to keep out the young toughs from @[The Commons](settlement:8ff1c19a-c29d-4050-9c7c-7200f23453be). 

 Though Pennywhistle is by no means an able fighter, he has recently begun the practice of walking around @[The Green](landmark:58c2143a-18ef-4281-89c4-96547a184d4a) nightly, to reassure his neighbors that everything is all right. Unbeknownst to the Mayor, Sherriff @[Pauli Bracegirdle](person:10f7097d-eb2f-47bb-b177-ccb245033073) follows Pelleas on these jaunts at a safe distance to protect the latter from harm.

articles.title: Penelope Sutherland
articles.content:
Lady Penelope Sutherland (but call her "Lady" and you might get punched) is the youngest daughter from a minor noble family, from a far-off land. After travelling for a year or so, she found herself in Haven, and after a few odd jobs joined the guard in order to pay rent.

Penelope is quick to laughter and quick to anger - loyal to her friends, but will hold a grudge forever.

articles.title: Petriko
articles.content:
A talented youth, Petriko and his partner @[Kivi](person:13263a5e-7fbd-44b8-9d51-72affe5373ad) spend their days teaching at a small dance and acrobatic school which they own, near @[The Commons](settlement:8ff1c19a-c29d-4050-9c7c-7200f23453be). Their incredible abilities have drawn many affluent clients to their small school. 

 At night, they perform at various points along @[The Street of Harps](settlement:6053011d-37a6-4d6b-8e0b-41925f3bbd77), the Plaza of Troubadours, as well as the Leiderstrasse. They have several times been employed to perform at houses in @[The Heights](settlement:1f0571c0-b8de-4b50-b010-5529cab6603b), and their popularity and fame is steadily increasing. 

 @[Kivi](person:13263a5e-7fbd-44b8-9d51-72affe5373ad) and Petriko are inseparable, yet they are not married, and do not seem to plan to do so. 

 Petriko is a stocky, but quick young man who, in his earlier fighting career, suffered a serious face wound which left him badly scarred. He decided to give up fighting and joined @[Kivi](person:13263a5e-7fbd-44b8-9d51-72affe5373ad) to become a truly amazing acrobatic team.

articles.title: Petrovka
articles.content: Young, only 17, relatively pretty, with long, thick brown hair and hazel eyes, and a trim figure, and sells flowers from a small cart. She can be found almost anywhere in the Guilders' Park area, or wandering in the Maze. She has a crush on @[Huiel Farris](person:f876117f-9fb2-447d-b4b6-1a9d8a939b68), and will usually show up at his office door each evening at the time he normally leaves and wait for him; Huiel does not know the depth of her feelings, but buys a small bouquet from her each night (he almost always gives it to old Mallana, the cook at @[The Lying Lawyer](landmark:0f5a29ce-4b27-422f-a557-e53239d964d0) - Mallana thinks he's a sweet boy). Petrovka will seldom miss a trial in which Huiel figures. Her prices are reasonable for her flowers, and they are always fresh in the morning.

articles.title: Phineous Tarkin
articles.content:
A middle aged man, with weary lines about his eyes and mouth, whose hair is thinning, particularly in the last three months since he's taken over the management of the Muses' Theater. The job has aged him, and it's obviously been some time since he had a good night's sleep. It's also been a while since he was sober. 

 Phineous invested a good deal of gold (his own, and his patron's) into refurbishing and renovating the Muses' Theater, and in producing this expensive premiere production. Now he sees all his dreams fading fast, in light of the present situation, and he has been indulging heavily in alcohol. 

 Phineous is desperate for a solution to his problem, and will eagerly accept help, promising great rewards. He will pay handsomely (1000gp) to the players should they succeed; although once he's sobered up, he may regret it.

articles.content:
Round as a dumpling, with rosy cheeks and bright eyes, and perpetually wearing a floured apron. Pippin sells hot pies and pastries from his pushcart on @[Trade Island](settlement:eec2fc60-5565-40fa-9047-69924589c400) (where the prices are higher) baked fresh every night in @[The Dell](settlement:e8aa9d8f-68be-4d89-9e11-6ba288e71515). The cart has an enchanted @[Brick](person:d9388a1c-1b0e-471b-89a1-50f0b805b6c3) in it to keep the goodies just-out-of-the-oven hot, 

 Price Range: High

articles.title: Pocheffski
articles.content: Pocheffski, a sallow-faced, squint-eyed man in his late fifties whose reflexes are still cat-quick despite the toll of advancing years on his vision is the Thieves Guild's Weapons Master.

articles.title: Poin Sestar
articles.content: A wiry student of the @[College of Physical Naturalism](landmark:c437c8f9-8314-4d26-aeb2-aa298bf4be19) and tends bar at @[The Bent Page](landmark:d5976734-958f-46d4-be01-ee5915b28d02) at night.

articles.title: Porginald
articles.content: Married to @[Bessie](person:3300ae5b-d242-47af-a2f7-a279bdb4440a), Porgy (as friends call him) helps out in the bakery. Together they have numerous children, all on the pudgy side.

articles.title: Portia Maggia
articles.content:
A small, delicately boned woman with intense dark eyes, short curly hair and finely chiseled facial features. She was a scholar of philosophy in her youth, and is now quite a successful independent spice finder. She dresses in a distinctly male fashion when travelling on business, wears two daggers on her person and knows how to use them very well. 

She also regularly wears two items of jewelry that are worthy of note: [ul][li]a mithril bracelet with a seashell pattern that identifies the wearer as an elf-friend, and[/li] [li]a belt buckle of lapis lazuli, formed in the shape of a P; when the center is touched, a defensive spell is activated so that anyone grasping her will receive a shock equal to a 1d6 temporary CON loss per melee round (CON = 0 means unconsciousness rather than death).[/li] [/ul] 

Portia wishes to be treated as an intellectual equal, and is strongly offended by men who make forceful sexual advances. If treated with respect, she is very outgoing and friendly, and has a great store of useful knowledge about events occurring inside and outside the city. 

There is only a 25% chance that Portia will be in Haven at any time; if in town, there is a reasonable chance that she is preparing for a new journey and may invite people she meets to accompany her on that trip, if they have made a good impression on her. articles.title: Prospero Maggia
articles.content:
Gilberto's younger brother Prospero, lives in @[The Commons](settlement:8ff1c19a-c29d-4050-9c7c-7200f23453be) section of Haven, and makes his money through heavier industrial enterprises like grain milling. Prospero loudly defames his siblings for abandoning their simple origins, and claims that they have become as pretentious as the nobles they supposedly supplanted as the city's administrators.  Gilberto and Prospero have not spoken to each other for many years and communicate with each other solely by innuendo.

Prospero has been frequently linked by rumor to the activities of the underworld organization known as @[The Black Hand](organization:d1a96263-4191-482e-ace6-360d25106f60), though no criminal charge has ever been levied against him. Prospero is in fact connected to, but not formally a member of, @[Cariadoc's Guild](organization:d7a77502-083f-49bb-b9b7-430867e5ea00) in @[The Black Hand](organization:d1a96263-4191-482e-ace6-360d25106f60) and owns the mill they use as headquarters. articles.title: Qaften
articles.content: An apprentice leatherworker of great skill but is a horrible salesman. He is easily bullied by customers and often forgets the prices of the goods.

articles.title: Querrel Seadreamer
articles.content: A Sindar elf who runs @[The Mallorn](landmark:11a61b6d-c93a-47c0-b483-46c0dcf8996d) with the help of his sisters @[Ygraillia](person:98478629-5626-4e1b-8e46-0bda89b317e3) and @[Melaina](person:3b5cada6-ba93-459b-a849-dfcc613d8a62).

articles.title: Rabon
articles.content: Running a low class bordello, Rabon is a lecherous, sour faced man who cares little for his "girls", save for their bodies and the money they bring in.

articles.title: Rael Gavotte
articles.content:
A handsome man of middle years, with dark hair and a well-kept goatee, and is always impeccably dressed. Rael is clever as a fox, devious as a dragon, and just as charming. 

 What Rael lacked in musical talent he made up for with ambition, and he now holds the post of Guild Magistrate, which gives him control over all petty disputes within the Entertainer's Guild. His dislike of the circus folk has much to do with the present unrest, and it is rumored that Rael's hand is always open when an important dispute must be judged. 

 Rael's parties at his luxurious home are legendary he is a lover of good food and wines, and his parties frequently are regular bacchanals, with ladies from @[The Street of Silk Veils](settlement:587a7a3a-ba45-4bfd-94bc-fe6e17ae023c) as hostesses. 

 Rael is admired by some, liked by few, watched warily by many, distrusted by most. And there are some, like @[Helvia Larksong](person:3b7960d3-c329-465f-b630-d0de2591906e), or @[Largo Profundo](person:650522c3-ae93-4b5e-b2bb-43bd5ef14271), who actually hate the man.

articles.title: Raf Poul
articles.content: Raf Poul, an associate of @[Nimrodel](person:c23b1ec6-6ac7-4c88-bff2-ef81a0a78957) the shipwright, is in union with @[Sindra](person:9abadd16-8953-4112-b062-6922cdda7760), the leatherworker

articles.title: Raku the Potter
articles.content:
Tall and skinny, with long auburn hair tied back in a ponytail, and a shaggy handlebar moustache; he is usually dressed in a mud-splattered tunic, with the sleeves rolled up, muddy breeches and bare feet. He smokes a pipe constantly, and is very easy-going, taking nothing in life seriously; very laid-back and mellow, 

 Raku makes various sizes of vases, pots, etc. on a treadle-powered wheel. He experiments with glazes, however, and the colors don't always come out the way he wants, so about 20% of his merchandise is half-price, due to mottled or otherwise odd colors, 

 Price Range: Fair
Quality: Generaly Good, aside from the above

articles.title: Ralki
articles.content: Ralki is a very diminutive, elderly dwarf with horn-rimmed spectacles, and a military posture. He does only custom tailoring and has an uncannily precise sense of fit. He serves all races with equal skill.

articles.title: Rampallio Aguirre
articles.content: Squire to @[Bruning de la Riis](person:743beb40-df18-47f5-8bdf-144dcc690b88) for the last twelve years, Rampallio is a short, wiry man with a thick black beard and a swarthy complexion. Through not an exceptional fighter by any means, Rampallio understands his employer's personal needs, and has often helped Bruning cover up for his various amorous affairs. The squire lives very frugally; he is rumored to have accumulated a substantial bankroll over the years, but its location is unknown. He will almost certainly (90%) accompany Bruning on any new expedition he undertakes, receiving one-third of any salary or shares of treasure paid to the knight. [br][br] [familytree:90000012-09bf-451b-af4f-a7fd455199d2] [br]

articles.title: Randy Shuttlecock
articles.content: Owner, @[The Fox and Goose](landmark:03624e67-ff96-4846-9f22-c639d0155534). He is middle-aged and quite handsome; Keeping fit is his second favourite hobby, after sampling the wares at the houses on Silk Veils.

articles.title: Rankim Lowlea
articles.content: See Street Encounter: Dueling Daggers

articles.title: Ranna Campanella
articles.content:
A fat, jolly blond-haired woman of middle age, with a cheerful grin, usually wearing colorful bell-shaped skirts and carrying a wooden spoon. 

 Knows and greets about everyone by name, and is quick to ask a newcomer about themselves. She never forgets a face or name, and is friendly and talkative. 

 She has no head for figures, however, and can be muddled with counting out a guests change, and can easily under, or overcharge him. Nor does she remember easily what items on her menu cost, and usually will ask someone else - even another "regular" customer. 

 But her memory is flawless when it comes to news and people, and she is an excellent source of information. 

 Her older son Gavin is keeper at the @[Carillon Tower](landmark:0723cf41-4ef8-46d2-baaf-7101f4146e4a).

articles.title: Raphael Swiftrider
articles.content:
A small wiry man, whose hair is thinning, his eyes are creased but still bright, and he smells of horses, leather, and tobacco. 

 Rafael is the horse trainer for the troupe. He has been around horses all his life, and knows each one of the heavy horses that pull double duty drawing wagons, as well as performing, and his own grey mare, Princess. Princess is well trained, for fighting as well as trick riding, and will obey only Rafael. If one of the horses is injured, he will nurse it as if it were his own child. Rafael does not sleep in a caravan, but beds down near where the horses are tethered. 

 An old campaigner, he has traveled with Simba and Fenris before. Distrusts Simba's griffin, for obvious reasons; will not tolerate mistreatment of horses. 

 Rafael has no minuses to fighting from horseback; he uses a lance with skill.

articles.title: Rasputin
articles.content: This burly half-orc runs a lucrative smuggling and protection business out of his house in @[The Labyrinth](settlement:e05f9a94-a44d-4991-b419-28cae89db0ee). While not a member of the Thives Guild is has the attention of @[The Black Hand](organization:d1a96263-4191-482e-ace6-360d25106f60), his sworn enemy, that aims to take him down.

articles.title: Ratchet
articles.content:
This seemingly ageless man has long golden hair, with deep blue eyes and fine, delicate, youthful features (even though it is known he is over 50 years of age). His father was an elven warrior who left on an expedition when Ratchet was two, and never returned. 

 Ratchet describes himself as the "eternal middle man." He owns a small shop off Holly, where he runs a buy-and-sell operation. He specializes in buying newly arrived merchandise (particularly musical instruments) and then reselling them as soon as possible. 

 If questioned concerning Dragonsbane (see Adventures, Street of Harps), he will remember it as an archaic piece of junk with numerous broken strings. He was happy to be rid of it, but he does not remember to whom it was sold.

articles.title: Raven
articles.content:
General alley basher/legbreakers/other muscle.

 Streetwise and a savvy brawler, Raven knows every dirty fighting trick in the book, and a few that have never been published. His agility and speed more than compensate for his lack of size, and he is never without a hidden weapon.

articles.title: Recci
articles.content:
A tall, loosely made man who appears unfinished. The nickname has been given him by the guards and prisoners at @[The Grey Halls](landmark:29cb4deb-4fef-475f-8c31-0d8e6f188cda), and he does deserve it; a low intelligence and a tendency to overt sadism would usually get one fired, but Recci's luck has functioned beautifully. Recci attained the position of watch chief through attrition rather than merit.

 He has never been caught out of line, nor has any fault or misstep been traced to him - @[Turin Khaey](person:8c4f7bc1-4696-4be1-b3f4-3e24f0c68fa8) suspects, but as yet has not sufficient evidence to do anything. 

 Recci hangs out at @[The Knighte Oute](landmark:9c8b1af3-8ee0-4161-a334-ceabc6b04d34) when off duty, and would likely (85%) succumb to a bribe if one were offered to him to free a prisoner. 

 He's not smart enough to double-cross anybody, and there is reasonable chance for a successful rescue, with his cooperation.

articles.title: Red Nick
articles.content: Spends most of his time sitting around the bar, drinking from his private stock. He leaves the serving of the regular ale and a peppery stew to the cook, @[Maggie](person:9dc5c5ee-90f7-4e4a-bcb3-d882685c5130).  He is a careful man, and will only deal with people he knows, or those who have some sort of good references. He often sells his merchandise to Alphonso Caradello, a member of the smuggling arm of @[The Black Hand](organization:d1a96263-4191-482e-ace6-360d25106f60), although Nick himself is not a member of the Hand.

articles.title: Redonso
articles.content: Runs a water driven mill as his public job but is also a torturer in the employ of @[The Black Hand](organization:d1a96263-4191-482e-ace6-360d25106f60). The mill itself is actually owned by @[Prospero Maggia](person:eb5339e3-7f79-4754-9d9c-85ed69a2c39b).

articles.title: Regin A'Queen
articles.content: A half-elf with an eye for trinkets. He is new in Haven and, as a result, habitually gets lost in the labyrinthine side streets every weekend. (His greatest dream is to accumulate enough money to visit his homeland some thousand miles north of Haven).

articles.title: Reliddack Wulviss
articles.content:
A guest at the @[Rose Garden Inn](landmark:d657f21f-881e-4050-bf0b-e5bc103ac61a), Reliddack is a jovial, older gnome with an engaging personality and sharp wit. His congenial nature and small stature make him well-liked, especially amongst children. 

Reliddack is known for growing thriving medicinal herbs, such as can cure even diseases heretofore believed incurable. Additionally, he has found cures for other, more aesthetic, afflictions, such as the appearance of old age. His access to such properties has gained him significant ground in the highest of social circles.

articles.title: Renna Buckwalter
articles.content: Renna is a very sweet-hearted older woman prone to bouts of forgetfulness; she hears a great deal of gossip but will hopelessly confuse the information in the retelling. She has little real business sense, and a shopper can often find incredible bargains at her store if they have the patience.

articles.title: Resoom
articles.content:
The Guild's Librarian is a tall but plain fellow with a permanently disheveled look; the books, maps and records he maintains are in a similar state of constant disarray. Resoom greatly raised his esteem among the Guild's leadership by risking life and limb to salvage many of the organization's important documents. As a result of his efforts (and those of other thieves following his directions), only about 20% of the Guild's most vital information was lost in the fire. Resoom's new domain is spread among several underground chambers, some of which are trapped to prevent unauthorized access or can be sealed off from neighboring areas. 

 Freed from the careful filing systems of his predecessors in this job, the librarian has rendered himself truly indispensable - because only he can be assured of finding anything among the haphazard piles and over-stacked, cluttered shelves that prevail. Anyone seeking a document without Resoom's help has only a 20% chance of finding it in its assigned place, with a +5% chance for each half-hour of searching performed. 

 Although he is less sarcastic than he used to be about the need for tight security around HQ, Resoom still prefers to leave those worries to others, and spends most of his evenings carousing in the neighborhood's sleazy pleasure palaces. 

 He lives in one of the houses above the new Guild complex.

articles.title: Ricoh
articles.content: A rather large "associate" of @[Barbara Weyr](person:30e906f3-52e8-4f20-b08e-2ce574d89664) who help her with rugs/carpets and the more shady side of her business

articles.title: Rigaletto Brandybuck
articles.content:
A vigorous entrepreneur, always looking for a new angle to increase his already substantial fortune. He dislikes competition, and will use threats or underhanded tactics to maintain his monopoly on sales of many prestigious products (see Dell, Scenarios). 

 Rigaletto Brandybuck, is one of the very few inhabitants of @[The Dell](settlement:e8aa9d8f-68be-4d89-9e11-6ba288e71515) seeking to gain influence in overall city affairs, and he owns a shop in both the North and @[The South Corridor](settlement:d684e9e8-9b69-45fc-8352-3de0e6e7f870) in addition to his shop and warehouse in @[The Dell](settlement:e8aa9d8f-68be-4d89-9e11-6ba288e71515). Rigaletto is not well liked in @[The Dell](settlement:e8aa9d8f-68be-4d89-9e11-6ba288e71515) because of his social airs, but this bothers him little, for he is much too busy cultivating his friendships with the major merchants of the Corridor.
articles.residence: Residence of Rigaletto and Paladin Brandybuck

locations.title: Residence of Rigaletto and Paladin Brandybuck

articles.title: Riklas Longstrider
articles.content: More of an investigative specialist than a trial lawyer; he is generally employed by the other lawyers of @[Barristers' Maze](settlement:ce6589a2-427d-4318-9641-17d8ea7b2641) to check out information and witnesses for their various cases. Few judges wish to allow him in their @[Courts](landmark:5fe07c2b-bce5-4c96-880d-d72a70bb1352), but if he does have a trial before them, they bear him no malice. He is of normal centaur build, with reddish hair and blue eyes. He lives outside the city walls from the Horse Gate, and, like @[Meron Glyptes](person:f4db812e-df9d-4430-93b9-91126c8d4cf2), is not allowed in either the Hanged Wan or @[The Lying Lawyer](landmark:0f5a29ce-4b27-422f-a557-e53239d964d0).

articles.title: Rimer
articles.content: Works for @[Lazar Symbocca](person:2c51d376-29e2-4868-ac54-050e58f8c59c) at @[Sym's Storage Company](landmark:950bc2b9-c121-4be6-a597-f3373ed455b0). He is a Black Hand member but doesn't know the full extent of Lazar's business.

articles.title: Rioldi Thorn
articles.content:
General alley basher/legbreakers/other muscle.

 A serious alcoholic, he will almost certainly show up for the job "hollering drunk" if paid any portion up front (which he will try to insist on). Very competent when sober. Neither the Guild nor the Hand will use him now, having been too often burned in the past. If the players are Guild or Hand members, there is a 60% chance they will know his reputation.

articles.title: Robin O'Leary
articles.content:
Dashing, handsome young man with long curly dark hair, and gorgeously curled moustaches. A fine luteist and singer, has a very glib tongue around members of the fairer sex, and is a flashy dresser. A notorious name-dropper; will try to pass himself off as one of the "In Crowd". His tales of relationships with the nobility and Great Guilders, however, are more than a little exaggerated. 

 He wears a handsome rapier on his tooled leather belt, which he cannot use to save his life.

articles.title: Rocky
articles.content: Rocky a big, scarred, potato-faced ex-­fighter, runs his tavern and the arena, which features numerous two-bit boxers, gladiators, and cock- or dog­fights several nights a week.

articles.title: Roderick
articles.content:
Guard in @[The Grey Halls](landmark:29cb4deb-4fef-475f-8c31-0d8e6f188cda). See scenario @[The Rescue Attempt](plot:226319b0-e928-43f5-ab74-bb3e6df90e77) 

 A slender black haired man with a mangled left hand, can normally be found In the evenings at any of four taverns in the area of the @[Horse Market](settlement:3987cb08-4abd-4e55-a582-128df2ff71db)

articles.title: Rodney of Shaftesbury
articles.content:
A moderate build, silvering hair, and watery blue eyes; his face is clean shaven, and he has a long, very unflattering nose. 

Rodney's family has rapidly lost its wealth over the last ten years (primarily as a result of Rodney's own abysmal choice of investments), and have been forced to sell all of their property holdings. His four children are now scattered across the countryside, and none would take him into their home. 

Despite his best friend Sir @[Falstaff of Borrinstorr](person:25385ea6-3ae8-4aa4-ac69-8628f498adb0)'s kindness, Rodney has become sullen and uncommunicative. He mistrusts all young people, and will try to sabotage any relationship that might be developing between Falstaff and a potential "foster" son. 

Rodney is an avid gambler (at cards, dice, or billiards), and Falstaff is likely to propose a game to liven up a quiet evening at a dinner party or tavern.

articles.title: Rohan Flanderin
articles.content: Wealthy owner of a spidersilk empire. He both manufactures and sells.

articles.title: Romano Maggia
articles.content:
Gilberto Maggio's eighteen-year-old son, called "Mano" affectionately by his family (and derisively by the Young Stallions), is a tall, wiry young man with heavily pomaded black hair and a thin moustache. Mano is already well-advanced in his wine-making apprenticeship, and shows an uncommon intuitive skill for selecting the proper blend of grapes to make a superior product. Unfortunately, he is impatient and quick to anger, and jealously protective of his sister Marita's virtue. Because of his temper, Mano has always been a prime target of the @[Young Stallions](organization:7340b23d-2c0c-45fd-8222-13b00aa2760c)' taunts. 

 Mano believes (correctly) that the Stallion @[Antonio Berensten](person:ec8f50d3-84f6-48a6-95d0-d7d6b5b65cb8) is lusting after his sister, and has avowed to himself to keep them apart. It is not uncommon to see Mano trailing one or the other of the two "lovers" around @[The Heights](settlement:1f0571c0-b8de-4b50-b010-5529cab6603b) (35% chance that Antonio or Marita will notice the tail). articles.title: Rombo Alecastle
articles.content: A well-known, but reclusive figure in @[The Dell](settlement:e8aa9d8f-68be-4d89-9e11-6ba288e71515) because of his past exploits as a participant in a number of highly successful dungeon expeditions. Rombo is looking his only son and heir.  See also scenario @[The Missing Heir](plot:c56eb5b8-f17e-4d6c-aa63-ce813753745a).

articles.title: Romulo Velasquez
articles.content:
Of all the artists receiving @[Gilberto Maggia](person:f8abcaf4-8f94-42f6-84ea-94c3c8c1b1a4)'s support, Velasquez is the most favored; he has a small private studio on @[Studio Lane](landmark:a3a5c599-c67d-41a6-b3be-d94b4271a605), and receives a generous monthly stipend. 

 Velasquez is tall and dark, with craggy features that are striking though not handsome; he considers himself quite a Lothario, and has indeed had his way with a number of young, aristocratic maidens. He has attempted to ply his charms with @[Marita Maggia](person:7c9dab1a-8221-41ca-83f6-0d3b49331e37), in the hopes of securing a more permanent place in the Maggia household, but received nothing but cold shoulder (he remembers these encounters with more than a little bitterness, and would like to find a way to take some wind out of Marita's sails). 

 On two previous occasions, he has been approached by agents of @[Prospero Maggia](person:eb5339e3-7f79-4754-9d9c-85ed69a2c39b), and asked to garner information on a particular business transaction being contemplated by Gilberto. Romulo considers such efforts an easy way to increase his income, and has no moral qualms about spying on his benefactor. [br][br] [familytree:0abd1b09-4093-4a05-9563-7ff27309b96c] [br]

articles.title: Ron Heavymight
articles.content: He is Borough Commander of @[The Labyrinth](settlement:e05f9a94-a44d-4991-b419-28cae89db0ee) stationed at the @[Market Barracks](landmark:8b369554-047b-483f-8486-6460bd10c977) of the Haven City Watch

articles.title: Rosina Maloti
articles.content: Rosina is the best of several seamstresses in Haven who specialize in costumes for the stage. A matronly lady with spectacles, she is an expert in costuming history, and can tell a good deal about a person by the way they dress. Rosina has a 30% bonus to penetrating a disguise, and can create authentic garb for almost any period in time and place.

articles.title: Rovon Kolae-Gileana
articles.content: Rovon, who hasn't earned his nickname yet, assists his mother at her market stall. He is also very rambunctious for a 7 year old - a 6'4" 280lb. 7-year-old. His father is Benzantree, a mercenary leader.

articles.title: Rowen
articles.content: @[Silverthorne](person:6314ff3e-fadd-42ba-aa6c-bf26fc2767bc) has a small band of loyal followers, who have sworn to defend him and his interests, and to help him regain his throne. Rowen is skilled with the bow. All are staying at @[The Mallorn](landmark:11a61b6d-c93a-47c0-b483-46c0dcf8996d), and may be encountered at various places throughout the city.

articles.title: Rowena Geronde
articles.content:
A tall and stately woman in her mid-forties, with dark hair and grey eyes, the Baroness Windermere cuts a regal figure. She dresses with conservative class, wearing clothes and jewelry that are understated but elegant. She has remained aloof from the Nobility-Guild struggle, for she refuses to judge individuals on the basis of a convenient label. 

 Her strong-willed independence is grudgingly respected by most in the community, but Rowena has few real friends. She keeps her emotions very secret, and rarely raises her voice; however, on those rare moments when she becomes angry, it is very wise to stay out of her way. 

 She always wears a silver medallion set with a large blue sapphire; the jewel Detects and Discerns all active Magic within a radius of 100 feet. If the medallion is held by anyone other than her, it becomes unbearably hot after sixty seconds and must be dropped. When traveling in areas where she believes she may need physical protection, she wears a matching pair of leather wrist thongs that, when activated, simultaneously produce a combined-effect spell that generates a Missile Repulsor shield (deflects up to 8 pts of missile weapons per melee round, with spear=4, crossbow bolt=2, arrow or sling stone=l pt; and can deflect a total of 60 pts of missiles before it is nullified) which also carries a charge of psychic electricity such that a person trying to pass through the aura (to grab Rowena or hit her with a close-range weapon) will take 2d6 pts of system-shock damage to CON per melee round (If CON is reduced below 0, a character is dead). [br][br] [familytree:c44f3336-7f83-4e89-a5c8-78896cc3f650] [br]

articles.title: Rufus
articles.content:
The night watchman for @[Dockside Warehouse Services](landmark:f71be1c6-a6ec-4faf-9495-f07abcb49755), the storage company owned by Constantine Maylino. Both Maylino and Rufus are Black Hand operatives. 

 Rufus, when sober, is a brilliant swordsman - ten years ago, as a mercenary commander, Rufus once was acclaimed first sword of Belakor. Now, however, he is beginning to feel his age, and the fading of his strength and the greying of his temples have proceeded apace. Further, his heavy drinking, always a problem, has intensified in recent years, and the once proud swordsman is known about the docks as a drunkard and a lush.

articles.title: Russell Miller
articles.content: Head of a fairly wealthy family of coopers. The family owns three workshops, and large warehouse and employ over 50 halfling, nearly all with the surname Miller.

articles.title: Rutmilla Panfusille
articles.content: Rutmilla, @[Tybalt de la Riis](person:4c0f8c89-3d7b-46e9-8e62-4506ed433370)' daughter, is big-boned and very homely, with a broad flat nose and moles on her chin. articles.title: Ryan Campanella
articles.content:
Ranna's youngest son, a red-haired, freckle faced boy of 14 who has the head for numbers Ranna lacks. He manages the business end of the @[Mixolydian Mode](landmark:11295957-2b7d-4d5c-bb99-2a0a765035f6), occasionally chastising his mother for undercharging customers or spending too much. 

 Ryan is not a musician, but he aspires to be a wealthy agent – he has a natural sales ability, and a quick wit. He's not into sharing gossip, however, and will get suspicious if asked too many leading questions.

articles.title: Samoradat
articles.content:
Tall, and big-boned, with dark hair in many small braids; Samoradat speaks with the accent of the Namorin Empire. She is a former slave who escaped to Haven many years ago; she is kind hearted to all who are oppressed, 

 Samoradat keeps a huge cauldron of stew a-boiling all day, which she sells for 3cp a bowl on her high counter which surrounds 3 sides of her stall. She has a small canister of Namorin seasonings that can be sprinkled on the stew if the customer desires - use more than a pinch, and one must make a saving roll against CON or suffer the results, 

 Samoradat has a soft heart, and has been known to feed penniless tieflings. She is friendly with old @[Kazan the Mender](landmark:1119fcaa-fd35-4977-9b86-0a99c6a56918) (see below) and is well-liked by the other "regulars" of the Island.

articles.title: Sarasin Mour
articles.content:
Common thief. 

 An Easterner, dark of skin and hair, speaks with a soft lilting accent and dresses in loose trousers, shirts, and a turban. More of a con-man than a thief, he is clever, a glib talker, and thinks fast on his feet. His thieving skills are good, but he considers burglary to be too much like work, and so makes his living running various scams. Always on the move, with no fixed abode, he is extremely difficult to find once the scam is revealed.

articles.title: Sberri Rand
articles.content:
Hardly looks like he had the same parentage as Kruegger - he is quite tall, almost 6" over 6', and very slender, with blond hair and ice-blue eyes. He works primarily on land investments, and could be considered an expert on real estate valuation. His real expertise, however, is in the field of entomology - he collects butterflies, and has a collection with few peers in the known world (he is rumored to have paid 2,000gp for one little bug!). 

 Sberri is quiet and studious, and is seldom found outside the office or the estate, unless he is taking a lepidopteran sabbatical (an annual occurrence - he is gone for a month, chasing butterflies). [br][br] [familytree:2d08983e-2a01-46eb-b160-6e3d032c0a45] [br]

articles.title: Serindë
articles.content:
The goddess of Truth is the patron of the largest religion on Antheros. Her devotees believe that there are absolutes of the universe, and all concepts might be reduced to a single (albeit complex) expression of their accuracy, no matter how unpleasant. Anything that can’t be reduced this way means that the worshiper has not pondered the subject deeply enough to figure it out.

Her greatest gifts to the races of mankind are presumed to be mathematics and logic. In fact her devotees are often found amusing themselves and each other with mathematical and logical puzzles. 

Her holy symbol is a checkerboard pattern that spirals inward, giving the illusion of three dimensions.

articles.title: Sikki
articles.content: An assistant weapons trainer at @[Eldri](person:b8240f19-94be-44ec-9e68-d2bf0235f2bb)'s establishment, Sikki often has the chance to watch potential candidates in action before he approaches them. Since Sikki himself is of common parentage, he believes the soothsayer's ancient words that the chosen one will be a commoner, "pure of heart and willing to let the sword guide his hand". Given the opposition Coppin and many of the others show to this theory, however, Sikki can only rarely get the opportunity to put a commoner or inexperienced fighter to the test; once previously he was caught and sharply reprimanded by Coppin, and threatened with expulsion from the Brotherhood if he was caught a second time.

articles.title: Silva Baraggio
articles.content:
The best known caravan master in Haven, Silva is a husky and robust man of middle years with a booming voice and a gruff but usually pleasant demeanor. It is well known that Baraggio has an eye for the ladies and that he seldom travels alone, though he professes love only for one woman, a songstress from @[The Street of Harps](settlement:6053011d-37a6-4d6b-8e0b-41925f3bbd77), @[Lisa Duncan](person:48574d9f-2f0a-4c7b-ba18-8a1894967194), with whom he has carried on a very passionate affair for almost five years; when in Haven he stays at her home. 

Most of the caravans Baraggio organizes these days are small to medium and wagon drawn groups, running fairly short routes normally (2-3 months round trip, the better to tend his many business interests in Haven). 

If a young woman of 15+ APP applies as a passenger for a caravan trip, there is a 65% chance Baraggio will suggest a liaison with her if she is unaccompanied by a husband or lover. Naturally, passage on the caravan will not be charged if she accepts.

articles.title: Silverthorne
articles.content:
A Noldor elf with piercing grey eyes and very pale blond hair who describes himself as "a simple traveler" and appears to be a fighter of some kind. If in his company for very long, one gets the impression that there is a great deal more to this "simple traveler" than meets the eye. 

 If players let slip the fact that they are adventurers or fighters, Silverthorne will be interested in hearing of their exploits, particularly if there are elves or half-elves in the party. This may lead to the players' involvement in Silverthorne's efforts to regain his throne (see @[The Renegade Prince](plot:5339dc97-4ba1-4c12-92f6-d028f8b05005), @[Scenarios](article:088e33cf-5a28-4c3f-bbe5-a243e610d2ff), the Cauldron).

articles.title: Silvertongue
articles.content:
An older man with silver hair to match his tongue. He is a @[Storyteller](person:70d31849-625d-4637-abce-ad4929efc841), and can be found almost daily in the Market, beguiling crowds (including many children) with his tales of wondrous cities, faraway lands, and courageous adventurers seeking fabulous treasures. Unbeknownst to the other denizens of the square, most of the stories are true since he was an adventurer himself in his earlier days under the name Duriyan the Bard). He participated in many of the expeditions of which he speaks. 

 If a group listens to him for a decent period, they may pick up information on various possibilities for quests. If they speak to him directly (having figured out that he's not just an old bag of wind), there is a chance for specific information (GMs - this is how to get a party started on a new adventure scenario!). Have the highest CHA in the party make a saving roll - a simple success gets some information, greater success gets more. 

 If "2" total is rolled on the info check, Duriyan will decide that one last adventure will be good for his soul, and may accompany the group if invited. 

 He has some interesting equipment, including his lute, a magnificent sword and scabbard, a chain shirt of exquisitely fine links, and his own mount and camping gear. Most of his possessions are enchanted and embedded with various spells (GM's discretion, but most of It falls into the useful category rather than the super-powerful). He knows many magical songs, including SLUMBER, EMOTION CONTROL, and WALL OF FEAR, however, he will use these only in times of grave crisis.

articles.title: Simba the Strong
articles.content:
A powerfully built man, who wears tunics that show off his impressive physique. His skull is clean shaven, but he wears a full black beard and earrings of gold, and a bronze armlet with ornamental runes that never comes off. 

 Simba manages the two lions, the bear, and the griffin that comprise the Beast show. His armlet has a Control Beasts spell embedded in it. The two lions are overweight, lazy beasts, but not tame without the armlet; the bear will do anything for a snack, but is short-tempered if it feels the snack is being withheld, The griffin is only half grown, and is actually devoted to Simba, who has raised it from a hatchling. All beasts are securely caged when not performing. 

 Simba distrusts Toric, and privately threatened to tear him limb from limb if he proves untrustworthy. Simba keeps to himself mostly, but is loyal to Fenris, and the troupe. He will fight if the troupe is attacked, releasing the griffin, and is a deadly with a whip.

articles.title: Sirius the Scribe
articles.content:
An old man with thin white hair; his eyes and hand are no longer what they were, but still are serviceable. Sirius can not walk very well, due to acute stiffening of his leg joints, so he spends most of his time on a low cushion, under an awning in his usual spot. Sometimes he ventures out to enjoy the sunlight; always his parchment and scribing tools are with him. Sirius serves as a sort of medeival notary public, validating papers, reading and writing for the illiterate. He does very little business now, preferring to nap, and will be cranky if awakened. The Island people look out for him, and he is accompanied by a large dog called Orion, who protects him and keeps him company - the dog also is old, and spends much of its time napping near its master. 

 Sirius has lived on @[Trade Island](settlement:eec2fc60-5565-40fa-9047-69924589c400) for twenty years and is familiar with the legends of the South Keep, which he will recount if flattered slightly when asked questions.

articles.title: Skiff Borden
articles.content:
Built like the dockworker he once was, he now works for @[Neberhard Ohlfaardt](person:aa435b8d-e5f0-4e61-8d17-d6db601760b6), along with three others filling a job officially described as "personal assistant". It is however primarily aimed at keeping @[Sui Tuong Ding](person:908c4354-d81f-42f0-9be5-c227e30d2e2c) out of the clutches of other men. Skiff is the fairly literate and well-spoken, and generally acknowledged as the leader. 

 If some young gentleman is engaged in soulful conversation with Sui, Skiff will approach the suitor and suggest he might be happier elsewhere (like Tasmania). If the subtle approach fails, Skiff will point out his friends and repeat the suggestion. If the young man is still not sufficiently impressed (either because he is accompanied by friends of his own, or too stupid to recognize a beating when it's staring him in the face), Skiff will ask @[Brick](person:d9388a1c-1b0e-471b-89a1-50f0b805b6c3) to provide a small demonstration of his physical prowess. If this final warning does not do the job, Skiff and the others will attack the suitor, with orders to thrash (but not permanently injure, if possible) the latter. 

 Skiff likes the job because it’s fairly easy and lets him spend time in high-class places they would never see otherwise. [br][br] [familytree:3cade294-0a89-4913-884a-a82dc2ef320c] [br]

articles.content: Skorindir is getting elderly for an elf, being the only on in HAven with white hair. He is white-haired, an unusual sight in @[Erinhir](settlement:96d2680b-e669-4c07-ba6b-f4727fb8d9d9), but is straight as a sapling, and still strong. articles.title: Sombur
articles.content:
The youngest of the @[Brotherhood of the Broken Blade](organization:4a287a6e-7bd4-4721-9333-79ee98681350), Sombur is an assistant cabinet-maker with little battle experience. His two older brothers were lost on the last ill-fated expedition to Arkendelve, and he has sworn to avenge them, an oath the Brotherhood felt they had to honor. Sombur is anxious to attain that vengeance, and will react with rabid enthusiasm if a candidate should arouse any sort of reaction from the blade (including the brief and insignificant flicker described in @[The Broken Blade](plot:4db0d0e3-3179-4e90-855f-ad252b32b4c5) Adventure outline). 

Though cooler and wiser heads will prevail when the Brotherhood's next meeting is held (and it may be an emergency session, if the young dwarf has succeeded in arousing the community's fervor), the candidate may experience several days of hectic notoriety as a legacy of his meeting with Sombur.

articles.title: Songbird
articles.content: @[Silverthorne](person:6314ff3e-fadd-42ba-aa6c-bf26fc2767bc) has a small band of loyal followers, who have sworn to defend him and his interests, and to help him regain his throne.  Songbird has a sweet voice and trained falcon. All are staying at @[The Mallorn](landmark:11a61b6d-c93a-47c0-b483-46c0dcf8996d), and may be encountered at various places throughout the city.

articles.title: Stagtamer
articles.content: @[Silverthorne](person:6314ff3e-fadd-42ba-aa6c-bf26fc2767bc) has a small band of loyal followers, who have sworn to defend him and his interests, and to help him regain his throne.  Stagtamer is a swordsman. All are staying at @[The Mallorn](landmark:11a61b6d-c93a-47c0-b483-46c0dcf8996d), and may be encountered at various places throughout the city.

articles.title: Stammrig
articles.content: Makes work boots and war boots of fine leather, built to endure hardship and rough terrain. Stammrig and his wife have sired three children, all of them amazingly daughters, and now of marriageable age that he hope to marry off via @[Meydal](person:c736e469-6750-4396-864e-3cc214f2aad7).

articles.title: Stella Tainley
articles.content: Stella, a tall, rather rounded blonde who wears her hair in braids adorned by thongs of rich cowhide, is an outdoorswoman who shares her husband's (Tenley Tainley) interest. She herself is quite a competent swordswoman, and during the feasting which follows the hunt, she may impulsively challenge a male newcomer to their circle to a mock combat (a battle not to the death, using weapons that have been blunted or padded to reduce their damage potential). Such events are often accompanied by wagering among the crowd, and the results (when Stella is victorious) are usually known all over @[The Heights](settlement:1f0571c0-b8de-4b50-b010-5529cab6603b) within hours (woe to the chauvinist loser with a thin skin). Stella wears no jewelry except a gold chain that matches the one worn by Tenley. [br][br] [familytree:18e57ef5-b368-4bea-8392-5dd001a5df14] [br]

articles.title: Stinky
articles.content:
A short, skinny (and grimy) person (race unknown) who seems to be interested in accumulating all the offerings dropped by the horses in the Market. As a manure collector, Stinky is without peer, and he and the usually bulging sack which trails along the ground behind him are studiously avoided by anyone with a sense of smell; no one knows why he collects, or what is done with his findings (and few wish to find out). 

 Stinky has infested the Market for many years, and is a fount of information about people, etc. in and about the area (assuming one can abide the redolence that clings to him). Unfortunately, the rebuffs he has suffered on approaching people have made him shy and reluctant to take the first step in communication, although he is quite voluble (in the Common tongue) if last bid. Each time a bid is asked questions. There is a 35% chance he has noticed the odd blue eyed palomino in the public pen rented by @[Liriki d'Alensis](person:288f5fff-813e-4adf-b1b0-b33ca41f7986), the gypsy trader (see The Young Stallion - Who Was under @[Scenarios](article:088e33cf-5a28-4c3f-bbe5-a243e610d2ff), the Horse Market).

articles.title: Strathos
articles.content:
Strathos is a warrior's god, and is extremely popular with most of those who follow the ways of battle.  Follower ascribe to a code for the warrior, with the promise of an eternal life in a Valhalla-like setting for those who follow the code to the best of their ability.

There is no acknowledged high priest/priestess for Strathos. In fact, all clergy of Strathos are old soldiers, former fighters whose wounds have retired them from the battlefield. Since great cunning (tactical ability and strategic genius) in one's leaders is much respected among fighting troops, most of the clergy are referred to as Uncle/Aunt Fox. Those of great physical prowess are called Uncle/Aunt Bear. 

The professed clergy of Strathos wear normal clothing with an over-tunic of white with a large red bullseye (a series of 4 concentric circles) on both chest and back. The colors are designed to stand out in the hurly-burly of a melee on the battlefield.

The clergy run a hostel for wounded and recuperating (and just plain down-on-their-luck) soldiers and fighters, where free food and lodging are available. They would welcome members of the Lydian Sisterhood if one would ever cross their doorstep. Recipients of this largesse are expected to contribute to the temple when life starts treating them a little better, so that the service may be continued. Hostels of this type are found in every sizable town and city. 

The proper form for acknowledgment is taught by older fighters to their younger comrades, as they are deemed worthy of the knowledge - there is a 25% chance that any blooded (having combat experience) 1st level fighter will have been taught, 65% for a 2nd level, and 99% for third level and above.
[p]
articles.honorific: God of War, Strength, and Courage; Patron of Warriors
articles.codes:
[h3]The Warrior's Code[/h3]
[ul]
[li]Always respect your superiors.
[li]Never desert a wounded comrade.
[li]Be noble in battle. Do not slaughter needlessly. Grant quarter to those who ask it.
[li]Surrender is not dishonorable. It is dishonorable to continue fighting when all hope of winning is lost, and fighting on can only cost lives that need not have been lost.
[li]When hired, earn your pay. Serve to the utmost of your ability.
[li]Keep your weapons and armor clean, fit, and ready.
[li]Never desert an employer until the agreed term of original service has expired.
[/ul]

articles.title: Sui Tuong Ding
articles.content:
This young maiden is truly a breathtaking beauty, with chestnut brown hair flowing 'round her slender, sinuous frame, full pouting lips and seductive almond eyes that few can resist. She is not bright by intellectual standards, but is very aware of her beauty and is wily about using it to get what she wants. Of course, as might be expected of a girl of 18, what she wants changes from day to day for she becomes bored with a particular pastime or fashion style very quickly. 

Sui was brought to Haven three years ago by her now husband @[Neberhard Ohlfaardt](person:aa435b8d-e5f0-4e61-8d17-d6db601760b6) who met her on one of his jouneys, in this case to Herudana.

She has not yet tried to cuckold old Neberhard, a fact which has greatly surprised several of Haven's young dandies.  This seems due more to her awareness of the four bully boys (@[Skiff Borden](person:3cade294-0a89-4913-884a-a82dc2ef320c), @[Wilverado](person:75bdd2f3-51b7-4071-8d64-174d67830f68), @[Cambol Tartyn](person:6b418e97-dc1a-46f6-bf33-6c2458b1feae), @["Brick"](person:d9388a1c-1b0e-471b-89a1-50f0b805b6c3)) that Neberhard has hired to protect her than to any great affection for her spouse. 

It is likely that a man of discretion and taste would probably find Sui too shallow to satisfy him in the long run (but, oh, lord, what a surface she has to explore until then!). [br][br] [familytree:908c4354-d81f-42f0-9be5-c227e30d2e2c] [br]

articles.title: Sulemon Duur
articles.content:
The recently appointed Grand Master of Haven's Thieves Guild, Duur is a short portly man with a receding line of flaming red hair. He has a taste for fine clothes, and a fastidious nature surprising in a man who has spent the last twenty years living amidst the debris of @[The Labyrinth](settlement:e05f9a94-a44d-4991-b419-28cae89db0ee). 

 Duur previously served as Master of @[The Labyrinth](settlement:e05f9a94-a44d-4991-b419-28cae89db0ee) Guild chapter, where he became known to many as the man charged with assigning "tunnel duty" to the Guild's more errant members. Duur has a solid head for organization, planning and business, and can clearly handle the administrative aspects of his duties as Grand Master as well or better than anyone. It is not as clear, however, whether his personal temperament can stand up to the great stresses of the job. 

 Sulemon is subject to rapid and extreme swings of mood, and often childishly acts on the basis of a momentary pique - almost everyone who has worked closely with him has learned to step carefully when the Master is on a rampage. Nonetheless, it is apparent from Sulemon's actions since assuming the office that he plans on remaining Grand Master for a good long time. Duur has reassigned or demoted a number of @[Azimuth](person:38b3505c-7430-4028-8042-c9ce2756fab1)'s former inner circle suspected of having "too much ambition", and replaced them with more loyal supporters. He can be very clever politically when the occasion demands it, and devious and cold- hearted as a wight. 

 A last curious aspect of Duur's character also bears noting. Grand Master Sulemon Duur is extremely superstitious, and spends an inordinate amount of time and money consulting astrologers, fortune tellers, and other practitioners of the occult "arts". He will often act on the predictions provided by these dubious authorities as if they were fact, resulting in some strange schemes indeed

articles.title: Surfey Yerdien
articles.content: Surfey, or "spearchucker" is a real bow-lover, makes some of the best and largest bows around, with a high moisture tolerance and long life. She got her nickname Spearchucker because she one accepted a bet that she couldn't make a bow capable of firing short spears. The resulting "giant longbow" was only useful in the hands of a giant (or really tall/strong goliath) and required a 22 STR just to achieve a short range shot.
